# CHAPTER 2 | RECITAL OF THE HYMN TO THE GODDESS. 37

> By the realization of even a single syllable <term>Akshara; literally "imperishable," referring here to the letters of the sacred alphabet as divine energies</term> of Her being, a person rivals 
> the Sun, the Celestial Bird <note>Tarkshya or Garuda</note>, the Moon, the God of Love <note>Kandarpa or Kama</note>, Shiva <note>Shankara</note>, Fire <note>Anala</note>, and Vishnu. (60)
> 
> The three worlds are adorned by the moonbeams of whose syllables;
> I bow to the Great Mother of Accomplishment <term>Siddhamatrika; the personified power of the alphabet that grants success</term>, the Sovereign of all. (61)
> 
> This triple world is strung upon the great thread of whose syllables, 
> from the Cosmic Egg <term>Brahmanda</term> to the outer shell <note>the "cauldron" or boundary of the universe</note>; I bow to that Mother of Accomplishment. (62)
> 
> That eleventh support, the Seed born from the triple triangle <note>Konatraya; often referring to the Yoni or the triangle representing the Goddess</note>,
> from which the world—from the Cosmic Egg to the outer shell—is still seen today. (63)

---

*Surge* (Kallolla)—means speed or force. *The agitation of the surge* (Ullola-kallana)—refers to the connection between what precedes and what follows. This is what is meant: by the previously mentioned contemplation <note>bhavana</note>, when the mantra is fully accomplished, one is no longer subject to the distress of being bound by Time. Regarding the verse *By whose syllable*: the meaning of "even a single measure" should be understood from the mouth of the worshipful Guru <note>original: "aradhyapada-mukhad"</note>. *When accomplished*—means in the manner described by the venerable teachers. 

One rivals the **Sun**—through radiance and light. One rivals the **Celestial Bird** <note>Garuda</note>—through the power to remove poison and the ability to cross over obstacles. One rivals the **Moon**—by being composed of nectar <note>amritamayattva</note>. One rivals the **God of Love**—through beauty and grace. One rivals **Shiva**—by being composed of supreme bliss. One rivals **Fire**—through brilliance and power. One rivals **Vishnu**—by becoming the soul of the universe. This is what is meant: even by the perfection of a single syllable belonging to the Mother <note>the alphabet</note>, such status is achieved. (88, 89, 90)

Regarding the verse *By whose syllable*: The **Moon** is mentioned because it is composed of nectar. **Moonbeams** refer to the nature of light and the expression of illumination. **Adorned** means connected to that. The **three worlds** consist of the triad of the Knower, the act of Knowing, and the Object known. She is the **Mother of Accomplishment** because she is the source of the perception of all objects, such as sound. This is what is meant: because word and object are inseparable, the soul's own perfection is established as being like fire <note>inseparable from heat/light</note>. 

Regarding the verse *By whose syllable*: **Strung upon the great thread**—it is "Great" because it is beginningless. It is a "thread" <note>sutra</note> because it sews together or indicates specific meanings. **Strung** refers to a fixed, inherent connection. **This** refers to the world's perceptibility. **From the Cosmic Egg to the outer shell**—"Cosmic Egg" represents the greatest limit or "vastness," while "outer shell" represents the most refined or subtle boundary. This is what is meant: since there is a complete pervasiveness of word and object as stated before, the text teaches their specific internal relationship, and thus the identity of the soul with that is established. (91, 92)

Regarding the verse *That eleventh*: **Support** means the substratum or location. **Seed** means the cause. That which is **born from the triple triangle** refers to the nature of the eleventh syllable <note>the letter 'E' in certain Tantric scripts is written as a triangle</note> which takes the form of a triple triangle; its emergence as the world is seen as a fact of direct perception. This shows that the expansion of the universe mentioned earlier is evident to the senses. This is what is meant: by teaching that even a single syllable of the Mother is the cause of the universe, the perfection of one's own identity with that is the intended conclusion. (93)

It emphasizes that mastering even one syllable allows a practitioner to rival the powers of the major deities and understand the universe as a manifestation of the Goddess.</summary>

# THE TANTRARAJA WITH THE MANORAMA COMMENTARY 38

She who is bound by the groups of letters beginning with *A, Ka, Ca* <note>original: "akacadi"; refers to the eight groups of the Sanskrit alphabet: vowels, gutturals, palatals, etc.</note>, whose body is the very syllables of the alphabet;
She who resides in the head, the arms, the heart, the back, the waist, and the feet. (64)

Through the gateway of the letter *I* <note>ī-kāra</note>, the essence of all essences, the highest of the high;
I bow to the Great Goddess, whose very nature is supreme bliss. (65)

Whose nature—be it with form or without form—even the gods do not know in the least even now:
"Who is She? From where? Where is She? And by what means?" (66)

I bow to Her, who is the form of the imperishable Mother-Syllables <term>Matrika; the sacred alphabet viewed as the source of all creation</term>,
The Supreme Auspicious One <note>Parā Śivā</note>, shining through the surging waves of the Kula lineage <note>Kula-kala; the family of spiritual tradition or the manifestation of divine power</note>. (67)

---

**Regarding the verse "She who is bound" (64):** This refers to the Goddess in Her complete form, consisting of the eight groups of powers <note>shaktis</note> associated with the alphabet which will be described later. 

**Regarding "In the head..." (64):** Through the individual letters of the alphabet <term>Matrikakshara</term>, She shines forth everywhere as the possessor of a body. The point is this: by teaching that the alphabet exists in the form of the body of all embodied beings, the identity <term>tanmayata</term> of one’s own self with Her is established. 

**"The derivation" <gloss>uddhara</gloss>:** refers to the written form of the script. 

**"The essence of essences" (65):** refers to Her own self. The text shows the meaning of the two "essence" words by the phrase "the highest of the high." 

**"Whose nature is supreme bliss" (65):** This refers to the letter *I*, which consists of the Point <term>Bindu; representing Shiva or pure consciousness</term> and the Emission <term>Visarga; representing Shakti or creative energy</term>. This is because it takes the form of the harmonious union <term>samarasya</term> of Shiva and Shakti. The point is: the letter *I* is the unified form of the Point and Emission, which are the causes of the alphabet. When one contemplates this—which will be described later as the "volition of the Point"—as one's own self, there is the experience of supreme bliss. (64-65)

**Regarding "Even now" (66):** This praises the previously mentioned mystery. 

**"The gods" <gloss>devata</gloss>:** refers to the senses <term>indriyas</term>. 

**"Who is She?"**—regarding Her essential nature. 
**"From what cause?"** 
**"Where?"**—meaning in what place. 
**"By what means?"** 
This refers to both the contemplation with form <note>sarupa-bhavana</note> and without form <note>arupa-bhavana</note>. The point is this: those whose six senses are not "pierced" by the side-glance of a Guru <note>adeshika-kataksha; the transformative grace of a teacher</note> do not know even slightly, at any time, what Her form is, for what reason, in what place, or by what means. Here, these four questions should be understood directly from the lips of the worshipful Teacher. Because this is an extreme mystery, it is not fully revealed here. (66)

**Regarding "I bow" (67):** "I"—meaning the Self in the form of the alphabet <term>Matrika</term>, which is condensed by the method of "pratyahara" <note>a grammatical/mystical technique of grouping the first and last letters to represent the whole</note> from the first letter to the last. 

**"Imperishable" <gloss>akshayya</gloss>:** refers to that which is born between the first letter *A* and the last letter *Ksha*. 

**"The form of the Mother-Syllables":** Shining through the path revealed in the seventh sutra...

### CHAPTER 2 | CONCLUSION OF THE FRUIT OF THE HYMN

(1) I bow to Her, the Mistress of the eight groups of Great Perfections <term>Siddhis; supernatural powers like becoming small or light</term>, in whom the eightfold form of the Mothers <term>Matrika; the personified powers of the Sanskrit alphabet</term> is established according to the sequence of the letter-groups <note>original: "vargānukrama-yogena"; refers to the categorization of the Sanskrit alphabet into eight groups: vowels, gutturals, palatals, etc.</note>. **(98)**

I bow to the holy Tripura, who is the treasury of the four sacred commands <note>original: "caturājñā-kośa-bhūtām"; refers to the four geographical/spiritual directions of the tantric tradition</note>, who resides in the city of fulfilled desires <note>Kamapurna</note>, in the sacred seat beginning with the letter 'Ja' <note>Jalandhara-pitha</note>, and within the final Holy Seat <note>Oddiyana-pitha</note>. **(99)**

Thus, this hymn of twelve verses grants all accomplishments. O Goddess, since your nature is the unbroken whole <note>akhanda-rupa</note>, this hymn is truly your own manifest form. **(100)**

---

**Regarding the phrase "Surging through the lineage"** <note>original: "kulollola-prollasanti"</note>: *Kula* (lineage/family) refers here to the "body," because it eventually dissolves <note>liyamana</note> back into the earth <note>prthivyam</note>. *Kala* refers to a "portion" or "part." "Surging upwards" describes the manifest stage of speech <term>Vaikhari; the highest and most audible level of sound</term>, which possesses a glory of an unthinkable nature. For the one who meditates:

This is what is being said: Whether considering the unmanifest form or the manifest form of the Mother-Alphabet <note>Matrika</note>, the practitioner achieves a state of identity <note>tanmayata</note> with their own Self. **(97)**

**Regarding the verse "Groups..." (98):** "By the sequence of groups" refers to the method taught in the seventh thread <note>sutra</note> of this text. The eightfold Mothers are also spoken of as yours. "Mistress of the eight groups of Great Perfections" means she is the ruler of the eight supernatural powers—such as *Anima* <note>the power to become infinitely small</note>—that arise from each group of letters.

The point is this: There are eight groups of the Alphabet; their presiding deities are the Eight Mothers <note>Ashta-matrikas</note>. From each of these arise the eight powers like *Anima*, totaling sixty-four. The collective power <note>samasti-shakti</note> that is the cause of these individual powers <note>vyasti-shaktis</note> is realized as one's own Self. There is a deep secret here which should be understood directly from the mouth of one's venerable Guru. **(98)**

**Regarding the verse "Desire..." (99):** "Beginning with the letter Ja" refers to the Jalandhara Seat <note>Jalandhara-pitha</note>, as 'Ja' is its first letter. The "Holy Seat" <note>Shri-pitha</note> refers to the Oddiyana Seat, which is the preeminent residence of the Goddess. She resides everywhere in the form of Space <note>akasha</note>, manifesting as the four sacred seats representing Earth, Water, Fire, and Air. "The treasury of the four commands" refers to the Sacred Traditions <note>Amnayas</note> of the East, etc. She is the "treasury" because she is the cause of all things.

*Tripura* is the Mother-Alphabet <note>Matrika</note>. She is so named because she fills and overflows through the three states of the Knower, the Knowledge, and the Known, which are the very nature of the Self. This is what is being said: through the glory of the Mothers taught in the eleven preceding threads, the power that manifests as the entire universe—explained through specific places and specific principles <note>tattvas</note>—is realized as being identical with one's own Self. From here onwards is our own commentary. **(99)**

With the verse beginning "Thus," the author teaches the reward for reciting this hymn. Because of the identity with you, the Mother-Alphabet, who is the Unbroken Form <note>Akhanda-rupa</note> unconditioned by space or time, let there be auspiciousness <note>Shivam</note>. **(100)**

## The Commentary on the Third Chapter.

In the previous second chapter, after teaching the glory of the Nine Masters, the methods of their worship, and other related matters, the author now teaches the sixteen mantras of the sixteen Nityas and their ancillary mantras—totaling twenty-five mantras in all. This is accomplished in the third chapter, consisting of one hundred verses, beginning with the words "Now, the sixteen..." and ending with "the mantra of the offering."

Therein, by the two verses beginning with "Now, the sixteen..." and ending with "declared previously," the purpose and scope of the chapter are stated. In that context: **By codes** means by their conventional names <note>original: "sāmayikairnāmabhiḥ"</note>. **Mentioned previously** refers to those taught in the twenty-fifth chapter of the *Former Tantra* <note>original: "pūrvatantre"</note>. **(1–2)**

By the three verses starting with "By Heart..." and ending with "declared," the nature and variations of the primary Nitya, the Lalitā-Vidyā, are taught. In that code:
*   **Heart** (*Hṛt*) represents the letter *Sa*.
*   **Breath** (*Prāṇa*) represents the letter *Ka*.
*   **Earth** (*Ilā*) <gloss>The terrestrial element</gloss> represents the letter *La*.
*   **Self** (*Haṃsa*) represents the letter *Ha*.
*   **Burning** (*Dāha*) represents the letter *Ra*.
*   **Fire** (*Vahni*) represents the letter *Ī*.
*   **Void** (*Kha*) represents the *Bindu* <term>Bindu; the nasalized dot signifying the union of Shiva and Shakti</term>.

By the sequence from "Self" to "Void" [Ha-Ra-Ī-M], the *Hṛllekhā* <term>Hṛllekhā; the "Heart-streak" seed-syllable, 'Hrīṃ'</term> is expressed as **Hrīṃ**. **Lalitā** refers to her specific Vidyā. **By the variation of Haṃsa** refers to the different ways the letter *Ha* is placed within the mantra. **(3)** **Starting with Haṃsa** means beginning with the letter *Ha*. [The text continues regarding] Lalitā—

# The Tantrarāja with the Manorama Commentary

-> The first [Vidyā] starts with *Haṃsa* <note>The letters Ha and Sa</note> and lacks the middle; the second has *Haṃsa* in the beginning and the middle. <-
-> The third is the primary nature <term>Prakṛti; the original or standard form of the mantra</term>; the fourth is formed by those [syllables] with the final Māyā <note>The syllable 'Hrīṃ'</note>. **(4)** <-
-> Among these, the fourth leads to Liberation, while the other three lead to Prosperity. <-
-> Thus the Vidyā of Tripurasundarī <term>Tripurasundarī; "The Beauty of the Three Cities," the supreme goddess of the Śrī Vidyā tradition</term> is correctly declared. **(5)** <-
-> "Pure" joined with "Space" is the first. "Lalitā" is the second. <-
-> "Void" joined with "Fire," followed by "Speed" joined with the "Pervasive." **(6)** <-
-> "Breath" combined with "Juice" and "Fire"; a pair of "Voids" joined with the "Moving." <-
-> "Sky" and "Earth," and this again joined with "Burning." **(7)** <-
-> "Water" joined with the letter "Ra," and "Heart" joined with "Forest-Power." <-

---

The word "Vidyā" <gloss>mantra</gloss> is to be supplied as the subject. Regarding the phrase "with *Haṃsa* in the beginning and middle": "middle" refers to placing the letters above the letter "Ka." "The third is the primary nature"—this means the Lalitā-Vidyā itself. "The fourth"—the fourth variety. "By those [syllables] with the final Māyā"—referring to the letters contained in the three groups <term>Kūṭa; a "peak" or cluster of syllables in a mantra</term>. "Final Māyā" means the *Hṛllekhā* <note>The syllable 'Hrīṃ'</note> residing at the end. 

The meaning is as follows: The fourth Vidyā, called "The Universal," is composed of the letters of the three stated groups in their specified order, but without the *Hṛllekhā* syllables at the end of the first and second groups, while retaining the *Hṛllekhā* at the end of the third group. **(4)** "Among these"—among the four Vidyās. **(5)**

With the three verses beginning with "Pure," the author teaches the eleven-syllabled Vidyā of the second Nityā, Kāmeśvarī. 
In that sequence:
"Pure" <gloss>Śuci</gloss> is the letter *Ai*. 
"Joined with Space"—"Space" is the *Bindu* <note>The nasalization dot signifying the infinite</note>. Joined with that, it becomes *Aiṃ*. 
"The first"—the word "syllable" is understood. 
"Lalitā"—refers to the Vidyā previously described. 
"Void" <gloss>Śūnya</gloss> is the letter *Na*. 
"Joined with Fire"—"Fire" is the vowel *I*; joined with that, it is *Ni*. 
"Speed" <gloss>Raya</gloss> is the letter *Ta*. 
"Joined with the Pervasive"—"Pervasive" is the letter *Ya*; joined with that, it is *Tya*. **(6)** 
"Breath" <gloss>Prāṇa</gloss> is the letter *Ka*. 
"Combined with Juice and Fire"—"Juice" <gloss>Rasā</gloss> is the letter *La*, and "Fire" is the vowel *I*; combined with those, it is *Kli*. 
"A pair of Voids"—two *Na* letters. 
"Joined with the Moving"—"Moving" <gloss>Cara</gloss> is the vowel *E*; joined with that, it is *Nne*. 
"Sky" <gloss>Nabhas</gloss>—

# Chapter 3 ] The Exposition of the Mantra of the Nityā Bhagamālinī

-> This is the Nityā Kāmeśvarī, the sole bestower of desires, [whose mantra] consists of eleven letters. **(8)** <-

-> [The mantra of Bhagamālinī] begins with the "Initial of Kāmeśvarī," then "Juice," then "Steady," and "Juice." Then "Steady" joined with "Earth," followed by "Moving." Then "Steady," and then "Juice" is recorded. **(9)** <-

-> "Steady" and "Void" joined with "Fire"; then "Juice" follows. "Steady" joined with "Earth," then "Gotrā" with "Burning" and "Fire." Then "Juice" and "Steady." **(10)** <-

-> "Sky" joined with "Wind," and "Juice" combined with "Moving." <-

---

<note>The following section provides the step-by-step decoding of the cryptic verses above.</note>

"The letter *Ma*." <gloss>Sanskrit: makāraḥ</gloss>
"Gotrā" refers to the letter *Da*.
"And this again" refers to the letter *Da* once more.
"Joined with Burning"—"Burning" refers to the letter *Ra*. It is joined together with the previous letter <note>forming the syllable 'Dra'</note>. **(7)**
"Water" <gloss>Sanskrit: Ambu</gloss> refers to the letter *Va*.
"Joined with Moving"—"Moving" <gloss>Sanskrit: Cara</gloss> refers to the vowel *E*. When combined with the letter *Va*, it becomes *Ve*.
"Joined with Forest-Power"—"Forest" <gloss>Sanskrit: Vana</gloss> refers to the vowel *O*, and "Power" <gloss>Sanskrit: Śakti</gloss> refers to the *Visarga* <note>the 'ḥ' sound represented by two dots</note>.
"Heart" <gloss>Sanskrit: Hṛt</gloss> refers to the letter *Sa*.
When these are combined, it results in the syllable *Sauḥ*.
The meaning of the phrase is that the mantra consists of eleven syllables formed in this manner. **(8)**

Through the twenty-three verses beginning with "Kāmeśvarī" and ending with "Mohinī," the teacher instructs on the twenty-five-syllable <term>Vidyā; a female deity's mantra, often personified as knowledge itself</term> of the third Nityā, Bhagamālinī <term>Bhagamālinī; "She who wears a garland of prosperity/wombs," the third of the fifteen Nityā deities</term>.

In that context:
"Initial of Kāmeśvarī" <gloss>Sanskrit: kāmeśvaryādiḥ</gloss> is the vowel *Ai* joined with a nasal dot <note>the Bindu</note>, resulting in *Aiṃ*.
"Juice" <gloss>Sanskrit: Rasa</gloss> refers to the letter *Bha*.
"Steady" <gloss>Sanskrit: Sthirā</gloss> refers to the letter *Ga*.
"Juice" refers to the letter *Bha*.
"Joined with Earth"—"Earth" <gloss>Sanskrit: Dharā</gloss> refers to the vowel *U*. Joined with the letter *Bha*, it becomes *Bhu*.
"With Moving" <gloss>Sanskrit: Sa-carā</gloss> means joined with the vowel *E*.
"Steady" refers to the letter *Ga*. When joined with the vowel *E*, it becomes *Ge*.
"Juice" refers to the letter *Bha*. **(9)**

"Steady and Void"—these refer to the letters *Ga* and *Na*.
"Joined with Fire"—each is joined with the vowel *I* <note>represented by "Fire"</note>, resulting in the syllables *Gi* and *Ni*.
"Juice" refers to the letter *Bha*.
"Steady" refers to the letter *Ga*.
"Joined with Earth"—"Earth" <gloss>Sanskrit: Bhū</gloss> refers to the vowel *Ū*. It is joined with the letter *Ga*. The term "Joined with Earth" is used here as a technical name for the letter itself. This is how technical terms are handled throughout this entire section. Thus, it becomes *Gū*.
"Gotrā" refers to the letter *Da*.
"With Burning" refers to being joined with the letter *Ra*.
"Fire" refers to the vowel *I*. Together, these form the syllable *Dri*.
"Juice" refers to the letter *Bha*.
"Steady" refers to the letter *Ga*. **(10)**

"Sky" <gloss>Sanskrit: Nabhas</gloss> refers to the letter *Ma*.
"Joined with Wind"—"Wind" <gloss>Sanskrit: Marut</gloss> refers to the long vowel *Ā*. Joined with the letter *Ma*, it becomes *Mā*.
"Juice" refers to the letter *La* <note>Note: The commentary here assigns 'La' to 'Rasa', though 'Bha' was used previously; this reflects a specific technical shift in the cipher</note>.
"Combined with Moving"...

## In the 3rd Chapter: Disclosure of the Bhagamālinī Nityā Mantra

-> With Moving and Speedy, following the third of the four letters <-
-> From the previous knowledge in sequence; then Juice and Steady. **(25)** <-
-> Heart-Lotus joined with Earth, Burning, with Moving, and Speedy, then Heart. <-
-> Burning joined with Water and Wind; Sky with Fire, then Juice. **(26)** <-
-> Steady also joined with Wind, then Void, with Fire, and the Sky-Goer. <-
-> The Swan joined with Pervading and Wind, Void, Pervading, and then Water. **(27)** <-
-> Burning, Mountain joined with Moving, likewise Burning and the Chariot. <-
-> Heart joined with Earth; Burning and the Chariot, both joined with Moving. **(28)** <-
-> Juice, Steady; then Breath shall be accompanied by Juice and Fire. **(29)** <-

---

**Joined with Burning** — **Burning** <term>Dāha: a code for the letter 'Ra'</term> refers to the letter *Ra*; therefore "joined with Burning" means accompanied by the letter *R*, resulting in the syllable *Rū*. **With Moving** <term>Cara: a code for the vowel 'E'</term> — joined with the vowel *E*. **Speedy** <term>Javī: a code for the letter 'Pa'</term> — refers to the letter *Pa*, resulting in *Pe*. **Following the third of the four letters from the previous knowledge in sequence** — this refers to a group of four letters starting from the third. The meaning is as follows: take the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth letters from the mantra of the goddess Kāmeśvarī <note>The first of the fifteen Nityā goddesses</note>. These four letters are to be placed before the syllable *Pe*. These are known as the secrets of the goddess Nityaklinne. **(25)** 

**Juice** <term>Rasa: a code for the letter 'Bha'</term> — the letter *Bha*. **Steady** <term>Sthirā: a code for the letter 'Ga'</term> — the letter *Ga*. **Heart** <term>Hṛt: a code for the letter 'Sa'</term> — the letter *Sa*. **Water** <term>Ambu: a code for the letter 'Va'</term> — the letter *Va*. **With Earth** <term>Kṣmā: a code for the vowel 'U'</term> — joined with the vowel *U*. **Burning** — the letter *R*, resulting in *Rū*. **Speedy** — the letter *Pa*. **With Moving** — joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Pe*. **Heart** — the letter *Sa*. **(26)** 

**Burning joined with Water and Wind** — the letter *R* joined with the letter *Va* and the vowel *Ā* <note>original: "vākārābhyāṃ"</note>, forming the sound *Rvā* <note>as in the word 'sarva'</note>. **Sky** <term>Vyoma: a code for the letter 'Ha'</term> — the letter *Ha*. **With Fire** <term>Sāgni: a code for the vowel 'I'</term> — joined with the vowel *I*, resulting in *Hi*. **Juice** — the letter *Bha*. **Steady** — the letter *Ga*. In this context, all words are used in a collective sense. **Joined with Wind** — joined with the vowel *Ā*, resulting in *Gā*. **Void** <term>Śūnya: a code for the letter 'Na'</term> — the letter *Na*. **With Fire** — joined with the vowel *I*, resulting in *Ni*. **Sky-Goer** — **Sky** refers to the letter *Ma* and **Moving** refers to the vowel *E*; meaning the letter *M* joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Me*. **(27)** 

**Swan** <term>Haṃsa: a code for the letter 'Ha'</term> — the letter *Ha*. **Joined with Pervading and Wind** — **Pervading** <term>Vyāpta: a code for the letter 'Ya'</term> refers to the letter *Ya*, and **Wind** refers to the vowel *Ā*; joined with these, it becomes *Hyā*. **Void** — the letter *Na*. **Pervading** — the letter *Ya*. **From that** — meaning "after this." **Water** — the letter *Va*. **Burning** — the letter *Ra*. **Mountain** <term>Gotrā: a code for the letter 'Da'</term> — the letter *Da*. **Joined with Moving** — joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *De*. **Likewise Burning** — the letter *R* joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Re*. **Likewise Chariot** <term>Ratha: a code for the letter 'Ta'</term> — the letter *Ta* joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Te*. **(28)** 

**Heart** — the letter *Sa*. **Joined with Earth** — joined with the vowel *U*, resulting in *Su*. **Burning and Chariot** — the letters *R* and *T*. **Joined with Moving** — joined with the vowel *E*. This means the letters *R* and *T* are each joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Rete*. **Juice** — the letter *Bha*. **Steady** — the letter *Ga*.

## The Tantrarāja with the Commentary named Manoramā

-> A double-Void joined with Moving, then that which was before, then after; <-
-> A double-Void and Gotrā shall be there, with Burning, Water, and Moving. **(20)** <-
-> Breath with Juice and Moving; then Gotrā and Pervading follow; <-
-> Gotrā joined with Burning and Wind, then Water and Pervading shall be. **(21)** <-
-> Wind and Space joined with Earth; joined with Water and Moving; <-
-> Juice, Steady, Water joined with Fire; a double-Wind joined with Moving. **(22)** <-
-> Swallow joined with Earth; afterward, Juice joined with Power; <-
-> Swallow joined with Earth, O Goddess! Juice, Pervading, and then Heart. **(23)** <-
-> With Burning and Water, and then Heart; Speedy, Water, and Wind; <-
-> And the Void alone, O Auspicious One! Juice with Moving and Steady. **(24)** <-

---

**Breath** <term>Prāṇa: code for the letter 'Ka'</term> — the letter *Ka*. **Joined with Juice and Fire** — **Juice** <term>Rasā: code for the letter 'La'</term> refers to the letter *La*; **Fire** <term>Agni: code for the vowel 'I'</term> refers to the vowel *I*. Joined with those two, it becomes *Kli*. **(19)** <note>This continues from the count of the previous page.</note> **Double-Void** <term>Śūnya: code for the letter 'Na'</term> — two *Na* letters — **joined with Moving** <term>Cara: code for the vowel 'E'</term> — joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Nne*. **Then that which was before, then after** — this means the letter following this one is the same as the letter that preceded it. Thus, *Kli*. **Double-Void** — two *Na* letters, *Nn*. **Gotrā** <term>Gotrā: code for the letter 'Da'</term> — the letter *Da*. **Joined with Burning** — with the letter *Ra*, resulting in *Dra*. **With Water** — with the letter *Va*. **Moving** — the vowel *E*. **(20)** <note>The syllable formed is *Dreve*.</note>

**Breath** — the letter *Ka*. **Juice** — the letter *La*. **Moving** — the vowel *E*. Joined with those two, it becomes *Kle*. **Gotrā** — the letter *Da*. **Pervading** <term>Vyāpta: code for the letter 'Ya'</term> — the letter *Ya*. **Gotrā** — the letter *Da*. **Joined with Burning and Wind** — **Burning** is the letter *Ra*; **Wind** <term>Marut: code for the vowel 'Ā'</term> is the vowel *Ā*, resulting in *Drā*. **Water** — the letter *Va*. **Pervading** — the letter *Ya*. **(21)**

**Wind** <term>Vāta: code for the vowel 'A'</term> — the vowel *A*. **Space** <term>Nabhas: code for the letter 'Ma'</term> — the letter *Ma*. **Joined with Earth** <term>Bhū: code for the vowel 'Ū'</term> — joined with the vowel *Ū*, resulting in *Mū*. **Water** <term>Vāḥ: here representing the letter 'Gha'</term> — the letter *Gha*. **Joined with Moving** — joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Ghe*. **Juice** <term>Rasa: code for the letter 'Bha'</term> — the letter *Bha*. **Steady** <term>Sthirā: code for the letter 'Ga'</term> — the letter *Ga*. **Water** — the letter *Va*. **Joined with Fire** — joined with the vowel *I*, resulting in *Vi*. **Double-Wind** <term>Vāyu: code for the letter 'Ca'</term> — two *Ca* letters. **Joined with Moving** — joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Cve*. **(22)**

**Swallow** <term>Grāsa: code for the letter 'Ca'</term> — the letter *Ca*. **Joined with Earth** <term>Dharā: code for the vowel 'U'</term> — joined with the vowel *U*, resulting in *Cu*. **Juice** — the letter *Bha*. **Joined with Power** <term>Śakti: code for the Visarga or 'H' sound</term> — joined with the *Visarga*, resulting in *Bhaḥ*. **Swallow** — the letter *Ca*. **Joined with Earth** — joined with the vowel *O*. Even though "joined with Earth" was used before for 'U', here it refers to the name of the vowel *O* as defined in the technical system, resulting in *Co*. **O Devi** is an address to the Goddess. **Juice** — the letter *Bha*. **Pervading** — the letter *Ya*. **Heart** <term>Hṛt: code for the letter 'Sa'</term> — the letter *Sa*. **(23)**

**With Burning** — with the letter *Ra* (this must be added to the following). **Water** — the letter *Va*, resulting in *Rva*. **Heart** — the letter *Sa*. **Speedy** <term>Raya: code for the letter 'Ta'</term> — the letter *Ta*. **Joined with Water and Wind** — **Water** is the letter *Va*; **Wind** is the vowel *Ā*, resulting in *Tvā*. **Void** — the letter *Na*.

## Description of the Knowledge of Bhagamālinī Nityā
### [ From the 3rd Chapter ]

-> Space joined with Water; Burning joined with Fire; Pure joined with Self. <-
-> Earth, with Juice, Earth, and Void; five seeds placed with one intervening. **(25)** <-
-> The five seeds placed between them joined with themselves; <-
-> they are in order: Earth-born, with Moving, Juice, Earth, and Space. **(26)** <-
-> Swallow joined with Moving twice; then Breath joined with Juice and Fire; <-
-> A double-Void joined with Moving, Heart-Burning, Water-Wind-Wind. **(27)** <-
-> Space joined with Fire; then Juice and Wind, Steady; <-
-> Make the Void with Fire, and Space joined with Moving, O Dear One! **(28)** <-

---

And the solitary consonant without a vowel is 'N'. **O Auspicious One** <term>Bhadre</term> is the address to the Goddess, placed between the internal letters. **Juice** <term>Rasa</term> refers to the letter *Bha*. **With Moving** <term>Sa-carā</term> means it is joined with the vowel *E*. **Steady** <term>Sthirā</term> refers to the letter *Ga*, resulting in *Ge*. **(24)** <note>This refers to the conclusion of the previous verse's decoding.</note>

**Space** <term>Viyat</term> is the letter *Ma*. **Joined with Water** <term>Ambu-yutaṃ</term> means it is joined with the letter *Va*. **Self** <term>Sva</term> <note>original: "sva iti"</note> refers to the resulting syllable *Mva*. **Burning** <term>Dāha</term> is the letter *Ra*; **Joined with Fire** <term>Agni-yuktaṃ</term> means joined with the vowel *I*, resulting in *Ri*. **Self** <term>Sva</term> refers to the **Dot** <term>Bindu: the nasalization mark</term>; joined with that, it becomes *Riṃ*. **Pure** <term>Śuci</term> is the vowel *Ai* <gloss>Ai</gloss>. 

**Earth** <term>Bhūmi</term> is the letter *Ba*. **Joined with Juice, Earth, and Void** — **Juice** <term>Rasā</term> is the letter *La*; **Earth** <term>Kṣmā</term> is the vowel *Ū*; **Void** <term>Kha</term> is the **Dot** <term>Bindu</term>. Joined together, they form *Blūṃ* <gloss>Blūm</gloss>. **Five seeds placed with one intervening** means that this multi-layered syllable *Blūṃ* is the primary seed, and it should be used five times, with a single different letter placed between each repetition. 

**The five seeds placed between them joined with themselves** — I shall now describe those five seeds which are placed above/between the repetitions of the aforementioned *Blūṃ* seed, each joined with its own nasal dot. **Earth-born** <term>Jyā</term> is the letter *Ja*, forming *Jaṃ*. **With Moving** <term>Sa-carā</term> is the letter *Bha* joined with the vowel *E*, forming *Bhe* <gloss>Bhe</gloss>. **Earth** <term>Bhū</term> is the vowel *O*. **Joined with Space** <term>Namo-yutaṃ</term> — **Space** <term>Namo/Nabhas</term> is the letter *Ma*; joined with that, it becomes *Moṃ* <gloss>Mom</gloss>. **(26)**

**Swallow** <term>Haṃsa</term> is the letter *Ha*. **Joined with Moving** <term>Cara-yutaḥ</term> means joined with the vowel *E*, forming *He* <gloss>He</gloss>. After the fifth repetition of the *Blūṃ* seed, the seed *Heṃ* should occur twice. The sequence is as follows: *Blūṃ Jaṃ Blūṃ Bheṃ Blūṃ Moṃ Blūṃ Heṃ Blūṃ Heṃ*. 

**Breath** <term>Prāṇa</term> is the letter *Ka*. **Joined with Juice and Fire** — **Juice** <term>Rasā</term> is *La*; **Fire** <term>Agni</term> is the vowel *I*; joined with those, it becomes *Kli*. **Double-Void** <term>Śūnya-yugmaṃ</term> is two *Na* letters. **Joined with Moving** <term>Cara-yutaṃ</term> means joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Nne*. **Heart** <term>Hṛt</term> is the letter *Sa*. **Burning** <term>Dāha</term> is the letter *Ra*. **Water-Wind-Wind** <note>original: "ambu marud-vātaḥ"</note> — **Water** <term>Ambu</term> is the letter *Va*; **Wind** <term>Marut</term> is the vowel *Ā*; joined with those, it becomes *Vā*. **(27)**

**Space** <term>Vyoma</term> is the letter *Ga*. **Joined with Fire** <term>Agni-sahitaṃ</term> results in *Gi*. **Juice** <term>Rasa</term> is the letter *Bha*. **With Wind** <term>Marutā</term> means it is joined with the vowel *Ā*. **Steady** <term>Sthirā</term> is the letter *Ga*, resulting in *Gā*. **Void** <term>Śūnya</term> is the letter *Na*. **With Fire** <term>Sāgni</term> means joined with the vowel *I*, resulting in *Ni*. **Space** <term>Nabhas</term> is the letter *Ma*. **Joined with Moving** <term>Careṇa-sahitaṃ</term> means joined with the vowel *E*, resulting in *Me*. **(28)**

**O Dear One** <note>original: "Priye"</note> is the address to the Goddess. **(28)** **Water** <term>Ambu</term> is the letter *Va*. **Space** <term>Viyat</term> is the letter *Sa*. **Sky** <term>Nabhas</term> is the letter *Ma*. The word **"and"** <term>tu</term> is used for conjunction. **Combined with Wind** <term>Marud-anvitaṃ</term> means joined with the vowel *Ā*, resulting in *Mā*. **Void** <term>Śūnya</term> is the letter *Na*. **Pervasive** <term>Vyāpta</term> is the letter *Ya*. **Heart** <term>Hṛt</term> is the letter *Sa*. **Joined with Speed, Burning, Void, and Fire**: **Speed** <term>Raya</term> is the letter *Ta*; **Burning** <term>Dāha</term> is the letter *Ra*; **Void** <term>Kha</term> is the **Dot** <term>Bindu</term>; **Fire** <term>Vahni</term> is the vowel *I*. Joined together, they form the syllable *Strīm*. **(29)**

**The Swan** <term>Haṃsa</term> is the letter *Ha*. **With Burning** <term>Sa-dāha</term> means joined with the letter *Ra*. **Joined with Water, Juice, Moving, and Void**: **Water** <term>Ambu</term> is the letter *Va*; **Juice** <term>Rasā</term> is the letter *La*; **Moving** <term>Cara</term> is the vowel *E*; **Void** <term>Kha</term> is the **Dot** <term>Bindu</term>. These are all joined together. What is meant is this: the letters *Ha*, *Ra*, *Va*, *La*, *E*, and the *Dot* form a single composite syllable <term>Kūṭa</term>, which is *Hrlūm*. **The Swan** <term>Haṃsa</term> is the letter *Ha*. **Joined with Burning, Fire, and Self**: **Burning** <term>Dāha</term> is *Ra*; **Fire** <term>Vahni</term> is the vowel *I*; **Self** <term>Sva</term> <note>often used for "Kha" or Void in this context</note> is the **Dot** <term>Bindu</term>. These are joined together. **The final** <term>Antyaṃ</term>—it should be understood that "seed-syllable" <term>Bīja</term> is the word to be supplied. This means the syllable *Hrīm*. This is the knowledge <term>Vidyā</term> of Bhagamālinī Nityā. **O Supreme Goddess** <term>Parameśānī</term> is the address to the Goddess. **(30–31)**

With the three verses beginning with **The Swan** <term>Haṃsa</term> and ending with **Beautiful One** <term>Sundarī</term>, he teaches the eleven-syllable mantra of the fourth Nityā, Nityaklinnā, and the fruits of its recitation. In that context, **The Swan** <term>Haṃsa</term> is *Ha*. **Joined with Burning, Fire, and Self**: **Burning** <term>Dāha</term> is *Ra*; **Fire** <term>Vahni</term> is *I*; **Void/Self** <term>Kha/Sva</term> is the **Dot** <term>Bindu</term>. Joined together, it results in *Hrīm*. This is the first seed-syllable. **The eight letters starting from the third syllable of Kāmeśvarī**: in the mantra of the Nityā known as Kāmeśvarī, one begins from the third letter and continues to the tenth letter. Here, the eight letters starting from the second letter <note>The commentator is clarifying the count of syllables extracted from a previous mantra</note> are taken, resulting in nine syllables in total. **Heart** <term>Hṛt</term> is *Sa*. **Water joined with Wind**...

## [ Chapter 3 ] Description of the Mantra of Bheruṇḍā Nityā. 48

Through the power of recitation and other rites, the fire [of the mantra] melts women as if they were butter. 
The practitioner perpetually becomes even more beautiful than the **God of Love** <term>Kandarpa</term>. **(34)**

Earth joined with Self is the first; then Life-breath joined with Burning and that; 
Essence joined with Burning and that; then Life-breath joined with Burning, the Forest, and Self. **(35)**

"And" <note>original: "kaṃ ca"</note> joined with Burning and that; Radiance joined with Burning and that; 
The Earth-Bow joined with Burning and that; then the final two syllables of Nityaklinnā. **(36)**

This is the nine-syllable Nityā known as **Bheruṇḍā**, the giver of all perfections; 
By simply remembering her, the three-fold poison is destroyed in an instant. **(37)**

---

**Water** is the letter *Va*. **Wind** is the letter *Ā*. Joined with these is **"Svā"**. **The Swan** is the letter *Ha*. Joined with **Wind** (the letter *Ā*), it means **"Hrāṃ"**. **The fire that melts women like butter**: This means that by merely seeing one who has perfected this mantra, women—who are helpful through wealth and life-force—become subservient. **(32-34)**

<margin>(1) The commentary manuscript 'Ti' reads "helpers in terms of wealth and obeisance <term>praṇāma</term>."</margin>

With the three verses starting from **"Earth joined with Self"** and ending with **"in an instant,"** he teaches the nine-syllable mantra of the fifth Nityā, **Bheruṇḍā**. In this context: **Earth** is the vowel *O*. **Joined with Self** means combined with the **Dot** <term>Bindu</term>; thus, **"Oṃ"**. This is the **first** seed-syllable. **Life-breath** <term>Prāṇa</term> is the letter *Ka*. **Burning** <term>Dāha</term> is the letter *Ra*. **Joined with that** means combined with the vowel *O*; thus the syllable is **"Krauṃ"**. **Essence** <term>Rasa</term> is the letter *Bha*. **Burning** is the letter *Ra*. **Joined with that** means the letter *Bha* combined with the vowel *O*; thus the syllable is **"Bhrauṃ"**. **Life-breath** is the letter *Ka*. **Joined with Burning, the Forest, and Self**: **Burning** is *Ra*; **the Forest** <term>Vana</term> is the vowel *O*; **Self** is the **Dot** <term>Bindu</term>. Joined with these, it becomes **"Kroṃ"**. **(35)**

**"And"** <note>represented by "kaṃ"</note> is the letter *Jha*. **Burning** is the letter *Ra*. **Joined with that** means the letter *Jha* combined with the vowel *O*; thus the syllable is **"Jhrauṃ"**. **Radiance** <term>Prabhā</term> is the letter *Ka*. **Burning** is *Ra*. **Joined with that** means the letter *Ka* combined with the vowel *O*; thus the syllable is **"Krauṃ"**. **Earth-Bow** <term>Jyā</term> is the letter *Ja*. **Burning** is *Ra*. **Joined with that** means the letter *Ja* combined with the vowel *O*; thus the syllable is **"Jrauṃ"**. **From the end of Nityaklinnā, the two**: This means the final two syllables of the Nityaklinnā mantra, which are **"Svāhā"**. **(36)**

**Nityā Bheruṇḍā**: This refers to her specific mantra. **Poison** <term>Garalaṃ</term> is **three-fold**, categorized as stationary, mobile, and artificial. Among these, **stationary** <term>sthāvara</term> includes plants like the *Kāraskara* <note>Strychnine tree</note> and *Karavīra* <note>Oleander</note>. **Mobile** <term>jaṅgama</term> includes creatures like cobras and vipers. **Artificial** <term>kṛtrima</term> refers to prepared concoctions, such as the juice of the *Likuca* <note>Monkey fruit</note> mixed with camphor and other substances. **(37)**

## In the Tantrarāja, accompanied by the commentary named Manoramā

The first syllable of Bheruṇḍā comes first here, followed by the first of Nityaklinnā. 
Then Water, the Void joined with Swan-Fire, then Water arising from Wind. **(38)**
The Heart joined with Fire, the Void joined with the Pervasive and the Pure, 
and the Void joined with Space and Power—this nine-syllable mantra is proclaimed. **(39)**
She is the Nityā who grants all goals, **Vajravāsinī**, the **Universal Devourer** <note>original: "Viśvaghasmarā"</note>. 
By merely remembering her, the three worlds are brought under one's control. **(40)**
The second of Vajravāsinī is first; then the fourth of Nityaklinnā; 
the fifth is the first of Bhagamālā, followed by the second of Bheruṇḍā. **(41)**

---

With the three verses starting with **"The first syllable of Bheruṇḍā"** and ending with **"three"** <note>The commentator refers to the group of three verses ending at 40</note>, the author teaches the nine-syllable mantra <term>vidyā</term> of the sixth Nityā, **Vajravāsinī**. In that context: **"The first of Bheruṇḍā comes first here"** means the first letter of the Bheruṇḍā-Nityā mantra becomes the first letter of the Vajravāsinī-Nityā mantra. By this, the syllable **"Oṃ"** is established. **"Followed by the first of Nityaklinnā"** means the first letter of the Nityaklinnā-Nityā mantra, which is the syllable **"Hrīṃ"**, is the second letter here. **"Then"** means immediately following. **"Water"** is the letter *Va*. **"The Void"** is the letter *Na*. **"Joined with Swan-Fire"** means combined with the letters *Ha* and *I*, resulting in the form **"Hi"**. **"Water"** is the letter *Va*. **"Arising from Wind"** means joined with the vowel *Ā*. **(38)** 

**"Heart"** is the letter *Sa*. **"Joined with Fire"** means combined with the vowel *I*, resulting in **"Si"**. **"The Void"** is the letter *Na*. **"The Pervasive"** is the letter *Ya*. **"And the Pure"** means with the vowel *Ai*. **"Joined with"** means combined with these two; the meaning is **"Nyai"**. **"The Void"** is the letter *Na*. **"Space"** is the letter *Ma*. **"Joined with Power"** means including the **aspiration** <term>visarga</term>, resulting in **"Maḥ"**. **(39)** 

**"Universal Devourer"** <note>original: "Viśvaghasmarā"</note> means she who consumes the entire universe at the time of the Great Dissolution. **(40)**

With the three verses starting with **"The second"** and ending with **"Tarini,"** he teaches the twelve-syllable mantra of the seventh Nityā, **Mahāvajreśvarī**. In that context: **"The second of Vajravāsinī"** refers to the second letter of the Vajravāsinī-Nityā mantra, which is **"Hrīṃ"**; this is her first letter. **"The fourth and fifth of Nityaklinnā"** <insert>(1)</insert> refers to the syllables of Nityaklinnā. **"The first of Bhagamālā"** is the syllable **"Aiṃ"**. **"The second of Bheruṇḍā"** is the syllable **"Kroṃ"**. **(41)** 

**"The second and third of Nityaklinnā"** are the two letters **"Ni-tya"**. **"The sixth and seventh of that same goddess"** refers to the letters **"ma-da"**. **"Then the eighth and ninth"** of that same goddess would be the letters **"dra-ve"**. **"The beginning of this"** means the first syllable of this Mahāvajreśvarī is **"Hrīṃ"**. **"She who carries one across the mass of bad dreams"** means she who carries one across **lack of discernment** <term>aviveka</term>. **(43)**

# [ Page 51 ]
### Chapter 3 ] The Description of the Mantras of Dūtī, Tvaritā, and the Nityās.

The second syllable of Nityaklinnā, the third, the sixth, the seventh, 
the eighth, the ninth, and then her first syllable—this is proclaimed. **(42)**
The Nityā **Mahāvajreśvarī** is declared to have a twelve-syllable mantra; 
she is the savior from the wilderness, the ocean, and the assembly of cruel sorrows. **(43)**
The last syllable of Vajreśvarī comes first; then Ether joined with Fire. 
Then Water joined with Wind, then the Earth-Syllable <note>original: "go"</note> joined with Earth <note>original: "kṣmā"</note>. **(44)**
Then Velocity joined with the Pervasive and the Pure. 
Following that, the final syllable of Vahnivāsinī—thus is **Dūtī Nityā** proclaimed. **(45)**
This seven-syllable mantra is the remover of all distress and the delight of the universe. 
Composed of the syllable *Hrīṃ*, it causes one to attain the state of Shiva and grants all spiritual perfections. **(46)**
The first of Vahnivāsinī comes first, then the beginning of Dūtī. 
The "Swan" <note>the letter Ha</note> combined with Earth and the Self <note>the vowel 'u' and the nasal 'm'</note>, followed by Brilliance and Speed... **(47)**

---

With the three verses starting from **"Mahāvajreśvarī"** and ending with **"grants perfections,"** the author teaches the seven-syllable mantra <term>vidyā</term> of the eighth Nityā, **Dūtī Nityā**. 

In this context: **"The last syllable of Vajreśvarī comes first"**—the final letter of the Vajreśvarī-Nityā mantra becomes the first letter of this Dūtī-Nityā mantra, meaning the syllable **"Hrīṃ."** 

**"Ether joined with Fire"**—Ether <note>original: "viyat"</note> refers to the letter *Śa*. Joined with Fire <note>original: "agni"</note> means it is combined with the vowel *i*. Thus, the second syllable is **"Śi."** 

**"Water joined with Wind"**—Water <note>original: "ambu"</note> is the letter *Va*. Joined with Wind <note>original: "marut"</note> means combined with the long vowel *ā*. This forms the third syllable, **"Vā."** 

**"The Earth-Syllable joined with Earth"**—The Earth-Syllable <note>original: "go"</note> is the letter *Da*. Joined with Earth <note>original: "kṣmā"</note> means combined with the long vowel *ū*. This forms the fourth syllable, **"Dū."** **(44)** 

**"Velocity joined with the Pervasive and the Pure"**—Velocity <note>original: "raya"</note> is the letter *Ta*. The Pervasive <note>original: "vyāpta"</note> is the letter *Ya*. The Pure <note>original: "śuci"</note> is the vowel *Ai*. When joined, they form **"Tyai."** 

**"The final syllable of Vahnivāsinī"** means the word **"Namaḥ."** **(45)** 

**"Remover of all distress"** means she is the destroyer of the misery born from a lack of discernment. **(46)**

With the four verses starting from **"The first"** and ending with **"causes,"** the author teaches the twelve-syllable mantra <term>vidyā</term> of the ninth Nityā, **Tvaritā Nityā**. 

In that context: **"The first of Vahnivāsinī"** means the syllable **"Oṃ."** 

**"Then the beginning of Dūtī"**—the syllable **"Hrīṃ"** is the second seed-syllable <term>bījam</term>. 

**"The Swan combined with Earth and the Self"**—The Swan <note>original: "haṃsa"</note> is the letter *Ha*. Earth <note>original: "dharā"</note> is the vowel *u*. The Self <note>original: "svam"</note> is the dot <note>the bindu or 'm' sound</note>. Joined together, they form **"Hūṃ,"** the third seed-syllable. 

**"Brilliance and Speed..."**

-> **The Tantrarāja with the Manoramā Commentary** <-

Wind, Radiance joined with the Wanderer, the Devourer joined with Power, followed by the Heart, Speed, Burning, and Fire—this shall be the eighth syllable, O Beloved! **(48)**

The Swan joined with Earth and the Breath, the Devourer joined with the Wanderer is the tenth. The second [syllable] is the eleventh. Brilliance joined with Sound is the twelfth syllable of the Nityā Tvaritā. **(49)**

She grants the attainment of wealth, beauty, fame, knowledge, prosperity, health, and long life. She is the pacifier of the pain of poison and the fulfiller of all desires. **(50)**

The Pure one joined with Ether is the first. The Flavor-element joined with Fire and the Life-breath joined with Ether is the second. The last is the Forest, the Heart, and the Powers. **(51)**

Thus is proclaimed the three-syllable mantra <term>vidyā</term> of this Nityā, Kulāsundarī. By merely remembering her, omniscience <note>all-knowingness</note> is produced. **(52)**

---

**[Commentary]**
"Joined with"—Brilliance—the letter *ha*. "With the Wanderer"—the vowel *e*. "Joined with Ether"—this forms the syllable *khe*, which is the fourth. <note>This refers back to the end of verse 47 on the previous page</note>. **(47)**

"Wind"—the letter *ca*. <insert>(Manuscript note: "words")</insert> "Radiance"—the letter *cha*. "Joined with the Wanderer"—joined with the vowel *e*, forming *che*, which is the sixth. "The Devourer joined with Power"—the Devourer is the letter *ca*; joined with Power—the Visarga <note>the ":" aspiration mark</note>—forming *caḥ*, which is the seventh. "Heart, Speed, Burning, and Fire"—these represent the letters *sa*, *ta*, *ra*, and *ī*, forming the eighth seed-syllable <term>bīja</term>, which is *strī*. "O Beloved!" is an address to the Goddess. **(48)**

"The Swan joined with Earth and Breath"—forms the ninth syllable, *hrūṃ*. <margin>Note: Another manuscript reads this as *hrauṃ*.</margin> "The Devourer joined with the Wanderer"—forms *ce*, the tenth. "The second"—referring to the second syllable of this very mantra, which is *hrīṃ*, making the eleventh. "Brilliance joined with Sound"—Brilliance is the letter *pha*; Sound is the letter *ṭa*; joined together they form the twelfth seed-syllable, *phaṭ*. **(49)**

"The pacifier of the pain of poison"—Poison refers to that born of snakes and similar creatures; pain refers to that born of poverty and so on; she is the destroyer of both. **(50)**

With the two verses starting with "The Pure one" and ending with "is produced," the author teaches the three-syllable mantra <term>vidyā</term> of the tenth Nityā, Kulāsundarī. In this: "The Pure one joined with Ether"—the vowel *ai* joined with the nasal point <term>bindu</term> forms the first seed-syllable, *aiṃ*. "The Flavor-element joined with Fire"—Flavor-element is the letter *la*, Fire is the vowel *ī*; joined together with "the Life-breath"—the letter *ka*, and "joined with Ether"—the nasal point, it forms the second syllable, *klīṃ*. "The Forest, the Heart, and the Powers"—forms the third seed-syllable, *sauḥ*. **(51)**

"By merely remembering her"—this implies that even for those who are averse to or unable to perform ritual repetition <term>japa</term> and formal worship, the results still manifest. **(52)**

# Chapter 3 | Discourse on the Mantra-Knowledge of the Eleventh Nityā

> The Swan joined with the Heart, Life-breath, Flavor, Burning, and Earth, combined with the mantra-knowledge <term>vidyā</term> of Kulāsundarī according to tradition. **(53)**
> 
> This Nityā-Nityā mantra consists of three syllables joined with six cluster-letters. Through forms such as the reverse order, she is brought forth in seventy-two variations. **(54)**
> 
> By worshipping her, a man becomes a perfected being <term>siddha</term>, a sky-traveler, and happy. The power of restraint and grace <note>original: "nigraha-anugraha"; the ability to punish or bless</note> arises for him at will, constantly. **(55)**
> 
> The penultimate syllable of Tvaritā’s mantra becomes the first. Brilliance joined with Burning and the Wanderer. The Heart joined with Burning, Earth, and the self. Then Vajreśī is the fifth... **(56)**

---

**[Commentary]**
With the three verses beginning with "The Swan" and ending with "constantly," the author teaches the three-syllable mantra of the eleventh Nityā (Nityā-Nityā) and the number of its variations. In that context, "The Swan joined with the Heart, Life-breath, Flavor, Burning, and Earth" is explained as follows: The Swan—the letter *ha*. The Heart—the letter *sa*. The Life-breath—the letter *ka*. Flavor—the letter *la*. Burning—the letter *ra*. Earth—the vowel *u*. The letter *ha* (called the Swan) should be joined with these five. 

This is what is being said: with these six letters beginning with *ha* and ending with the vowel *u* <note>(1) manuscript Tī. adds: "ai ī o 1 ī e o 2..." as an additional reading here</note>, each is joined in the direct order <term>anuloma</term> of beginning and end, creating six variations. Then, each is joined in the reverse order <term>pratiloma</term> from *u* back to *ha*, creating another six variations. When these are combined according to tradition with the six types of the "Secret Mantra" <note>the code-language for the mantra</note> which is the source of the Kulāsundarī-Nityā mantra, seventy-two variations of the mantra arise. Among these, the first is the primary one. **(53)** 

With the verse beginning "Nityā-Nityā," it is stated that among the one hundred and twenty <note>(2) manuscript Tī. reads: "seven hundred and twenty"</note> variations to be described later, there are seventy-two variations. This is said to demonstrate the primary practical application of the majestic variations that appear in sequence. **(54)** 

With the verse beginning "By worshipping her," the author describes the power of one who has perfected the mantra. In that context, "at will" means by the power of yoga to restrain or grace as described in the later chapter on Nityā-Nityā. **(55)**

With the five verses beginning with "The penultimate of Tvaritā" and ending with "the giver of desires," the author teaches the seventeen-syllable mantra of the twelfth Nityā, Nīlapatākā (The Blue Banner). In that context, "the penultimate of Tvaritā"—the letter before the last letter of Tvaritā's mantra. [The combinations are:] 1. *śa-ha*, 2. *sa-ha*, 3. *l-ka*, 4. *l-va-ha*, 5. *l-va-stra*, 6. *l-spha*. Thus is the direct order...

---

<note>(1) Manuscript Tī. includes an additional passage: "ai ī o 1 ī e o 2 ī o 3 ai o ī 4 o ai ī 5 o ī ai 6 These are the...".</note>
<note>(2) Manuscript Tī. reads "seven hundred and twenty" instead of "one hundred and twenty."</note>

--- Page 108 ---
<meta>This page continues the technical construction of the mantras for the Nityā goddesses. It concludes the variations for the eleventh Nityā (Nityā-Nityā) and provides the complete seventeen-syllable mantra for the twelfth Nityā, Nīlapatākā ("The Blue-Bannered"), along with the benefits of her worship.</meta>

->The Air joined with the self is remembered as the fifth; then the two beginning with the middle of the Tenth [Nityā] in sequence. (1) Earth joined with Flavor, the Earth-vowel, and the self; then the sixth [syllable] of Vajreśī in order. **(57)**<-

->The six syllables [of Nityamadadravā], then the third [syllable] of Tvaritā follows. Brilliance joined with Burning, the Wanderer, and the self; then her first [syllable] follows. **(58)**<-

->This is declared as the seventeen-syllabled Nityā named Nīlapatākā. She grants victory in battle and the magical accomplishments <term>siddhis</term> of the sword, the [magic] sandals, and the clairvoyant collyrium. **(59)**<-

->She is the one who subdues <term>prashādhani</term> spirits such as Vetālas, Bird-spirits, Servants, and Piśācas. She is the means for attaining hidden treasures and cave-dwellings and the magical collyrium; she is said to grant all desires. **(60)**<-

---

**[Commentary]**
There are six variations: *Irṃ* 1, *Ir* 2, *Lū* 3, *Lū* 4, *Slū* 5, *Slṛ* 6 (2). Thus, there are six variations in reverse order. In this way, among the twelve variations (3), by applying the six-fold symbolic code <term>saṅketa-vidyā</term>, seventy-two variations become possible. *Ai-Ī-Oṃ* 1, *Ī-Ai-Oṃ* 2, *Ī-Oṃ-Ai* 3, *Ai-Oṃ-I* 4, *Oṃ-Ī-Ai* 5, *O-Ī-Ai* 6. These are the six variations of the root symbolic mantra <term>mūla-saṅketa-vidyā</term>. (4)

"Directly Brahman, the Heart-streak" <note>original: "hṛllekhā"; the mantra syllable Hrīṃ</note> refers to *Hrīṃ*, which is the first seed-syllable <term>bīja</term>—this is the remainder of the instruction.

"Brilliance joined with Burning and the Wanderer"—this is the letter *Pha* joined with the letter *Ra*, the vowel *E*, and the nasal drop <term>bindu</term>, forming *Phreṃ*, which is the second.

"The Heart joined with Burning, Earth, and the self"—this is the letter *Sa* joined with the letter *Ra*, the vowel *Ū*, and the nasal drop <term>bindu</term>, forming the third syllable, *Strūṃ*.

"Then the fifth of Vajreśī"—this means the syllable *Oṃ* is the fourth. **(56)**

"Then Air joined with the self"—this is the vowel *Ā* with the nasal drop. *Āṃ* is the fifth.

"The two beginning with the middle of the Tenth remembered in sequence"—this means the two middle seed-syllables of the tenth Nityā, Kulāsundarī, which are *Klīṃ* and *Aiṃ*, become the sixth and seventh syllables of this mantra.

"Earth joined with Flavor, the Earth-vowel, and the self"—the letter *Va* joined with the letter *La*, the vowel *U*, and the nasal drop, forming *Vlūṃ*, which is the eighth seed-syllable.

"The sixth of Vajreśī in order" **(57)** refers to the six syllables "to the one who intoxicates with the nectar of eternal joy" <note>original: "nitya-mada-drave"</note>. With these six, the mantra reaches fourteen syllables.

"The third of Tvaritā follows"—this is *Huṃ*, the fifteenth seed-syllable.

"Brilliance joined with Burning, the Wanderer, and the self"—this is the letter *Pha* joined with *Ra*, the vowel *E*, and the nasal drop, forming *Phreṃ*, the sixteenth syllable.

"Then her first follows"—this means the syllable *Hrīṃ* is the seventeenth. **(58)**

# Chapter 3 | Exposition of the Vidyās of the Nityā Goddesses: Vijayā, Sarvamaṅgalā, and Jvālāmālinī

->Flavor, Sky, Burning, Pervading, and Earth preceded by Forest,<-
->joined with the Self, is considered the single-syllable mantra of Nityā Vijayā. **(61)**<-
<note>In the symbolic code used here, "Self" refers to the nasalized dot or bindu.</note>

->In debates, in battles, in difficulties, and in legal disputes, she always bestows victory;<-
->Vijayā, the glory of the universe, grants success through mere remembrance. **(62)**<-

->The Heart joined with Water and Forest, and the Self, becomes the Nityā Sarvamaṅgalā.<-
->The one who masters her single-syllable mantra becomes a sky-farer in an instant. **(63)**<-
<note>sky-farer: original "khechara"; a being who has attained the siddhi of flight or high spiritual realization.</note>

->Earth in the Void; Earth with the Sky; Flavor; and then Steady Water.<-
->Speed joined with Fire; the Bow-string and Water; Air joined with Flavor and Air. **(64)**<-

->The Sky joined with Air; Flavor in the Void joined with Fire...<-

---

The text here introduces matters such as the Sword and the Magical Sandals <note>original: "khaḍgapādukā"</note>, which will be explained clearly in the later chapters dedicated to the Nityā Nīlapatākā. **(59, 60)**

Through the two verses beginning with "Flavor" and ending with "Glory," the author teaches the single-syllable mantra <term>vidyā</term> and the power of the thirteenth Nityā, Vijayā.
In this context:
"Flavor" <note>rasa</note> refers to the letter *Bh*.
"Sky" <note>nabhas</note> refers to *M*.
"Burning" <note>dāha</note> refers to *R*.
"Pervading" <note>vyāpta</note> refers to *Y*.
"Earth" <note>kṣmā</note> refers to the vowel *Ū*.
"Preceded by Forest" means joined with the vowel *Au*.
"Joined with the Self" means with the nasal dot <term>bindu</term>.
This is what is meant: the single-syllable mantra is a cluster <term>kūṭa</term> formed of the letters *Bh, M, R, Y, Ū, Au,* and the nasal *Bindu*. The cluster is *Bhmryūm̐*. **(61)**
"In battles and difficulties" refers to wars that are otherwise impossible to win. **(62)**

Through the verse beginning with "Heart and Water," the author teaches the single-syllable mantra and power of the fourteenth Nityā, Sarvamaṅgalā. There, "Heart, Water, and Forest joined with the Self" refers to a cluster joined with the letters *S* (Heart), *V* (Water), *Au* (Forest), and the nasal *Bindu*. The single-syllable mantra is *Svaum̐*. **(63)**

Through the eight verses beginning with "Earth in the Void" and ending with "it shall be," the author teaches the sixty-three-syllable mantra of the fifteenth Nityā, Jvālāmālinī.
In this context:
"Earth" is the letter *O* <note>(1) Some manuscript versions read "the letter Ū".</note>.
"In the Void" is a double *N*, as in *Nne*.
"Earth with the Sky" is the letter *O* with *M*, as in *Mo*.
"Flavor" is *Bh*.
"Steady" is *G*.
"Water" is *V*.
"Speed" is *T*.
"Joined with Fire" is with the vowel *I*, as in *Ti*.
"Bow-string" is *J*.
"Joined with Water and Air" means joined with *V* and the long vowel *Ā*, as in *Jvā*.
"Flavor and Air" is *Lāṃ*. **(64)**

"Sky" is *M*.
"Joined with Air" means joined with the long vowel *Ā*, as in *Mā*.
"Flavor in the Void" is the letter *L* and *N*...

<meta>This page continues the detailed encoding of the mantras (vidyās) for the Nityā goddesses. We have moved from the previous goddesses to the complex, multi-syllable mantra of the fifteenth Nityā, Jvālāmālinī (The Goddess Garlanded with Flames).</meta>

# Page 56
## The Tantrarāja Tantra with the Manoramā Commentary

->Earth joined with the Mover, and Water joined with the preceding letter. **(65)**<-
->Water in Fire; the Heart; Burning and Water; Flavor and Earth; Speed;<-
->the Heart joined with the Self; the Soul-swan with Air; Burning; and the Breath joined with Air. **(66)**<-
->Burning joined with Fire; the Breath and the Mover; the Bow-string with Air; Speed;<-
->Water with the Mover; Earth; the Heart joined with Fire; the Bow-string and Water; and Flavor joined with the Self. **(67)**<-
->Speed joined with Fire; the Bow-string and Water; and Flavor. These two are then repeated.<-
->Speed joined with Burning; through this, those three letters are repeated twice.<-
->Then the Soul-swan joined with Burning, Air, and the Self. **(68)**<-
->The Soul-swan with Burning, Fire, and the Void; and that same Soul-swan joined with Burning and Earth.<-
->There are seven Burnings for her; and then the five starting from the eighth... **(69)**<-

---

**And the Speed...** In "joined with Fire," it means the letter *T* joined with the vowel *I*, forming *Ti*. 
**Earth** <note>original: "gotrā"</note> refers to the letter *D*. 
**Joined with the Mover** <note>original: "careṇa sahitā"</note> means joined with the vowel *E*, forming *De*. 
**Water** refers to the letter *V*. 
**Joined with the preceding letter** means the letter *V* is joined with the vowel *I* <note>following the pattern of the previous syllable</note>, and when combined with the Earth-syllable *De*, it forms *Devi*. **(65)**

**Water in Fire** — Water is *V* and Fire is the vowel *I*, forming *Vi*. 
**Heart** <note>original: "hṛt"</note> is the letter *S*. 
**Burning and Water** — Burning is *R* and Water is *V*, forming *Rv*. 
**Flavor and Earth** — Flavor is *Bh* and Earth is the vowel *U*, forming *Bhū*. 
**Speed** is the letter *T*. 
**Heart joined with the Self** — "Joined with the Self" <note>svayuk</note> means joined with the nasal dot <term>bindu</term>, which specifically qualifies the Heart-syllable *S*, forming *Saṃ*. 
**The Soul-swan with Air** <note>original: "haṃsaśca marutā"</note> refers to the letter *H* with the vowel *Ā*, forming *Hā*. 
**Burning** is the letter *R*. 
**The Breath joined with Air** — Breath <note>prāṇa</note> is *K* joined with the vowel *Ā*, forming *Kā*. **(66)**

**Burning joined with Fire** — The letter *R* joined with the vowel *Ī*, forming *Rī*. 
**Breath and Mover** — The letter *K* with the vowel *E*, forming *Ke*. 
**Bow-string with Air** — The letter *J* with the vowel *Ā*, forming *Jā*. 
**Speed** is the letter *T*. 
**Water with the Mover** <note>original: "careṇāmbu"</note> forms *Ve*. 
**Earth** is *D*. 
**Heart joined with Fire** — The letter *S* with the vowel *I*, forming *Si*. 
**Bow-string and Water** — The letters *J* and *V* together, forming *Jv*. 
**Flavor joined with the Self** — The letter *L* with the dot <note>bindu</note>, forming *Laṃ*. **(67)**

**Speed joined with Fire** — The letter *T* with the vowel *I*, forming *Ti*. 
**Bow-string and Water** — The cluster *Jv*. 
**Flavor** — The letter *L*. 
**These two are then repeated** — This refers to the two previous letters <note>Jv and L</note>, which should be repeated to form *Jvala jvala*. 
**Speed joined with Burning** — The letter *P* joined with *R*, forming *Pr*. 
**Through this, they are repeated twice** — Using this letter *Pr*, the previously mentioned two-syllable group is repeated twice, meaning one should recite the three syllables *Prajvala* twice <note>forming "Prajvala prajvala"</note>. 
**The Soul-swan joined with Burning, Air, and the Self** <note>original: "haṃsodāhamarutsvayuk"</note> results in the seed-syllable <term>bīja</term> *Hrīṃ*. **(68)**

**The Soul-swan with Burning, Fire, and the Void** — This also refers to the syllable *Hrīṃ*. 
**Joined with Burning and Earth** — This refers to the Soul-swan <note>the letter H</note> joined with a dot, forming *Haṃ*. 
**Seven Burnings** — The syllable *Ra* should be recited seven times. 
**Then** — After this. 
**For her** — Of this mantra <note>vidyā</note>. 
The word **"are"** <note>syuḥ</note> connects to both what precedes and follows it, like the eye of a crow <note>a traditional metaphor for a word that serves two sentences at once</note>. 
**The five starting from the eighth** — Of this mantra...

# In the Tantrarāja along with the commentary named Manoramā

->Through the letters of Life, Fire, Earth, Water, and Space, joined with the seven-syllable Power-mantra, (66)<-

The text now teaches the twenty-syllable mantras. The phrase "by the letters declared in the code" means the following: letters of the alphabet <term>Mātṛkā; the "little mothers" or phonemes of the Sanskrit language</term> are divided among the five elements as described in the twenty-five verses starting with "Wind" <note>original: "vāto marut"</note>.

Each of these mantras is composed of ten letters associated with Life, Fire, Earth, Water, and Space respectively, followed by the two-syllable word for Power <note>original: "śakti"</note>, and ending with a seven-syllable formula. Thus, four of the mantras consist of twenty-one syllables, while the Space mantra consists of twenty syllables. These five mantras correspond to the five elements in the stated order. 

The structure of these five mantras is written in the ritual manual for the worship of the goddess Lalitā Nityā <note>original: "lalitānityāsaparyākrama"</note>, but their form is clearly revealed here. To visualize this, one should draw eleven vertical lines and six horizontal lines with equal spacing. This creates five rows, each containing ten boxes. 

In these boxes, one should write the letters of the alphabet from 'a' onwards in the following order:

| Row | Contents (Letters of the Alphabet) | Elemental Association |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | The five short vowels (a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ) <note>each written twice to fill ten boxes</note> | Life / Air <note>original: "prāṇa"</note> |
| 2 | The five long vowels (ā, ī, ū, ṝ, ḹ) | Fire <note>original: "agni"</note> |
| 3 | The diphthongs and nasals (e, ai, o, au, aṃ) | Earth <note>original: "ilā"</note> |
| 4 | The consonants from *ka* to *ma* and *ya* to *śa* in groups of five | Water <note>original: "ambu"</note> |
| 5 | The remaining five letters (ṣa, la, sa, ha, kṣa) | Space / Ether <note>original: "kha"</note> |

One should observe that the ten letters in the top row constitute the "Life" element. The ten letters in the second row constitute "Fire." The ten in the third row are "Earth." The ten in the fourth row are "Water." The ten in the fifth row are "Space." At the end of these ten letters, one adds the ten-syllable name of that element (except for Space, which uses a single syllable), then adds the two-syllable word "Shakti" (Power), and finally the seven-syllable formula. (66)

By following this method, the five Elemental Mantras of twenty-one syllables are formed. "By their light" means by their power or influence. "Exists" <note>original: "vartate"</note> means that the universe is maintained or created by them even now. (67)

With the three verses starting from "Regarding the former" and ending with "the mantra," the text teaches the sixteen-syllable Offering Mantra <term>bali-mantra; a mantra used when presenting offerings</term> common to all Sixteen Nityās <note>the sixteen aspects of the lunar goddess</note>.

# [In Chapter 3] Description of the Five Element Mantras | 63

The sound *rasa* <note>original: "rasa", a code for the letter 'sa'</note> should be joined with the pervasive light; this is the third [syllable], and the fourth follows. *Rasa* joined with Earth <note>the letter 'la'</note> and *raya* <note>the letter 'ra'</note> joined with a vowel, O Supreme Goddess! (99)

*Rasa* joined with the pervading Earth <note>the syllable "bhyo"</note>; then *Hamsa* <note>the letter 'ha'</note> joined with Earth and Space <note>the nasal 'm'</note>. These are the first and last letters. Thus is declared the sixteen-syllable mantra of the **Offering** <term>Bali-mantra; a ritual formula used when presenting food or aromatic offerings to the deities</term>. (100)

This consists of the essence of the Fire element, well-proclaimed as "pervading." By internalizing this in the heart, that element is assimilated into one’s own self. (101)

---

### Thus ends the third chapter in the 
### Śrī Kādimata of the Sixteen Nityā Tantras.

---

**The commentary named "Manoramā" (The Delight of the Mind):**

The two dentals <note>original: "dantyakau", referring to sounds produced by the teeth</note> — in the eight-syllable Soul Mantra <note>original: "ātmāṣṭākṣaramantra"</note> and the preceding element, the knowledge of Kurukullā <note>a red goddess of magnetizing and enchantment</term>, the fourteenth and fifteenth syllables are "sarva" <note>meaning "all"</note>. These two syllables become the third and fourth syllables here. "Water, not Fire" <note>original: "ambu nāgniḥ"</note> — the word "joined" is understood. It results in the sound *vi*. "Space, the Void" <note>original: "vāḥ sūnyaṃ"</note> results in *dhra*. "Life joined with the flow of water" — the letter *ka* joined with the vowels *ṛ* and *ta* is produced. (98) 

*Rasa* should be joined with the pervading light — this results in *bhye*. The terms "Maya" and "Shakti" in this Tantra refer to the *Hṛllekhā* <note>the seed-syllable "Hrīṃ"</note> and the *Visarga* <note>the aspirate "ḥ" sound</note> respectively. In this context, the addition of one or the other is determined by the strength of the oral tradition. The third and fourth syllables are "sarva", which are the ninth and tenth syllables here. *Rasa* joined with Earth — the word "joined" is understood — results in *bhū*, which is the eleventh syllable. *Raya* joined with a vowel results in *te*, the twelfth syllable. "O Supreme Goddess" is a form of address. (99) 

*Rasa* joined with the pervading Earth results in *bhyo*, the thirteenth syllable. *Hamsa* joined with Earth and Space results in *haṃ*, the fourteenth syllable. The first and last letters — the eight-syllable Soul Mantra followed by *svāhā* <note>the exclamation used when making an offering into fire</note> — forms the fifteenth. Thus, the sixteen-syllable mantra is declared as the Offering Mantra for all the Sixteen Nityās. (100)

->Thus, in the commentary named *Manoramā* (The Delight of the Mind),<-
->written by Subhagānandanātha on the complete Tantra known as<-
->the Śrī Kādimata (from the Sixteen Nityā Tantras) and reflecting<-
->the essence of the King of Lions of the Prapañcasāra,<-
->the third chapter, which illuminates the nature of the<-
->Nityā-vidyā, is now fully concluded and<-
->reviewed.<-

->The total number of sections in the third chapter consists of one diagram (yantra),<-
->and the total length of the commentary is stated to be<-
->two hundred and ninety-seven and a half verses.<-

# Now Begins the Fourth Chapter

->Now, O Beloved! I shall describe in proper sequence<-
->the worship of the first among the Sixteen Nityās,<-
->which daily bestows the fulfillment of all goals. (1)<-

->Listen, through these next three chapters, to the<-
->daily, occasional, and desire-based rites,<-
->by which even one burdened by great sins attains success. (2)<-

->The mantras for the three-fold placement, the four seats,<-
->the invocation mantra, and the collective offering mantra; (3)<-

->The seed-syllables for the ritual gestures and weapons,<-
->the visualization of the goddess with her retinue,<-
->and the ritual sequence for daily worship; (4)<-

->The names of the powers within the nine enclosures,<-
->the method of worship, the union of the self with the mantra,<-
->the ritual offerings, and the sequence of recitation. (5)<-

->The first [seed-syllable] is Wind joined with itself; the second is<-
->Air with its own; the third is through the sound of the heart.<-
->This is the first [goddess]. (6)<-

## Now Begins the Fourth Chapter

In the previous <term>Third Chapter</term> <note>original: "tṛtīya-paṭale"</note>, the knowledge of the <term>Sixteen Nityās</term> <note>a group of sixteen lunar goddesses in the Tantric tradition</note> was taught. Now, the author teaches the sequence of worship—both daily and occasional—for the primary goddess, <term>Lalitā</term>, who is the "Owner of the Limbs" <note>the central figure to whom the other Nityās are subordinate</note>. This is covered in the next three chapters, starting with "Now, the Sixteen Nityās," each consisting of approximately one hundred verses. 

Within these first five verses, the contents of the fourth, fifth, and sixth chapters are summarized. Here, <term>Daily</term> <note>original: "nitya"</note> refers to the regular worship. <term>Occasional</term> <note>original: "naimittika"</note> and <term>Desire-based</term> <note>original: "kāmya", performed to achieve a specific result</note> are adjectives describing the worship. The phrase "even one burdened by great sins" refers to someone who <insert>harbors a hatred for discernment</insert>. (2)

From the "mantras of the three-fold placement" <note>original: "nyāsa-traya", the ritual practice of "placing" mantras on the body to sanctify it</note> until the mention of "seed-syllables," the author lists twenty-two mantras in a verse and a quarter. The tradition <note>original: "sampradāya"</note> holds that the order of the three placements is mentioned here out of sequence simply to facilitate the meter of the verse. The "collective offering mantra" consists of <gloss>two seed-syllables</gloss>. (5)

From the verse beginning with "Wind" until the mention of "cleaning," the author teaches the <term>Wisdom of Hand Purification</term> <note>original: "kara-śuddhi-vidyā"</note> and the method of its performance. In this context, "Wind joined with itself" results in the first seed-syllable, *Om*. "Air with its own" refers to the second...

# [ Fourth Chapter ]
## Description of the Six-fold Placement, the Goddess’s Seat, the Circle Seat, and the Mantra Knowledge

> One should perform the purification of the hands by rubbing them together.
> Then, the six limbs: Heart, Head, Tuft, Armor, Eyes, and Weapon. (7)
> 
> The second [mantra] is known as the goddess <term>Kulasundarī</term> <note>Literally "The Beauty of the Clan," one of the sixteen Nityā goddesses</note>. 
> The third, beginning with the Power-seed, is the <term>Goddess’s Seat</term> <note>original: "devyātmāsana"</note>; it is formed with this mantra. (8)
> 
> From the union with <term>Haṃsa</term> <note>A sacred mantra associated with the breath and the soul</note> among the three, the <term>Circle Seat</term> <note>original: "cakrāsana"</note> is declared.
> The fifth is joined with the "Heart of Haṃsa," and is likewise the <term>Seat of All Mantras</term> <note>original: "sarvamantrāsana"</note>. (9)

---

The second—<term>Āṃ</term> is the second seed-syllable. Together with this heart-seed, the third—<term>Sauḥ</term> is the third.
"This is the first"—this refers to the <term>Vidyā</term> <note>The sacred mantra-knowledge</note> mentioned previously. (6) "Purification"—Purification means making the hands fit to touch the implements of worship. "By rubbing them together"—one should understand this as rubbing the palms of the left and right hands against each other.

With the passage beginning with "Heart" and ending with "Beauty," the author teaches the <term>ṣaḍaṅga</term> (Six Limbs) and the <term>ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa-vidyā</term> <note>The ritual practice of projecting six specific syllables onto parts of the body for protection and sanctification</note>.
There, the "second"—one should understand this as the second mantra among the twenty-two specified. (7)

With the second half of the verse beginning with "The third" and ending with "with this," the author teaches the mantra for the <term>Goddess’s Seat</term>. In that context,
"The third is she herself"—it is the same <term>Kulasundarī</term> mantra mentioned in the Six-fold Placement. "Beginning with Power"—here, "Power" refers to the seed-syllable <term>Hrīṃ</term> <note>original: "khā"</note>.
The word "in the three" from the beginning of the next verse follows from the "Invocation Mantra." This implies the following:
One should place the seed-syllable <term>Hrīṃ</term> before each of the three seeds. Thus: <term>Hrīṃ Aiṃ</term>, <term>Hrīṃ Klīṃ</term>, <term>Hrīṃ Sauḥ</term>. The "Goddess’s Seat"—the seat or "place of attainment" for all the Powers who are manifestations of the Goddess in their limited forms; it means the place of attainment for all deities. Here, the sequence of the description deviates from the initial list for the sake of convenience, as the four "Seat-mantras" are related to the second mantra. The counting of "The third" is also for convenience of instruction. (8)

With the first half of the verse beginning with "In the three," the author teaches the mantra for the <term>Circle Seat</term>. There, "from the union with Haṃsa"—by adding the sound "Ha" to the beginning of each of the three seeds of the <term>Bālā</term> mantra, one recites: <term>Haiṃ</term>, <term>Hklīṃ</term>, <term>Hsauḥ</term>.
This is the fourth, the <term>Circle Seat</term> mantra. "Circle Seat" means the seat or place of attainment for all <term>Yantras</term> <note>Sacred geometric diagrams</note> which are composed of the essence of the mantras and deities.

With the second half [of verse 9] beginning with "Haṃsa," the author teaches the mantra for the <term>Seat of All Mantras</term>. There, "joined with the Heart of Haṃsa" is the phrase to be completed. As before, by adding the sounds "Ha" and "Sa" to the beginning of the three seeds, one recites: <term>Hsaiṃ</term>...
