# Adorned with red incense, red garments, and garlands, and decorated with red ornaments (1). 
# With a cheerful heart, and a body scented with camphor (2). || 19 ||

# Seated in the lotus posture, facing east, having restrained the breath and controlled the senses, 
# Having given a ritual offering with the sixteen-syllable mantra, he should worship the Gurus. || 20 ||

# Afterwards, by his (the Guru's) command, he should perform the worship on his head according to the rule, 
# Having meditated upon the Master who has become one with the Deity, and himself as being of that same divine nature. || 21 ||

# One should worship the lamp made of nine gems, shining with nine sections, 
# Using the Matrika [the sacred alphabet] at the beginning, then the name, and ending with the word "Salutation." || 22 ||

---

With the three verses beginning with "Red" and ending with "that same nature," the author teaches the sequence for beginning the worship.

In those verses: **Lotus posture** <term>Padmāsana — a cross-legged sitting position used in meditation</term>. This is not described here because it will be explained later in the text. **Having restrained the breath** — having performed breath control <term>Prāṇāyāma — the yogic practice of regulating the breath</term>. Although breath control will also be explained later, I will explain it a bit here: closing the left nostril, one should expel the breath <note>original: "mārutaṃ"</note> through the right nostril according to one's strength. Then, closing the right nostril, one should inhale the breath through the left nostril with full strength. Again, having performed "exhalation" <term>Recaka</term> and "inhalation" <term>Pūraka</term> in this way, and having held the breath inside according to one's power <note>This refers to Kumbhaka, or breath retention</note>, one should slowly, slowly release it. This is the sequence of breath control everywhere. 

**Controlled** — one whose internal and external senses are withdrawn from all other objects. **With the sixteen-syllable mantra** — with the mantra whose nature was taught at the end of the third chapter. Having given a ritual offering <term>bali — a food offering to spirits or deities</term>, one should worship as before. **The Gurus on the head** — this means one should worship them as residing in the crown aperture <term>Brahmarandhra — the spiritual center at the top of the skull</term> according to the tradition. **His** — refers to one's own Master. **According to the rule** — in the manner that will be described. **The Master who has become one with That** — with the understanding that the Master exists in the very form of the Deity. || 19 || 20 || 21 ||

With the eight verses starting with "Nine gems" and ending with "Mothers," he teaches the sequence of worship for the dwelling place of the Goddess and provides the mantras for it. In those verses: **Using the Matrika at the beginning** — this means one should utter the fifty-one letters of the alphabet from *A* to *Kṣa*, accompanied by the nasal dot <term>Bindu — a dot representing the sacred nasal resonance</term>, preceded by the two seed-syllables. After that, one adds the specific name, and then the word "Salutation" <note>original: "Namaḥ"</note>. 

For example: Hrīṃ (7) Śrīṃ (7) Aṃ (7) Āṃ (7) Iṃ (7) Īṃ (7) Uṃ (7) Ūṃ (7) Ṛṃ (7) Ṝṃ (7) Lṛṃ (7) Ḹṃ (7) Eṃ (7) Aiṃ (7) Oṃ (7) Auṃ (7) Aṃ (7) Aḥ (7) Kaṃ (7) Khaṃ (7) Gaṃ (7) Ghaṃ (7) Ṅaṃ (7) Caṃ (7) Chaṃ (7) Jaṃ (7) Jhaṃ (7) Ñaṃ (7) Ṭaṃ (7) Ṭhaṃ (7) Ḍaṃ (7) Ḍhaṃ (7) Ṇaṃ (7) Taṃ (7) Thaṃ (7) Daṃ (7) Dhaṃ (7) Naṃ (7) Paṃ (7) Phaṃ (7) Baṃ (7) Bhaṃ (7) Maṃ (7) Yaṃ (7) Raṃ (7)

### In the 5th Chapter: Explanation of the Mantras for the Worship of the Nine Gems, etc.

# The Topaz, the Sapphire, and the Cat’s-eye, the Coral as well as the Pearl; 
# Toward the Northeast, the Emerald, the Diamond, the Hessonite, and the Ruby. || 23 ||

# One should also worship the Garden of Wish-fulfilling Trees and the Seasons. 
# Then, one should worship the forms known as the Senses in the West. || 24 ||

# One should first worship the "Elephants" of the Sense-objects in the East using their own names. 
# From the West moving toward the center, one should worship the Nine Gems in reverse order. || 25 ||

# Time, Gesture, the Sacred Alphabet, the Gem, the Region, and the Teacher; 
# Reality, the Planets, and the Form—each ending with the name of the Mistress of the Wheel. || 26 ||

---

**laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ Salutation to the Island of the Nine Gems.** <note>original: "laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ navaratnadvīpāya namaḥ"</note> By this mantra [the worship is performed]. In this context, up until the section on the sense-objects, one should perform the worship using the respective names of the entities ending with the word "Salutation" <note>original: "namas"</note>. || 22 ||

With the verse beginning with **"The Topaz,"** the author teaches the names of the nine gems. There, the statement **"Toward the Northeast, the Emerald"** is made because in the chapter on the goddess Kurukullā it will be stated that the Topaz is in the West; therefore, he shows the circumambulatory order <note>original: "prādakṣiṇyakramaṃ"</note>. **Toward the Northeast** means in the Northeastern direction. || 23 || 

**The Garden of Wish-fulfilling Trees** <term>Kalpakodyāna — a celestial garden where trees grant all desires</term> is worshipped with: **hrīṃ śrīṃ Salutation to the Garden of Wish-fulfilling Trees.** Right here in the Island of Gems, one says: **hrīṃ śrīṃ Salutation to the Seasons.** 

**The Senses** <term>Indriyas — the ten faculties of perception and action</term> are ten: hearing, touch, sight, taste, smell, speech, hands, feet, anus, and the genitals. **In the West** means in front of the Goddess's pavilion <term>Maṇḍapa — a ritual hall or pavilion</term>: **hrīṃ śrīṃ Salutation to the Horses of the Senses.** 

**The Sense-objects** <term>Indriyārthas — the targets of the senses</term> are the ten known as sound, touch, form, taste, smell, speech, grasping, movement, excretion, and sexual bliss, in that order. **In the East** means at the back of the Goddess's pavilion: **hrīṃ śrīṃ Salutation to the Elephants of the Sense-objects.** Thus one should worship the Nine Gems. || 24 || 25 ||

With the verse beginning with **"Time, Gesture,"** the author teaches the worship mantras for the nine sections made of the nine gems, which represent Time and the other categories, each embodied by the Nine Lords. This refers to the **Lords of the Teachers** <note>original: "gurunātha"</note>. 

There, the nine-fold nature of **Time** <term>Kāla</term> is derived from its forms as: the minute <note>original: "ghaṭikā" — a unit of about 24 minutes</note>, the day-and-night, the day of the week, the lunar day, the fortnight, the month, the season, and the year. 

The nine-fold nature of the **Gesture** <term>Mudrā</term> is through the previously mentioned gestures of "Agitating" and so on. 

The nine-fold nature of the **Sacred Alphabet** <term>Mātṛkā</term> is through the sequence of letter-groups <note>original: "varga"</note> that will be explained later. 

The nine-fold nature of the **Gem** is according to the forms already stated. 

The nine-fold nature of the **Region** <term>Deśa</term> is the same as the nine-fold nature of the gems. 

The nine-fold nature of the **Lords** <note>original: "Nāthas" — the spiritual masters</note> is according to the stated order. 

The nine-fold nature of the **Realities** <term>Tattvas</term> is through the process of "five-fold division" <note>original: "pañcīkaraṇa"</note> of the triad consisting of the Knower, the Knowledge, and the Known. This is because these are accepted as eternal. 

The nine-fold nature of the **Planets** <term>Grahas</term> is quite well-known. 

The nine-fold nature of the **Forms** <term>Mūrtis</term> consists of: skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen, vitality, and the breath. These are all named as ending with the **Mistress of the Wheel** <term>Cakreśvarī</term>. || 26 ||

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for the internal ritual worship (puja) described in the "Tantra-raja." # In the King of Tantras, along with the commentary named "The Mind-Delighting"

# Having worshipped in the stated order, O Beloved, the Mistress of each respective Wheel; [then worship] the Ruby Pavilion in the center, surrounded by a moat of the water of compassion. || 27 ||

# One should worship Region, Time, as well as Form and Sound in the corners, along with the Goddess of Form, and then the Music Yoginis. || 28 ||

# Along with the Wheel of all "Hidden," "Revealed," and "Perfected" Yoginis, one should worship all the Mothers, endowed with the seven-syllable forms. || 29 ||

# One should place the consecrated offering-water in a golden vessel with a base, mixed with yellow pigment, camphor, saffron, and a small amount of musk. || 30 ||

# One should contemplate the elements of Fire, Sun, and Moon, O Supreme Goddess! One should chant [the mantra] ten times and satisfy the Yogini with that water. || 31 ||

---

The phrase **In order** means: one should worship these nine Mistresses of the Wheels <term>Cakreśvarī — the female deity presiding over a specific level of a mandala</term> by uttering the name of the specific wheel followed by the title "Mistress of the Wheel." The formula is: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the Power-Sandals of the Mistress of the Wheel of Time.* <note>original: "hrīṃ śrīṃ kālacakreśvarīśaktipādukāṃ pūjayāmi"</note> In this context, the word "Power" <note>original: "śakti"</note> is included based on traditional lineage. The plural is used because each of the nine deities has nine forms. **O Beloved** is an address to the Goddess. **A moat of the water of compassion** means a pavilion made of rubies surrounded by a moat filled with water that consists of the Goddess’s mercy. The ritual formula is: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, Salutation to the moat of the water of compassion; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, Salutation to the Ruby Pavilion.* <note>original: "hrīṃ śrīṃ karuṇātoyaparikhāyai namaḥ; hrīṃ śrīṃ māṇikyamaṇḍapāya namaḥ"</note> Here too, the addition of the word "Salutation" <note>original: "namas"</note> is according to tradition. || 27 ||

With the verse beginning with **Region**, the author teaches the goddesses who represent the forces of limitation <term>saṅkoca-kārikā — powers that contract infinite consciousness into limited experience</term>. Among them: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the Power-Sandals of the Goddess who takes the form of Region.* One should follow the same pattern for others, such as those related to the "Mantra-shaktis," and likewise in the reverse order of the "Nivritti" <note>original: "nivṛttyādi-vilomataḥ" — referring to the stages of cosmic dissolution</note> and so on. Here, the terms **Region, Time, Form, and Sound** are mentioned twice to show the relationship between cause and effect. The first set represents the "effect" in nine-fold form; the second represents the "cause." **The Music Yoginis** are the goddesses who delight in dance, song, and musical instruments. The formula is: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the Power-Sandals of the Music Yoginis.* Here also, the addition of the word "Power" and the use of the plural follows the previous rule. || 28 ||

The first half of the verse beginning with **All Hidden** is itself the form of the mantra, excluding the final syllable. In this context, **Yogini** <note>original: "yogini"</note> refers to the collective group of Yoginis. The formula is: *Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [to the] Wheel of all Hidden, Revealed, and Perfected Yoginis...*

-># Chapter 5: Discourse on the Ritual Offering and Related Rites<-

One should meditate on the three sections of the Mantra-Knowledge <term>vidyā-khaṇḍa-trayam — the three specific divisions of the sacred mantra associated with the Goddess</term> in the base of the spine, the heart, and the cranial aperture. One should envision them as red, and through the infusion of that radiance, one's own body becomes red. || 32 ||

Then, after performing breath control <term>prāṇāyāma — the yogic practice of regulating the life-force</term> and the previously mentioned purification of the hands, one should establish the ritual seat using the first and the third through sixth syllables [of the mantra]. || 33 ||

**I worship the Divine Sandals.** <note>original: "śrīpādukāḥ pūjayāmi"</note> In this context as well, the plural is used due to the multiplicity of the deities, and the word "Divine" <note>original: "śrī"</note> is used as explained previously. **All the Mothers** means all the Powers <note>original: "śakti"</note>. The application of this practice is common to each of those respective Powers. This is what is expressed in these eight verses: the Goddess is the manifestation of the form imagined through words, arising from the embodied form of the body and senses. || 28 ||

With the two verses beginning with **"Gold..."** <note>original: "hema..."</note> and ending with **"...of the Yoginis,"** the author teaches the method of preparing the ritual offering <term>arghya — a consecrated water offering</term> for the worship of the deity and its subsequent use. In that context, **the Moon** <note>original: "candra"</note> refers to camphor. **Light** <note>original: "laghu"</note> refers to agarwood. || 30 ||

**"O Supreme Goddess"** is the address used for the Goddess. **"One should chant it ten times"** — the word "it" refers to the third section of the Mantra-Knowledge. **"With that"** means with the offering water. **"Yoginis"** refers to the Powers that make up the Goddess's retinue.

This is what is being said: Within the water held in the ritual vessel at the base, one should recognize the three sections of the Mantra-Knowledge as being composed of Fire, Sun, and Moon. One should then perceive the five substances placed within it as being composed of the five elements, beginning with Earth. After showing the "Cow" and "Womb" hand-gestures <term>mudrās — ritual hand positions used to channel energy</term> as previously described, and visualizing the Sacred Wheel <term>śrīcakra — the complex geometric diagram of the Goddess</term> within the water, one should perform the worship. 

This is done according to the external sequence to be described in the chapter on the Goddess Nityaklinna, using the six-limbed mantras and the sixteen Nitya mantras once each, then ten times with the third section of the Mantra-Knowledge, and once with the Root-Knowledge and the Nitya mantra. Having recited these, one should perform the prescribed actions with that offering water. || 31 ||

With the verse-and-a-quarter beginning with **"In the base..."** and ending with **"...having performed,"** the author teaches what should be contemplated during the time of breath control. In that context, **"in the aperture"** means in the cranial opening <term>brahmarandhra — the "hole of Brahma" at the top of the head where the soul is said to exit</term>. **"By the infusion of that radiance"** means by the infusion of the radiance of those [three sections]. **"Infusion"** <note>original: "vedha"</note> refers to becoming one with that essence. 

The first and last sections of the Mantra-Knowledge, which are of the nature of Fire and Moon and located in the base and the cranial opening respectively, have their light spread upward and downward. The middle section, which is of the nature of the Sun and located in the heart, has its light spread both upward and downward, thereby merging with the others. This is what is meant: One should contemplate internally and externally the three radiances — the spread of the Sun-light of the second section in the heart, which is inlaid with the Fire-light of the first section in the Root-base <term>mūlādhāra — the lowest energy center at the base of the spine</term>, and the Moon-light of the third section in the cranial opening which is connected to it — as a single, undivided, merged form. Breath control is performed as before, followed by the recitation and worship of the Wisdom of Lalita—

*The wise practitioner should worship using the names joined between [the seed-syllables and the word] "salutations." *With the palm extended, one touches the heart and the head. The "tuft" <note>śikhā — the lock of hair at the crown of the head</note> is correctly touched with the fist, keeping the thumb pointing downward.* || 35 ||

*With both hands held in that same manner, one touches the "armor" <note>kavaca — a protective energy field</note> from the shoulders down to the navel. The index, middle, and ring fingers are used in order to touch the three eyes.* || 36 ||

*With the two palms extended, the "three claps" <note>tāla-traya — a rhythmic clapping to clear the ritual space</note> are performed. The "weapon" <note>astra</note> mantra is uttered with a snapping sound made by the index finger and the thumb.* || 37 ||

*By doing this in the cardinal directions, the intermediate directions, above, below, and in the center, one destroys all obstacles. Then, having performed the placement <term>nyāsa</term> of the Goddesses of Speech beginning with Vashini according to the previously stated method...* || 38 ||

---

In states of deep meditation <term>samādhi</term>, breath control <term>prāṇāyāma</term> and the three sections of the sacred Knowledge <term>vidyā-khaṇḍa-trayam</term> should be envisioned as a triple radiance. In other contexts, one should only visualize the triple radiance residing in the three primary energy centers <term>ādhāra-traya — usually referring to the base, heart, and head</term>. || 32 ||

Through the five verses [33-38] beginning with **"Having performed"** and ending with **"according to the method,"** the author teaches the ritual placement and other rites. <note>The text notes a variation in the manuscript count of verses here.</note> Among these, with the first [mantra] — which was stated in the previous chapter starting with the words **"the wind combined with the self"** — and with the four mantras from the third to the sixth, one should worship the four seats <term>āsana</term>. In these four mantras for the seats, the initial two seed-syllables are not added, according to the tradition.

# Chapter 5: On the Daily Worship, the Fire Ritual, and the Conclusion
### Page 85

One should perform the invocation using the "seventh Knowledge" <term>saptamī-vidyā — referring to the specific mantra of the Goddess Tripurasundari</term> and then the "Three-Fold" gesture <term>trikhaṇḍā-mudrā</term>. Having placed her in the center of the womb <note>original: "yoni" — the central triangle of the Śrī Cakra</note> of the middle chakra which stands before the practitioner... || 39 ||

...and having meditated on her in that form, surrounded by her attendants, one should display the ritual hand-gestures <term>mudrā</term>. Seventeen such gestures have been declared; then, one should worship her with ritual offerings <term>upacāra</term>. || 40 ||

In the space between the goddesses Jayinī and Vimalā, one should worship the nine Lords <note>the lineage of spiritual masters or Gurus</note> in groups of three <margin>(1) The manuscript reads "exclude the Lords of the thirty."</margin>. Then, one also worships the fifteen Nityas <note>the lunar goddesses representing the days of the moon's cycle</note> as they are the Goddess's own forms. || 41 ||

One should recite the specific mantras into the form of the Goddess <margin>(2) The manuscript reads "one should worship those specific ones."</margin>, becoming one with her in the proper sequence. Beginning with the western gate, one should then worship the right door-post <note>original: "dakṣa-śākhā"</note> <margin>(3) The manuscript reads "the right door-post."</margin> of the entrance... || 42 ||

...and similarly in the eight directions around her, as well as below and above, as previously described. In the same way, one should worship the eight Mother-goddesses starting with Brāhmī in the first enclosure. || 43 ||

---

"With the Knowledge of the Beautiful One" <note>Sundarī-vidyā</note> is the phrase that completes the sense here. In every instance of the "Three Placements" <term>nyāsa</term>, there is no "abundance of the two seed-syllables" <margin>(4) The commentary manuscript reads "abundance of the two seed-syllables."</margin>. According to the union previously mentioned—that is, the union of the letters and syllable-clusters <term>varṇa-kūṭa</term> explained in the previous chapter. || 35–38 ||

With twenty-five verses starting from "Invocation with the seventh" and ending with "pleasant speech," the author teaches the Goddess’s daily worship, the method for the daily fire ritual <term>homa</term>, and the conclusion of the worship <margin>(5) The commentary manuscript reads "worship and the sacrificial offering."</margin>. In this context, "with the seventh" refers to the sacred mantra <term>vidyā</term>. "With the Three-Fold gesture" refers to the hand-sign described in the previous chapter starting with the words "the heart of the Swan" <note>haṃsa-hṛd</note>. "In that form" means the physical appearance described in the previous chapter in the verse beginning "The Red One" <note>lohitā</note>. One should display the mudrās. "Seventeen have been declared" means one should show the seventeen hand-gestures starting with "Establishing" and ending with the four "Weapons" mentioned in the previous chapter. By "offerings," he means either sixteen or five; the five offerings are perfume, flowers, incense, a lamp, and food offerings <term>naivedya</term>. || 39–40 ||

"The thirty" refers to the Divine, the Perfected, and the Human masters <note>divya, siddha, and mānuṣa gurus</note> seated in rows of three from the Goddess's left side to her right side; the Goddess herself makes the group "thirty." "Becoming one with her" means that her presence resides within those specific forms as well. "In order" means in the sequence of increasing from one. "Right door-post" refers to the post of the gate on the side of the Goddess that is not the left. || 41–42 ||

Regarding the phrase "around": here, one worships first in the cardinal directions, then in the intermediate directions. In each of those locations, one worships on the Goddess’s right side. Similarly, just as with the powers like "Atomicity" <term>aṇimā</term>, one worships Brāhmī and the other Mothers there on the Goddess’s left side.

# In the Tantrarāja, with the Commentary Named Manoramā
### Page 87

## Chapter 5: On Daily Worship, Fire Sacrifices, and the Science of Wisdom

In the application of the recitation mantra <term>japa-mantra — the repetition of a sacred formula</term>, one uses the five "perfected" mantras <note>original: "siddha-mantraiḥ"</note>. The bow used in such a rite is gross in form, made from a thick stalk of sugarcane. || 51 ||

One should worship at the center of the womb-triangle <note>original: "madhya-yoni" — the central triangle of the Śrī Cakra</note>, at its tips and corners, according to the prescribed sequence of numbers. One should worship the Shaktis <note>personifications of divine power</note> beginning with Kameshvari, and worship Shiva in the very center. || 52 ||

After displaying the nine ritual gestures <term>mudrās</term> and then the four weapons-gestures in sequence, and after performing the offerings <note>original: "upacārān" — such as incense, lamps, and food</note> combined with the prescribed internal yoga: || 53 ||

Having recited the mantra ten times, the practitioner should contemplate their own self as the very body of the deity. Within one's own self <note>original: "svātmani"</note>, one should worship the fifteen Eternal Goddesses <term>Nityās — the goddesses representing the fifteen days of the waxing moon</term>. || 54 ||

Then, after worshipping with devotion using the five mantras of the "Elemental Selves" <note>original: "bhūtātmabhiḥ" — referring to the purification of the five elements within the body</note>, and worshipping with the eight-syllabled mantra of the Self, one should then begin the main recitation. || 55 ||

One should recite the mantra a thousand times before the Goddess, or a hundred times as the daily requirement for that day. Alternatively, it is said that one may recite it sixty times at each of the three junctions of the day <note>dawn, noon, and sunset</note>, according to the form previously described. || 56 ||

---

**Commentary:**
**These are the four gestures.** **In sequence** means in the order previously stated. **Offerings** refers to those mentioned before. **In sequence** here implies that one should perform the sixteen types of service <term>ṣoḍaśopacāra</term> using the specific lineages and the Nityā goddess corresponding to that particular lunar day. **Combined with the prescribed yoga** refers to the instructions given at the end of the previous chapter. || 52 || 53 || Regarding the mention of **fifteen**, this is because the practitioner’s own self is established as the sixteenth, which is the "Science of the Sixteen-Fold Playful Lalitā" <note>original: "ṣoḍaśa-līlā-lalitā-vidyā" — The Goddess Lalitā is the 16th, encompassing the other 15 Nityās</note>. || 54 || **By the elemental selves** refers to what was taught in the third chapter. **The eight-syllabled mantra of the Self** is also of the form taught in the third chapter. According to tradition, the mantras of the elemental selves begin with two seed-syllables <term>bījas</term>, and the seven-syllable arrangement should not be used for the Self-mantra. || 55 ||

In the verse beginning with **a thousand**, the author teaches the primary and secondary options for recitation. There, the mention of **one hundred** serves as a form of penance or daily rule. The phrase **or according to the prescribed form** refers to the five... <meta>catchword: five...</meta>

# In the Tantrarāja, with the Commentary Named Manoramā
### Page 88

Then, after making an offering of flowers and worshipping with the root mantra, one should perform the fire sacrifice. This is done either in a ritual pit or upon a prepared earthen altar, after sprinkling it with water from the offering vessel using sacred grass. || 57 ||

One should draw four lines pointing east and four pointing north. After placing the fire in the middle, one should discard the portion belonging to the "flesh-eaters" <note>original: "kravyādāṃśa" — referring to spirits who consume raw flesh, here represented by a piece of charcoal</note>. || 58 ||

After sprinkling water around the fire and strewing sacred grass, one should meditate upon the "potency of the fire" <note>original: "vahni-vīryaṃ"</note>. One should then make nine offerings of clarified butter into each of the seven tongues of the fire. || 59 ||

Then, following the sequence of worship, after offering sixteen oblations with the root mantra, one should contemplate the Goddess as being dissolved into the Light situated in the central point <note>original: "binduge dhāmni" — the internal spiritual center between the eyebrows</note>. || 60 ||

Then, one should present a food offering <term>bali — a ritual gift of food to secondary deities or spirits</term> in front of the deity to the goddess Kurukullā using three mantras, by providing cooked rice, side dishes, flowers, and water in the prescribed manner. || 61 ||

---

Because the meaning of what was taught in the twentieth chapter is always present in the heart, the word "or" <note>original: "vā"</note> is used here for emphasis. What is expressed is this: through the described ritual, one should recite the mantra according to the triple count of that day or the sixty divisions of time <note>original: "ghaṭikā" — a unit of 24 minutes</note>, as if the counts were joined together. || 56 || **Then:** after the recitation. **With the root:** using the root-science <term>vidyā — the specific mantra of the deity</term>. **Worshipping:** it is understood that the deity is to be brought near into the fire. **In the ritual pit:** in the form described in the nineteenth chapter. **Or upon a prepared earthen altar:** the term "altar" <term>sthaṇḍila</term> refers to a specific type of sacred space made of sand, four-sided, measuring one hand in length and width, and one finger-breadth in height. || 57 || **In the middle:** this means in the central square among the nine squares drawn with sacred grass. Everywhere, if a mantra is not specifically mentioned, the two mantras to be used are the third section of the "Science" <note>the practitioner's primary mantra</note> and the "Eternal Science" <note>Nityā-vidyā</note> belonging to that specific day. **Discard the flesh-eater portion:** this means throwing away a piece of charcoal toward the southern direction with the mantra "Homage to the flesh-eaters" <note>original: "kravyādebhyo namaḥ"</note>. || 58 || **Sprinkling around:** the act of sprinkling water in a clockwise direction with <term>kuśa</term> or <term>darbha</term> grass. **Into the seven tongues:** into the tongues of fire named Hiranyā and others, which will be described in the nineteenth chapter. The tradition is to make the offerings while remembering each specific tongue and using the third section of the Science and the Daily Eternal mantra. In all other places, one uses the names of those specific tongues. || 59 || **With the root:** using the root mantra. The tradition is that at the end of the fire sacrifice, one should recite the mantra the same number of times as the offerings made. **In the Light in the central point:** this means between the eyebrows. || 60 || **In front:** in front of the deity. **With three mantras:** one should give the offering to Kurukullā with three mantras. **In the manner described:** in the manner taught by the Guru.

# In the Tantrarāja, with the Commentary Named Manoramā
### Page 88

#### Chapter 5 | Description of the Fivefold Worship

Having worshipped the Goddess situated in the <term>Chakra — the sacred geometric diagram of the Sri Yantra</term>, the practitioner, now himself possessing her form, should unite the host of powers <note>original: "shakti-cakra"</note> with himself using the "Space Gesture" <note>original: "kha-mudrā"</note> and the "Sky-farer Gesture" <note>original: "khecarī"</note>. || 62 ||

Then, having performed the three-fold <term>Nyāsa — the ritual "placement" of mantras on the body to divinize it</term> preceded by breath control, and having recited the pair of hymns, he should wander happily, embodying the nature of the Goddess. || 63 ||

O Goddess of gods! Hear now the special forms of daily worship, spoken in sequence. These are recommended for those who are incapable of the full, expanded ritual, or during times of emergency. || 64 ||

Otherwise, O Sovereign Goddess, if one is capable but chooses a condensed worship, it becomes harmful <note>The text warns that shortcuts taken out of laziness or arrogance, rather than genuine necessity, are spiritually counterproductive</note>. The first level consists of the center with the "weapons" <note>original: "hetibhir"</note>; the second is focused on the nine triangles <note>original: "navayoni"</note>. || 65 ||

The fourth is described as proceeding from the fourteen-angled circuit <note>original: "caturdaśāra"</note> to the center. The fifth level destroys all suffering and pain and grants all desires. || 66 ||

---

...with the gesture <note>original: "mudrayā"</note>. This is described as striking the palms together three times, then extending both index fingers with both hands in fists, one above the other; this gesture is used when showing the offered sacrificial food to the deity. || 61 ||

**He himself possessing her form:** This means possessing the same form as the Goddess, having attained her grace through the expanded ritual. **With the space-gesture:** This refers to the Great Tripura Gesture <note>original: "mahā-tripura-mudrā"</note> mentioned previously, which is visualized as the three sections of the sacred mantra located at the base of the spine <note>original: "mūlādhāra"</note>, the heart, and the crown of the head. **Host of powers:** The group of Shaktis. **With the Sky-farer:** The gesture whose construction was taught earlier, involving the contemplation of its mantra. The specific method of uniting these with one's self must be learned from the mouth of a Guru. || 62 ||

**The pair of hymns:** Those dedicated to the Master <term>Nātha — the spiritual lineage head</term> and the Goddess. **Embodying the Goddess:** Because he has completed all his duties and made himself happy through the three-fold ritual placement and other rites. || 63 ||

With the verses starting with "Worship," the text teaches the five-fold process of worship according to the variations of condensation and expansion. There, **for those incapable:** This refers to people such as royalty or those with domestic duties <note>original: "rāja-vanitā-ādīnām"</note> who may lack the time or focus for the full ritual. **In emergencies:** In times of fire, fever, or other crises. || 64 ||

**Otherwise harmful:** This refers to a practitioner who is capable of the full ritual but chooses to condense it out of their own will. It is "harmful" because it stems from an improper sense of independence from the rules. **The first is the center with the weapons:** This is the most condensed form, involving worship of the four central deities with the four "weapons" <note>the bow, arrows, noose, and goad of the Goddess</note>. **The second is in the nine triangles:** This means the worship proceeds from the nine triangles to the center. || 65 ||

**From the fourteen-angled circuit to the center:** This means the third <insert>and fourth</insert> levels of worship begin from the circuit of fourteen triangles and move inward.

# In the Tantrarāja, with the Commentary Named Manoramā
### Page 100

->O Goddess of gods! Hear now the procedure for that fifth level in the worship of Kurukullā.<-
->Thus, the five levels of worship have been proclaimed, granting the accomplishment of all goals. || 67 ||<-
->The practice of the Mantra, its success, the vows for it, and what must be avoided;<-
->The signs of its favor, and the obstacles arising from past tendencies; || 68 ||<-
->Hear these in order, O Sovereign Goddess, for they always bring joy.<-
->By these, even a mortal becomes an accomplished soul, liberated while alive and becoming one with Me. || 69 ||<-
->Bathed in fragrant waters, assuming the form described previously for worship,<-
->And having satisfied the Teacher with wealth, one should follow the ritual sequence in a sanctuary of gems. || 70 ||<-
->At each of the three daily junctions, one should repeat the mantra a thousand times in silence.<-
->One should offer milk-porridge mixed with plantain, jaggery, and sugar. || 71 ||<-

---

Regarding the phrase **possessing the form described**: this refers to the fourth type of worship, which proceeds from the outer square toward the center. The **fifth** refers to the final level of worship. || 66 || **The procedure for that**: the process for this fifth level of ritual service will be explained in the twenty-second chapter concerning Kurukullā <note>Kurukullā is a goddess in the Tantric tradition often associated with enchantment and the power of attraction; here she represents a specific, advanced stage of the ritual</note>. "Hear it there" is the intended meaning. || 67 ||

With the two verses beginning with **The practice of the Mantra** and ending with **becoming one with Me**, the author introduces six subjects <note>The manuscript version 'Vaṃ' reads: "the six questions of meaning"</note> and the fruit of their success. In this context:
*   **The practice of the Mantra** <note>original: "vidyāyāḥ sādhanam"</note> refers to the <term>Purashcaraṇa — the preparatory ritual involving a massive number of mantra repetitions to "awaken" the power of the prayer</term>.
*   **Success** refers to the completion and mastery of that preparatory ritual.
*   **The vows** are the specific disciplines observed during the preparatory ritual.
*   **What must be avoided** applies both during the time of practice and at all times.
*   **The signs of its favor** are the omens indicating the Mantra is becoming effective.
*   **Obstacles** are the hindrances to that success.
*   **Arising from past tendencies** <note>original: "prāktanād yataḥ"</note> refers to the influence of bad habits and attachments from previous lives. || 68 ||

Regarding the phrase **those which bring joy**: this means that the contemplation of one's own Self—which is the ultimate fruit—manifests through these practices. Hear those. **By which... becoming one with Me** means the practitioner attains the same divine form as the Goddess. || 69 ||

With the seven half-verses beginning with **Bathed**, the author teaches the method of practicing the Mantra and the success of its preparation. Here, **possessing the form previously described for worship** means assuming the divine body described in the <term>Nityā-pūjā — the regular daily worship</term>. **Having satisfied** means pleasing the Teacher <note>original: "Guru"</note> with wealth and other gifts; one should only proceed once instructed by a satisfied Teacher. **The sequence** refers to the daily ritual order. || 70 ||

**A thousand** means a thousand repetitions at every junction <note>The three "junctions" or Sandhyās occur at dawn, noon, and sunset</note> of the day. **Plantain** <note>original: "mocā"</note> refers to the fruit of the banana tree. **Sugar** <note>original: "sitā"</note> refers to refined sugar. **One should offer** means presenting these as an oblation at every junction. || 71 ||

# [ Chapter 5 ] Instruction on Mantra-Accomplishment, the Preparatory Rite, and so on. | 101

->One should also perform the **waving of lights** <note>original: nīrājana; a ritual of lustration or waving lamps</note> with camphor during those same junctions.<-
->One should perform the **fire sacrifice** <note>original: homa</note> at one-tenth the count of the mantra repetition, and the **libation** <note>original: tarpaṇa</note> with water mixed with camphor. || 72 ||<-
->Beyond the daily obligatory rituals, one should chant **two thousand** times every day.<-
->By this, O Goddess, the **one hundred thousand** <note>original: lakṣa</note> repetitions will be completed by the end of the period. || 73 ||<-
->Thus, three hundred thousand repetitions are prescribed for the first age, the **Krita Yuga**.<-
->In the **Treta** age, it is double that; in **Dvapara**, it is remembered as triple. || 74 ||<-
->In the **Kali** age <note>the current age of spiritual decline</note>, it is said to be four times the count of the letters.<-
->The "third-seven" number is that by which it becomes **twenty-one**. || 75 ||<-

---

**"One-tenth"** refers to the total number of mantra repetitions. **"With water mixed with camphor"** <note>original: indu-maj-jalaiḥ; literally 'water in which the moon (camphor) is immersed'</note> refers to water scented with camphor for the libation. The word "and" in the verse implies that the one-tenth rule also applies to this libation. || 72 ||

**"Beyond the daily rituals"** means that these repetitions are distinct and separate from the count performed during the three daily junctions (dawn, noon, and sunset) which comprise the sixty *ghatikas* <note>a unit of time equaling 24 minutes</note> of a standard day. By saying **"the one hundred thousand is completed,"** it means the practitioner should chant 2,134 repetitions daily in addition to the base two thousand <note>this adjustment ensures the 100,000 goal is reached within a standard lunar month</note>.

The essence of the instruction is as follows: The person who desires to perform the **preparatory rite** <note>term: Purashcaraṇa; a multi-step ritual process intended to "awaken" the power of a mantra</note> should first satisfy their **Guru** <note>spiritual teacher</note> with wealth according to their capacity. Having received the Guru's permission, the practitioner stays in a red-colored worship pavilion, avoids all improper or idle chatter, eats a regulated diet, abstains from sexual contact, and maintains a mind free from distraction. 

Bathed in fragrant waters, wearing fine red garments, and adorned with red ointments, garlands, and ornaments, the practitioner follows the sequence of daily rites. After the daily obligatory rituals, one performs the **sequential worship** <note>original: krama-pūjā</note> as previously described. In each of the three junctions, one should perform 1,112 repetitions of the mantra. Then, one performs the libation at one-tenth of that count. Following this, a fire sacrifice is performed—also at one-tenth the count—using **"Three Sweets"** <note>a mixture of honey, ghee, and sugar</note> with Palasha flowers, safflower blossoms, or white water-lilies. Finally, one should perform worship with an equal number of fragrant red flowers and complete the chanting until the full count of one hundred thousand is reached. This applies to all cases. || 73 ||

Regarding the **"three hundred thousand"**: This means that for all **Pinda**, **Kartari**, and **Bija** mantras <note>these are technical classifications of mantras based on whether they consist of a single syllable, a "scissors" structure, or a primary seed-syllable</note>, one should chant one hundred thousand for each unique (non-repeated) letter in the **Krita Yuga**. In the Treta, Dvapara, and Kali ages, the count is increased by halves, being double, triple, and quadruple respectively, as stated before. For mantras ranging from one to nine letters in length (known as Pinda, Kartari, and Bija), the repetition is based on the count of unique letters multiplied by the requirements of the specific Age. For mantras from ten to twenty letters, the repetition is similarly a "lakh" (100,000) per letter according to the Age. For mantras from twenty-one to one hundred letters...

# [ Chapter 5 ] Instruction on Mantra-Accomplishment, the Preparatory Rite, and so on. | 102

->By that same logic, in the other world-ages, the number is said to be eight-fold,<-
->provided that no obstacle arises from the pleasures or distractions caused by women. || 76 ||<-
->When those numbers are completed, one should pray and then return to one’s own regular routine.<-
->Hear now, O Goddess of Devas, the things to be avoided during those ritual days, and always. || 77 ||<-
->Conversations with atheists <note>original: nāstikaiḥ; those who deny the authority of the Vedas</note>, sexual intercourse, and censuring others;<-
->Excessive sleep and grief, as well as idle chatter and wandering to foreign lands. || 78 ||<-
->These are the things to be avoided on those ritual days, O Daughter of Shankara!<-
->Now hear what is destructive for everyone, everywhere, and at all times: || 79 ||<-
->Coveting the gems, houses, or wives of others, and the slandering of the same;<-
->One should never direct anger or physical violence toward women, even if they are wicked. || 80 ||<-

The rule is simply **one hundred thousand** <note>original: lakṣa</note> repetitions. Beyond that, for mantras with a specific number of letters, the repetition is **ten thousand**. This is the rule stated in the *Mantra-tantra-prakāśikā* <note>a liturgical manual on mantras and rituals</note>. This standard should be accepted throughout this entire Tantra whenever a specific number for the **preparatory rite** <note>original: purashcaraṇa</note> is not mentioned. || 74 || 

The **"third-seven"** number refers to the fact that in the third section of the **Vidyā** <note>original: vidyā; here referring to the specific female deity's mantra</note>, there are seven non-repeating letters. The "remainder" implies **twenty-one hundred thousand** (2.1 million). This means that in the first age, the **Krita Yuga**, the total count for the chanting is twenty-one lakhs. || 75 || 

**"By that"** means in that specific sequence. **"In other ages"** refers to the **Treta** age and those following it. **"Pleasures caused by the agitation of women"** refers to the enjoyment permitted by young women; the meaning is that the prescribed number for the ritual chanting should be free from any obstacles arising from such worldly pleasures. || 76 || 

**"Completion"** refers to the successful attainment of the goal. **"One's own routine"** refers to the daily obligatory practices already prescribed. 

With the second half of the verse beginning with **"the things to be avoided,"** the author introduces the prohibitions for those devoted to the Vidyā. In that context, **"on those days"** refers specifically to the days of the preparatory rite, while **"always"** refers to all times. || 77 ||

Through the three verses beginning with **"atheists"** and ending with **"should not direct,"** the text instructs on what must be avoided both during the preparatory rite and in general life. || 78 || 

**"On those days"** refers to the days of the preparatory rite and similar observances. **"Other things"** refer to those that are to be avoided at all times. || 79 || 

**"Slandering them"** refers to the act of censuring others. **"Even if they are wicked"** means even if the women are disobedient or ill-behaved. || 80 ||

With the three verses beginning with **"The reprehensible things"** (84) and ending with **"constantly"** (86), the Lord instructs on the signs that indicate obstacles to the Deity’s favor, arising from an abundance of past sins. # [ Chapter 5 ] Instruction on the Position of the Tortoise | 104

->**Main Text**<-

Without knowing the position of the Tortoise <note>original: kūrma-sthiti</note>, he who proceeds with the rules of planning and construction <note>original: yojanādi-vidhi</note> does not attain the stated fruits; instead, he meets with destruction. || 88 ||

Therefore, one should perform all actions only after knowing the divisions of the Tortoise. That Tortoise is fourfold in this world; hear its types, O Beloved! <note>Addressing the Goddess</note> || 89 ||

The first is the Supreme Tortoise <note>original: para-kūrma; the cosmic tortoise supporting the earth</note>; then that which pertains to the Country <note>deśa</note>; and that which resides in the Village, the Cattle-pen, or the House. These are the four ways it is situated. || 90 ||

One should then divide the country, village, or house—the building site <note>vāstu</note>—into nine parts. From the East to the West, one should place the letters from *Ka* to *Ma*. || 91 ||

One should place four identical letters in the two supreme positions. Between the Northeast <note>Īśāne</note> and the Center, one should place the vowels starting from the East. || 92 ||

***

->**The Manorama Commentary**<-

[The Guru] indicates [the results]. **For a long time through many births.** Regarding the phrase "attainment of the lineage tradition" <note>original: sampradāya-siddhi</note>, the following is an expert’s explanation of the meaning and maintenance of the word *Sampradāya*:

> "Correctness is called *Sama*; the excellence of love comes from what is given <note>dāyataḥ</note>. Through this, the highest knowledge is born; that is the very life-breath of the **Lineage Tradition** <note>sampradāya</note>."

The meaning is this: the knowledge obtained from a true Guru through a lineage, which brings about the attainment of one’s desired goals, is what constitutes a "Good Lineage Tradition." || 87 ||

With the eleven verses starting with **Without the Tortoise** and ending with "always," the author teaches the division of the Tortoise's position—which is common to all Tantras—the fruit of knowing it, and the transgression of ignoring it. **The stated fruits** refers to the worship of deities and so on as previously described. **Otherwise**—means not only the failure to obtain the stated results, but the failure in all actions such as the construction of houses, ritual circles <note>maṇḍala</note>, villages, towns, cities, or trading posts. || 88 ||

**That** refers to the Tortoise. **Its types** refers to the modes of the Tortoise's position. || 89 ||

**The Supreme Tortoise** is the stable Tortoise that supports the Earth, which is fifty million *yojanas* <note>a traditional unit of distance, roughly 8-9 miles</note> in extent. **Then the second**—as mentioned. **Its situation**—the arrangement of the Tortoise. || 90 ||

Regarding the instruction **Divide into nine**, the meaning is as follows: By drawing four lines at equal intervals running East-to-West and South-to-North, nine cells <note>koṣṭha</note> are formed. Starting from the cell in the Eastern row and ending in the middle cell of the Western row, in those five cells, one should write the letters of the alphabet in groups of five, from *Ka* to *Ma*, in clockwise order. Following that, the four letters from *Ya* to *Ha* are placed in the cells pertaining to the Northwest and North. (1)

***

<margin>(1) The text reads "extending through the directions" in the Vamsha manuscript, and "the restraint of the directions" in the So. manuscript.</margin>

# [ Chapter 5 ] Description of the Form of the Tortoise | 105

->**Main Text**<-

Starting from the Northeast <note>original: īśānte</note>, including the intermediate directions, the square where the first letter of the name <note>the name of the person, house, or village</note> falls is considered the **Mouth**. On its two sides are the **Hands**; then follow the **Feet** in the belly/flanks. || 63 ||

There is one **Tail** in the following position, and the **Back** is in the center; thus, it is composed of six limbs <note>original: ṣaḍaṅga</note>. Success in all aims <note>original: sarvārtha-siddhi</note> is achieved in the mouth, while the hands grant only little success. || 64 ||

The belly/flanks always bring fruitlessness, and the feet cause all manner of sorrow. Death is certain in the tail, but the back grants all possible goals. || 65 ||

Therefore, knowing this well, one should perform all that has been enjoined. Consonants <note>original: vyañjana</note> are used for the Country Tortoise, and vowels <note>original: svara</note> for the House Tortoise. || 66 ||

Both [vowels and consonants] are used for the Village Tortoise and its kind, but for the Supreme Tortoise, those three <note>vowels, consonants, or their combination</note> are not used. Because the Supreme Tortoise always faces East, success is proclaimed through it. || 67 ||

***

->**The Manorama Commentary**<-

After writing in the [other] squares, one should write the remaining two letters, *La* and *Kṣa*, in the Northeast square. In the very central square, in the eight directions starting from the East and ending in the Northeast, one should write the sixteen vowels—starting with *A* and ending with the *Visarga* <note>the 'ḥ' sound</note>—in pairs of two, moving clockwise <note>original: prādakṣiṇyena</note>. 

When this is done, whichever square in the aforementioned diagram contains the first letter of the name of the house or other entity, that square is to be known as the **Mouth** of that Tortoise. The two squares situated on either side of that square are its pair of **Hands**. The two squares following those are its **Belly** <note>original: jaṭhara; or stomach</note>. || 63 || 

The square following those is its **Tail**. The ninth square, which is in the very center and contains the vowel letters, is its **Back**. Thus, the form of the Tortoise is composed of six limbs: mouth, hands, belly, feet, tail, and back. In every case, the visualization of the Tortoise’s mouth and other limbs begins from the square containing the first letter of the name. || 64 ||

**Grants all aims**—the word "worship" <note>bhajana</note> is implied here as the remainder of the thought. || 65 || 

**All that is enjoined**—the phrase "the application of worship" is implied here. **Consonants** refers to those found in the letters of the name. **Vowels** refers to those found in the first letter of the name. || 66 || 

**Both** means both the vowel letters and the consonant letters. The meaning is as follows: in the stated diagram, whichever square contains the consonant of the first letter of the name for a **Country Tortoise**, that is its mouth. Whichever square contains the vowel of the first letter of the name for a **House Tortoise**, that is its

### Manoramā Commentary on the Tantrarāja

# [ Chapter 5 ] The Results of the Tortoise Mapping | 106

->**Main Text**<-

Thus, this fourfold division of the Tortoise has been described to you. By using this, success <note>original: siddhi</note> shall be attained by all mantra-practitioners in all places. || 98 ||

By multiplying the length and the width <gloss>(1) Variant reading: the sum of the length and width</gloss> and dividing that sum by eight, one determines the group <term>Varga<gloss>the eight categories of the Sanskrit alphabet</gloss></term> from the remainder. One should assign the first letter of that group <gloss>(2)</gloss> to the name of the site. || 99 ||

In ritual sites where the form is unknown <gloss>(3)</gloss>, the site becomes known through the name. In their respective positions [on the Tortoise's body], misfortune and emptiness <gloss>(4)</gloss> are fixed. || 100 ||

The pervasiveness consisting of the Space-element <note>original: vyomatattva</note> has been correctly described. By maintaining this in the mind, that principle <note>tattva</note> is assimilated into one's own self. || 101 ||

***

->**The Manorama Commentary**<-

**The Mouth:** For villages and similar sites, where the vowel and consonant of the first letter of the name of the Tortoise are seen together in a square, that is its **Mouth**. One should perform the prescribed actions in the limbs corresponding to those two. If the two letters fall in limbs that are mutually compatible, one may choose either limb as desired. 

In the case of the **Country Tortoise**, if the first letter of the name is only a vowel, one should designate the first square of the directional matrix <note>the Mātṛkā grid</note> as its mouth. It faces East—this refers to the **Supreme Tortoise**. By this—because of its fixed position—the success mentioned is achieved, as it depends on the arrangement of the Tortoise's limbs. || 97–98 ||

With the two verses beginning with "By multiplying" and ending with "emptiness," the author teaches the method for assigning names to specific types of sites <note>Vāstu</note> or planets whose names are unknown. In this context: **By the length** means the measurement of its long side. **By eight** means the number eight. **From the remainder** means the remainder left after the calculation. **Group** <note>Varga</note> refers to one of the eight groups of letters. **One letter** among the letters of that group is the **initial letter** of the name. || 99 ||

**Where the form is unknown** means in cases of unknown names. This is what is being said: for a ritual site of unknown name or one conceived in one's own mind, one should multiply the length by the width. Divide that number by eight. From the remaining number, identify which group among the *A-Ka-Ca-Ṭa-Ta-Pa-Ya-Śa* <note>these are the eight groups of the Sanskrit alphabet: vowels, velars, palatals, retroflexes, dentals, labials, semivowels, and sibilants</note> it belongs to. Then, one should create a name starting with one of the letters in that group. 

**Known through the name** <gloss>5)</gloss> implies this applies to sites with known names as well. One should then map the limbs of the Tortoise—the feet, tail, and belly/flanks. **Emptiness** means fruitlessness. || 100 ||

***

<margin>(2) Variant: "one should assign the first [letter] of those to the name" in some manuscripts.</margin>
<margin>(3) Variant: "of unknown form" in the root text.</margin>
<margin>(4) Variant: "it is thought" in some manuscripts.</margin>
<margin>(5) Variant: "known names" in the commentary manuscript.</margin>

## Thus ends the fifth chapter, fully examined, in the Tradition of the Kadi School <gloss>(1)</gloss> within the Tantras of the Sixteen Nityas.

***

Thus, in the auspicious **Tantras of the Sixteen Nityas** <note>The Sixteen Nityas are goddesses representing the phases of the moon in the Shri Vidya tradition</note>, in the commentary called **Manoramā** (The Delight of the Mind)—composed by **Subhagānandanātha**, also known by the title *The Light of the Lion-King of the Essence of the Universe*—this fifth chapter, which focuses on elucidating the sequence of worship for the Nitya goddess **Lalitā** and others, is now fully completed and examined.

# Now Begins the Sixth Chapter

->**The Root Text**<-

Now, O Beautiful One <note>original: "Sundari," an epithet for the Goddess</note>, I shall describe the occasional and desire-based rituals for those souls who are devoted to the daily worship of the sixteen Nityās <note>The Nityās are sixteen goddesses representing the lunar days or Tithis</note>. Listen! || 1 ||

The daily <term>Nitya<gloss>obligatory daily rituals</gloss></term>, the occasional <term>Naimittika<gloss>rituals performed on specific dates or events</gloss></term>, and the desire-based <term>Kāmya<gloss>optional rituals performed to achieve a specific goal</gloss></term> rites are each dependent on the one preceding it. If one seeks to worship otherwise <gloss>(1)</gloss>, they will bring about a succession of calamities. || 2 ||

Occasional worship should be performed by the perfected ones who are already devoted to daily worship. I will now describe the method for that, beginning from the month of *Phālguna* <note>late February to March</note> and continuing through the year. || 3 ||

In the month of *Caitra* <note>March to April</note>, one should perform the ritual using the *Damana* <term>Damanaka<gloss>Artemisia indica, a fragrant plant sacred to Shiva and Shakti</gloss></term> plant, either including the roots or using branches. On the night of the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, one should establish the plant using the sacred mantra <term>Vidyā<gloss>literally "knowledge," referring here to the specific mantra of the goddess</gloss></term>. || 4 ||

***

### The Manoramā Commentary

In the previous chapter, the author taught the rules for the daily worship of the goddess Lalitā. Now, in this sixth chapter—consisting of one hundred verses—he teaches the sequence for occasional and desire-based worship for those devoted to all the Nityā goddesses. 

Through the first twenty-two verses, starting with "Now, the sixteen Nityās...", he explains the sequence of occasional worship. In the first two verses, he outlines the scope of the chapter and warns of the spiritual obstacles <note>original: "pratyavāya," meaning a sin of omission or karmic backslide</note> that arise if one performs these rituals in the wrong order.

Regarding the phrase **"The occasional and the desire-based"**: the word "worship" is implied. 

**"Dependent on those preceding them"**: This means that only those who are constant in daily worship are qualified to perform occasional rites. Similarly, only those devoted to both daily and occasional worship are qualified for the desire-based rituals. 

**"Otherwise"**: This refers to performing the worship by reversing or ignoring this established order. This rule applies to everyone. || 1-2 ||

With the verse beginning **"Daily worship..."**, the author introduces the specific rules and qualities required for all occasional rites. || 3 ||

With the verse beginning **"In Caitra..."**, the author teaches the sequence for the *Damana* flower ritual. 
**"With roots"**: referring to the *Damana* plants. 
**"With clusters"**: meaning the branches. This is considered the secondary or "lesser" option. 
**"Establish it with the Vidyā"**: This means that in all occasional rites, one should take the specified ritual materials on the night before the rite, place them in a pure vessel, and sprinkle them while reciting the *Vidyā* <note>the mantra</note>. One should then honor them with scent, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings—

<margin>(1) A variant reading in the 'Bhu' manuscript reads: "seeking to become a vessel" <note>original: bhājanaṁ caicchan</note>.</margin>

<summary>This page introduces Chapter 6 of the Tantrarāja Tantra, establishing that Occasional (Naimittika) and Desire-based (Kāmya) rituals can only be performed by those who have mastered Daily (Nitya) worship. It begins describing the specific seasonal rite of offering Damanaka plants in the month of Caitra.</summary>

### Chapter 64: On the Worship for Each Month | 109

->**The Root Text**<-

On the following day, at the conclusion of the daily worship, one should perform the ritual with these [items]. In this same month, on the Full Moon day, the Spring Festival worship <term>Vasantotsava<gloss>A celebration of spring, often involving flowers and fragrances</gloss></term> should be conducted. || 5 ||

One should perform a brilliant worship as described before, using flowers that bloom in that season, camphor <note>original: "Candra," literally 'moon,' a common poetic name for camphor</note>, sandalwood, fragrant scents, and saffron <note>original: "Kāśmīra," referring to the region famous for saffron</note>. || 6 ||

In the month of *Vaiśākha* <note>April–May</note>, on the Full Moon, one should worship with golden lotuses <margin>1. Variant: "Snow-lotuses" (Hima-puṣkara)</margin>. Alternatively, one may use camphor, musk, and sandalwood mixed with cool water. || 7 ||

In the month of *Jyeṣṭha* <note>May–June</note>, on the Full Moon, one should worship the Goddess with the fruits of the plantain, jackfruit, and mango, following the previous rules to attain all spiritual success. || 8 ||

In the month of *Āṣāḍha* <note>June–July</note>, on the Full Moon, one should worship the Auspicious Lady <note>Shiva, the feminine form of the Auspicious One</note> using sandalwood mixed with saffron, cardamom, cubeb <margin>2. Variant: "Ela-kakkola"</margin>, and jasmine. || 9 ||

In the month of *Śrāvaṇa* <note>July–August</note>, on the Full Moon, one should worship the Goddess with the Sacred Threads <term>Pavitra<gloss>Specially woven threads offered to the deity to atone for omissions in ritual</gloss></term>. O Auspicious One! Listen now to this method, which bestows good fortune. || 10 ||

***

### The Manoramā Commentary

After having worshiped with the five offerings <note>perfume, flowers, incense, lamp, and food</note> and placing the items in a suitable spot within the worship area... || 4 ||

**On the following day:** After the completion of the sequence of one's own daily worship, one should perform a special worship with those [items] and also perform a worship of the Guru according to one's financial capacity. || 5 ||

With the verse beginning **"In this [month]"** and ending with **"brilliant,"** the author teaches the Spring Festival worship. **In this month** refers to the month of *Caitra*. Using sandalwood, camphor, and fragrant substances with full garlands and saffron—**as before** indicates that this is preceded by the preliminary consecration <term>Adhivāsa<gloss>A preparatory rite where the deity is invited into the ritual items the night before</gloss></term>. || 6 ||

With the verse beginning **"In Vaiśākha,"** the author teaches the worship for that month. There, **golden lotuses** are used; the variant **"snow-lotuses"** implies flowers in cool water. This is an alternative for **those who are unable** <note>original: "ashakta," referring to practitioners who cannot source the primary rare materials</note> to find the golden lotuses. **Camphor, musk, and sandalwood** should be understood as being used to scent the water. Here too, the rite must be preceded by the preliminary consecration. || 7 ||

With the verse beginning **"In Jyeshtha,"** the worship for the month of *Jyeṣṭha* is taught. In each case, **as before** means including the preliminary consecration. || 7 <note>Note: The manuscript numbering repeats 7 here</note> ||

With the verse beginning **"In Āṣāḍha,"** the worship for *Āṣāḍha* is taught. Here too, one should worship after the preliminary consecration. || 8 ||

With the ten verses beginning with **"In Śrāvaṇa"** and ending with **"is destroyed,"** the ritual of offering the Sacred Threads <margin>3. Variant: "Pavitrārohaṇa" (The Ascent of the Sacred Threads)</margin> in the month of *Śrāvaṇa* is described.

->[The sacred threads should be made] of gold or silver, or of threads produced from silk,<-
->or those made of cotton, dyed red, auspicious, and multiplied ninefold. || 11 ||<-

->One should make the sacred thread <term>Pavitra<gloss>A ritual cord or garland offered to a deity to rectify any defects in the year's worship</gloss></term> for all the Powers <term>Śaktis<gloss>Feminine personifications of divine energy</gloss></term> sixteen finger-breadths <note>original: "ṣoḍaśāṅgula"; an aṅgula is a traditional unit of measure roughly equal to the width of a finger</note> [in length],<-
->or nine finger-breadths long, joined with an equal number <margin>1. Variant: "joined with an equal number of strands and knots, etc."</margin> of strands and knots. || 12 ||<-

->Alternatively, for the Powers belonging to the enclosures <note>original: "vṛtti-śaktīnām"; referring to the deities stationed in the concentric circles of a mandala</note>, [the length should] extend to their specific number of finger-breadths.<-

[The commentary] explains the sequence of the festival worship. In that context—with the "sacred threads" <note>pavitraiḥ</note> to be described hereafter, which are the very essence of the cosmic principles. The procedure for that—

**The Procedure for the Sacred Thread.** || 10 || "Or" indicates another option. "Red"—dyed with saffron, sandalwood, and other such substances. || 11 || "Nine finger-breadths"—this connects to the word "threads." "Or" indicates another option; "joined with an equal number of strands and knots, etc." <margin>3. Variant: "joined with an equal number of strands and knots, etc."</margin> In the option where the length is sixteen finger-breadths, one should make it with sixteen strands and sixteen knots. In the option where the length is nine finger-breadths, one should make it with nine strands and nine knots. Here, the word "etc." refers to the matter of dyeing; the meaning is that one should perform the dyeing at every knot. || 12 || "Alternatively" indicates a further option. "Up to the measure of their specific number in finger-breadths"—here the word "etc." refers to the strands and knots.

What is being said is this: for whichever enclosure there is a specific number of Powers, one should make a sacred thread with that many finger-breadths in length and that many strands and knots—this is one option. In this option, [the sacred thread] for the eight [Mothers] would be eight finger-breadths long with eight strands and knots; for the nine Masters <note>Nāthas</note>, nine finger-breadths long with nine strands and knots; for the three deities like Kāmeśvarī, three finger-breadths long with three strands and knots. For the primary deity standing in the center, because she consists of the sixteen Eternities <term>Nityās<gloss>The fifteen moon-phase deities plus the Tripurasundarī Herself</gloss></term>, one should make a thread with sixteen strands and knots. For the other fifteen Eternities who are parts of Lalitā's body, one should make a thread fifteen finger-breadths long with fifteen strands and knots. "Having made"—this connects to the text below. "Following the preliminary consecration"—as described previously. "With them"—meaning with the sacred threads. || 13 || "Of that measure"—in the three options <margin>4. Variant: "in the three options"</margin> described for the various parts, that is the length; it should be understood as being joined with one hundred and eight strands and knots. || 14 || "For Powers such as Vārāhī and Kurukullā"—the word "etc." refers to the fifteen Eternities. "Like the Root Power"—meaning like the primary Goddess...

->One should make the <term>Pavitra<gloss>A ritual sacred thread offered to a deity to atone for omissions in worship</gloss></term> according to one's own measure, following the stated number.<-

---

**Commentary:**
...regarding the previously mentioned fivefold set, that which is accepted as fivefold is similar. For the limbs of the <term>Nityās<gloss>The fifteen eternal goddesses representing the days of the waxing moon</gloss></term>, the measure is fourteen or five [finger-breadths], and for the Goddess stationed in the center, it is fifteen or five. || 15 ||

**By one's own measure**—this means from the shoulder down to the navel. **Tradition** refers to the sequence of the letters of the alphabet. **Agama** (Scripture) refers to the <term>Kādi-mata<gloss>A specific lineage of Tantric teaching beginning with the letter 'Ka'</gloss></term> and others. || 16 ||

**By the measure of the garment**—this refers to the measurement used for the Power-Yoginis. || 17 ||

The section beginning with **"along with the strands and knots"** describes the fivefold method for those who are unable to perform the previously mentioned fivefold ritual. || 18 ||

**Confusion of measurements** refers to the mutual mixing of the five different systems of measurement mentioned. || 19 ||

With the verse beginning with **"Now, in the month of Bhādrapada,"** the text instructs on the worship for the month of Bhadrapada. In that context, **"along with the previously mentioned ritual"** means including the preliminary consecration <note>original: "adhivāsa-pūrvam"</note>. || 20 ||

With the four verses beginning with **"In the month of Āśvayuja,"** the text instructs on the sequence of worship for the month of Ashvayuja <note>this refers to the autumnal Navaratri festival</note>. In that context, **"the first day after the new moon"** refers to the first lunar day immediately following the new moon. **Offerings** means food offerings. || 21 ||

**Starting from a hundred and increasing by that amount**—this means an increase of one hundred each time. Thus, on the full moon, it becomes more than six hundred.

->Having invoked the Goddess into a young girl and worshipped her with devotion,<-
->one should offer jewelry, clothes, and other gifts, and then present the <term>Dakṣiṇā<gloss>A traditional monetary gift or honorarium given to complete a ritual</gloss></term>. || 23 ||<-

->O Beloved! One should worship in this manner, increasing [the number of girls] from one upwards until the full number is reached.<-
->By this, the wise practitioner becomes perfected, and even a King will become his servant. || 24 ||<-

->In the month of <term>Kārttika<gloss>Typically October–November</gloss></term>, on the full moon day, one should worship with saffron.<-
->At night, one should perform fire offerings and light lamps fueled with clarified butter. || 25 ||<-

->One should place sixteen lamps in sequence before the Goddess while reciting the <term>Vidyā<gloss>The specific sacred mantra of the deity</gloss></term>,<-
->and place one lamp before each of the attendant <term>Śaktis<gloss>Secondary goddesses or personified powers</gloss></term>. || 26 ||<-

->Alternatively, one may place one lamp in the center of a vessel with nine surrounding it,<-
->and offer them using the <term>Mūla-vidyā<gloss>The root or primary mantra of the tradition</gloss></term> along with flowers. || 27 ||<-

->In the month of <term>Mārgaśīrṣa<gloss>Typically November–December</gloss></term>, on the full moon day, having offered coconut water mixed with camphor <note>original: "candra-yuk", literally "joined with the moon," a poetic term for camphor</note>,<-
->one should worship according to the rules with cakes made of black gram flour. || 28 ||<-

***

The meaning is that one should perform the fire sacrifice with the root mantra. Regarding the recitation (*japa*): the meaning is that one should perform the recitation between one hundred and two hundred times. "Having worshipped" means following the sequence prescribed for daily worship. || 23 || "Increasing from one upwards": on the full moon day, one should worship sixteen <term>Kanyakās<gloss>Young girls who have not yet reached puberty, viewed as embodiments of the Goddess</gloss></term>. "By this" refers to the act of sacrifice. The point being made is this: after the remaining worship of the Goddess and the fire sacrifice, one should perform the worship of the girls. || 24 ||

With the three verses beginning with "In Kārttika" and ending with "with flowers," the author teaches the procedure for the <term>Kārttika-dīpotsava<gloss>The Festival of Lights in the month of Karttika</gloss></term>. There, one should perform the fire offering using the mantras prescribed for daily rites <margin>2. Variant: "following the daily sequence."</margin>. || 25 || "With the Vidyā" refers to the <term>Śrī Vidyā<gloss>The "Auspicious Knowledge," the central mantra of this Tantric system</gloss></term>. "Of the Śaktis" refers to the attendant powers such as <term>Vārāhī<gloss>The sow-headed goddess</gloss></term> and <term>Kurukullā<gloss>A goddess associated with enchantment</gloss></term>; the words "with their respective mantras" are implied. In this tradition, when the fifteen <term>Nityās<gloss>The fifteen eternal goddesses representing the days of the lunar fortnight</gloss></term> are worshipped separately, one should place fifteen lamps using their respective mantras. Regarding Vārāhī and Kurukullā, the procedure is the same as for the main Goddess. || 26 || "Alternatively" introduces another option; this is the secondary or less preferred method. || 27 ||

With the verse beginning "In Mārgaśīrṣa," the author teaches the worship for the month of Mārgaśīrṣa. Here, "joined with the moon" means mixed with camphor. The meaning is that after offering coconut water as the <term>Arghya<gloss>A traditional water offering of honor</gloss></term>, one should worship with cakes made of black gram flour. "According to the rules" means preceded by the <term>Adhivāsa<gloss>A preliminary rite of consecration or "perfuming" the offerings</gloss></term>. || 28 ||

# Chapter 64 | Description of Worship according to the Months

In the month of <term>Pauṣa<gloss>Typically December–January</gloss></term>, on the full moon day, one should worship with sugars or jaggery. To achieve the perfection of one's desires, one should offer cow’s milk. || 29 ||

In the month of <term>Māgha<gloss>Typically January–February</gloss></term>, on the full moon day, one should always worship with white and other [black] sesame seeds, along with offerings of milk, white sugar-cakes, and similar items. || 30 ||

In the month of <term>Phālguna<gloss>Typically February–March</gloss></term>, on the full moon day, one should worship with lotuses made of gold and silver, and with mango blossoms and fragrant <term>Madhuka<gloss>The Mahua tree, prized for its sweet, fermentable flowers</gloss></term> flowers to attain what is desired. || 31 ||

On the equinoxes, solstices, and <term>Darśa<gloss>The New Moon</gloss></term> days, as well as on the <term>Yugādi<gloss>The anniversary days marking the start of the four cosmic ages</gloss></term> days, one should perform special worship. This should also be done on the holy days prescribed in the <term>Āgamas<gloss>The sacred tantric scriptures</gloss></term>. || 32 ||

For those self-controlled practitioners who are constantly devoted to the daily and occasional rites, the "Optional Rituals" <note>original: "kāmya-rūpāṇi," rituals intended to bring a specific result or fulfill a wish</note> are now described through various forms of worship. || 33 ||

These optional rituals are said to be performed through the use of <term>Yantras<gloss>Sacred geometric diagrams used as a focus for power</gloss></term>, fire-offerings, meditative actions, contemplation, Yoga, libations, and ritual worship. In specific applications, one should worship according to the variations. || 34 ||

***

With the verse beginning "In the month of Pauṣa," the text instructs on the worship for that month—either on that day or on another specified lunar phase.
**Cow’s [milk]**—pertaining to the cow. The use of the word "cow" is to exclude the milk of goats, buffaloes, and other animals. || 29 ||

With the verse beginning "In the month of Māgha," the text instructs on the worship for that month. There—**with white**—means those that are pure white.
**With others**—means black sesame seeds. The word **"and"** implies another option. **Sita**—means sugar. The word **"and so on"** refers to fruits and other offerings. **Always**—meaning during the worship performed on all days of that period. || 30 ||

With the verse beginning "In the month of Phālguna," the text instructs on the worship for that month. There, **of gold and silver**—refers to flowers <note>The commentator clarifies that the gold and silver items offered should be in the shape of flowers</note>. || 31 ||

With the verse beginning "Equinoxes," the text instructs on special types of worship on holy days. There, **on the Yugādi days**—refers to the specific lunar dates mentioned in months like <term>Vaiśākha<gloss>April–May</gloss></term> which are known as the starts of the Yugas. **Special**—refers to the specific worship, the daily worship, and the occasional worship. **In the Āgamas**—refers to days such as the birthday of one's Guru. || 32 ||

Following this, with the next sixty-eight verses beginning with "Daily," the text instructs on the rules for Optional Worship. There, with the two verses ending with "from worship," the text explains that those who are fit to perform these optional rituals can attain their desires through worship alone. There—**of the self-controlled**—means those who possess discrimination. **Optional forms**—meaning the desired goals that are to be sought. **Through worship**—through variations such as Yantras, fire-offerings, and so on. **Action**—refers to [rituals such as] placing needles into dolls...
