## [ Chapter 13 continued ]

### Results of Offerings and the Design of Sacred Diagrams

> By offering goat-meat and fats, one obtains land rich with crops from the surrounding region. By offering lotuses for three days, one attains the favor of Lakshmi <note>The goddess of wealth and good fortune</note>. || 30 ||
> 
> Now I shall describe the Yantras <term>Yantra: A geometric diagram used in meditation and ritual to center power or represent a deity</term> which grant various desired fruits. Listen to their specific methods with an attentive mind, O Shive <note>A संबोधन/address to the Goddess as the auspicious one</note>! || 31 ||
> 
> There are ten letters belonging to the Dūtī-Nityās <note>The "Messenger Eternals," a group of goddesses in this specific tantric lineage</note> which are without beginning or end. When combined with the sixteen vowels, they are said to number one hundred and sixty. || 32 ||
> 
> Having drawn two squares, and within them a pair of circles; within those an octagon, and within that another pair of circles— || 33 ||
> 
> Having done this, one should write the primary Mantra <term>Vidyā: The specific sacred sound-form of the goddess</term> in the center along with the name [of the person for whom the ritual is performed]. In the spaces between the circles and in the eight outer corners— || 34 ||
> 
> —one should write two letters in each. In the space between the two outermost circles, one writes the elemental seed-syllables <note>original: "bhūtāṇān" (syllables representing Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Space)</note> appropriate to the specific ritual task. Within the outer square— || 35 ||
> 
> —one should write the alphabet <term>Mātṛkā: The "Little Mothers," referring to the letters of the Sanskrit alphabet which are considered the source of all manifestation</term> in the cardinal directions, twelve letters at a time in sequence. The final four letters are to be written in the four corners. || 36 ||

---

...or in the other fortnight <note>Refers to the two halves of the lunar month</note>. || 28 || "Three times seven nights" means twenty-one days. The term *kṣaurātaiḥ* is connected to "goat-meat." A goat or a ram is intended here. || 29 || 30 ||

Regarding the section beginning "Now the Yantras," the text teaches the construction of ten Yantras through these seven verses. The meaning is as follows:

Having produced two circles using a compass of the desired size, one should construct an octagon outside them as previously described. Using the corners of that octagon as a guide, one should draw two more circles. Outside of those, one should construct two squares with a two-finger-width <note>original: "dvyaṅgula"</note> interval between the inner and outer boundaries. 

In the very center of everything, one writes the "Heart-Syllable" <term>Hṛllekhā: The seed-syllable HRĪṂ, central to many Tantric traditions</term> of the Mantra along with the letters of the name. The remaining six letters of the modified Mantra <note>original: "vidyā-śeṣa"</note> are written in the path between the inner circles. 

Of the letters modified by vowels, which number one hundred and sixty, the first sixteen letters are written in the eight outer corners, starting from the tip of each corner and moving clockwise <note>original: "prādakṣiṇyena"</note>, writing two letters in each. In the path between the outer circles, the elemental seed-syllables should be written according to the specific ritual goal. 

Finally, in the path created by the outer squares, one should write the letters of the alphabet, twelve in each direction, starting from the North-East, South-East, South-West, and North-West. Regarding that writing: of those letters of the alphabet, the last two vowels—the nasal dot and the double-dot breath <note>original: "bindu-visarjanīyayor" (Anusvāra and Visarga)</note>—the dot should be joined to the fourteen vowels, while the double-dot...

# [ Chapter 13 ]

## Description of the Application and Fruits of the Ten Types of Sacred Diagrams

One should combine the vowels with the *bindu* <note>original: "bindu"; the nasalized dot in Sanskrit representing the seed of pure consciousness</note> and place them in the ointment <insert>*</insert> <note>original: "añjane"; likely refers to a ritual paste or ink</note> thereafter. In this way, the Yantras <term>Yantra: A sacred geometric design used as a tool for ritual and meditation</term> are created, which truly serve as the ten abodes of the Perfected Beings. || 37 ||

Having first drawn the design using red ochre <note>original: "gairikaiḥ"; a red earth pigment often used in sacred drawings</note>, one should invite and worship the Auspicious Goddess <note>Shiva</note> there. On the seventh day of the lunar fortnight, during the three junctions of time <note>dawn, noon, and dusk</note>, one should offer sugar cakes— || 38 ||

—along with milk porridge <note>original: "payasaḥ"</note> in the morning and at noon. However, in the evening, one should offer curd-rice <insert>†</insert>, milk, and plantains <note>banana fruit</note>. || 39 ||

The focused practitioner should perform this worship for an entire Mandala <term>Mandala: Here refers to a ritual cycle, often lasting 40 or 48 days</term> or half of one. One shall obtain their heart's desire through the grace of the Goddess with very little effort. || 40 ||

Having drawn the second diagram with cinnabar <note>original: "daradaiḥ"; a bright red mineral ore of mercury</note> and having invited the Goddess on that day, one should offer well-cooked goat meat and rice mixed with honey. || 41 ||

By doing so, one will be able to bring a king under their influence without effort; likewise, one can enchant a beloved woman for the duration of one's life. || 42 ||

Having prepared the third diagram with vermilion <note>original: "sindūraiḥ"</note> and invited the Goddess there, and having worshipped for that many days, one can subdue various types of enemies. || 43 ||

---

Having joined the thirty-four letters from *Ka* to *La*, one should write the final letter *Ksha* in the corners of the square, within the four-sided frame, outside the two outer circles beyond the octagon, along with the *visarga* <note>the two dots representing an aspirated 'h' sound</note>. This is the first Yantra. For the second and subsequent Yantras, one should write the second letter and so on, a hundred times as before, in the eight corners of this very same Yantra. The others are the same. [This explains verses] 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, and 37.

With the twenty-two and a half verses starting with "the first" and ending with "are declared," the teacher instructs on the ten types of Yantra applications and their results. There, in the first Yantra: "One should worship"—meaning according to the daily ritual sequence. "Sita" means sugar. || 38 || The meaning is that the three offering substances, such as milk porridge, should be offered respectively during the three junctions of the day. || 39 || "In this way for half"—means for half a Mandala cycle. || 40 || "With cinnabar"—using the mineral ore. "On that day"—on the seventh day. || 41 || "So long"—for the previously mentioned Mandala period. "Should worship"—following the daily sequence. Here—

# [ Chapter 13 ]

## The Specific Materials and Fruits of the Sacred Diagrams (Continued)

Having created the fourth diagram with saffron <note>original: "kuṅkumaiḥ"</note>, one should worship [the Goddess] in its center in the same manner. Within seven days, all calamities shall vanish by her grace. || 44 ||

Having created the fifth diagram with sandalwood <note>original: "chandanaiḥ"</note>, one should worship the Auspicious Goddess <note>original: "śivām"; here referring to the feminine power or the consort of Shiva</note> in its center. Offer only milk porridge <term>Pāyasa: A sacred sweet rice pudding made with milk and sugar</term>, plantains <note>original: "mocā"</note>, and white sugar combined with ghee <term>Ghṛta: Clarified butter used in rituals and cooking</term>. || 45 ||

By making these offerings at the three junctions of the day <note>dawn, noon, and dusk</note> for a month, one overcomes all diseases entirely. Having conquered illness, one may live happily for a long time, spending the remainder of one's life free from affliction. || 46 ||

One should perform a ritual anointing <term>Abhiṣeka: A ceremonial bathing of a sacred object or person</term> at that very spot, having established a ritual pot and worshipping with the prescribed materials. To the teacher, one should give a ritual honorarium <note>original: "dakṣiṇām"</note> and donate wealth on the earth according to one's capacity. || 47 ||

If the ritual was for the restoration of life, one might even give all of one's possessions. One should offer as much wealth as is required to ensure that the teacher reaches a state of total satisfaction. || 48 ||

Next, one should draw the sixth diagram using sandalwood mixed with camphor. This can be drawn on a smooth stone slab, a ritual seat, or on a plastered floor. || 49 ||

One should offer cooked rice with ghee, milk porridge, sweet cakes <note>original: "apūpa"</note>, and various side dishes. The self-controlled practitioner should worship at the three junctions of the day while chanting the sacred mantra <note>original: "vidyām"</note>. || 50 ||

By the mere offering of these fragrances, living beings are freed even from the terrible fever born of malevolent sorcery. Indeed, the powers of Mantra and Yantra are unthinkable! || 51 ||

Having fashioned the seventh diagram on a copper plate, and having invoked and worshipped the deity there <insert>1</insert> <note>original: "kṛtvā’vādhyābhipūjya vā"; a variant reading suggests "having invoked and worshipped them"</note>, one should establish it in the temple. By doing so, Fortune <note>Lakshmi</note> becomes very steady for you. || 52 ||

Having fashioned the eighth diagram on silver, one should wear or keep it for the attainment of all prosperity. Having fashioned the ninth on gold, O Auspicious One ❊! <insert>*</insert> <note>A variant reading for "Shive" (O Auspicious One) is "Kshive"</note>, one should wear it as an ornament or jewelry. || 53 ||

---

**[Commentary: The Manorama]**

In this section, the "worship of all" refers to the regular daily sequence of rites. "In the same manner" means as previously described, following the worship of the second diagram. || 42 ||

"For that many days" is as stated before. "In that way" implies including the offering materials used in the worship of the second diagram. "Two kinds [of enemies]" refers to those who are natural and those who are created. Among them, "natural" <note>original: "sahaja"</note> means those born of one's own family or internal nature, while "created" <note>original: "kṛtrima"</note> refers to those who have become enemies through some offense. || 43 || "In that way..."

# [ Chapter 13 ]

## The Statement of the Rite of Life-Breath Installation

->With the tenth [diagram], one should accomplish all tasks by worshipping the Auspicious Goddess <note>original: "shivām"; here referring to the feminine energy or Devi</note>.<-
->Whatever work is desired, that should be placed in the center of the diagram. || 54 ||<-
->Having done so, one should worship her there while remembering that task in one's heart.<-
->Within a specific number of days, one attains that goal; of this, there is no doubt. || 55 ||<-
->Having made ten of these diagrams on birch bark <term>Bhūrja: The bark of the Himalayan birch tree, traditionally used as a surface for writing sacred mantras</term> and having worshipped them,<-
->one should place them inside a vessel made of beeswax <note>original: "siktha"</note> filled with honey <note>original: "kṣaudra"</note>. || 56 ||<-
->Concentrated in mind, one should worship at the three junctions of the day <note>dawn, noon, and dusk</note> with red sandalwood and red flowers.<-
->Facing the person to be influenced <term>Sādhya: The target of a ritual or the person one wishes to attract or heal</term>, one should constantly recite the sacred knowledge <note>the mantra or "vidyā"</note> while remembering them. || 57 ||<-
->Bound by the neck as if by a noose <note>original: "pāśena"</note>, they fall at one's feet,<-
->with hands folded in reverence upon their head, saying, "I am your servant." || 58 ||<-
->Within twice-seven nights <note>fourteen days</note>, men, women, and even kings are subdued.<-
->By making it [the diagram] in that specific way <margin>Or: "making the corners in a specific way"</margin> and daily at the three junctions, || 59 ||<-
->women afflicted by the fever of desire <note>original: "kāma-jvara"</note> will slowly rise from their beds.<-
->Abandoning family, shame, and discernment, they shall become his servants. || 60 ||<-
->Thus, the applications of the diagrams have been declared.<-
->Now I shall tell you the Rite of Life-Breath Installation <term>Prāṇapratiṣṭhā-vidyā: The ritual process of "awakening" a diagram or image, conceptually infusing it with living breath and consciousness</term>; listen, O Parvati! || 61 ||<-

Wind, Sky joined with Earth, the Touch-sensory letter joined with Pervasion;

# [ Chapter 13 ]

## Description of the Six-Limbed Ritual Placement, the Meditation on Life-Force Energy, and Other Rites. 228

With the seven syllables starting with *Ya* <note>original: "ya-ādi-sapta-akṣaraiḥ"; these are the semi-vowels and sibilants: ya, ra, la, va, śa, ṣa, sa</note>, one should perform the Six-Limbed Placement by combining them in pairs. One should also place those same syllables within the tissues of the body, such as the skin, while they are enclosed within the syllable of Power. || 69 ||

One should meditate on the Goddess of Life-Force <term>Prāṇaśakti: The personification of the vital breath or cosmic energy that animates all living beings</term>. She is glowing red and dressed in red garments. Her crown is adorned with red jewels, and her lower lip is as tender as a red sprout. || 70 ||

Her face is graced with a beautiful smile and a pair of eyes like red lotuses. In her two hands, she holds a cluster of flowers and a noose. || 71 ||

She is surrounded on all sides by ten Powers <note>These represent the ten types of vital breaths: Prāṇa, Apāna, Samāna, Udāna, Vyāna, Nāga, Kūrma, Kṛkara, Devadatta, and Dhanañjaya</note> who are similar to herself. One should worship her in the center of a lotus, accompanied by these infinite powers. || 72 ||

---

"Wind"—this means the letter *Va* accompanied by "Water." <note>This section decodes the esoteric code for the 40-syllable mantra</note> "Sky joined with Earth" refers to the letter *Ma*. This is the twenty-first letter. || 65 || "Void joined with Illusion"—Illusion refers to the *Visarga* <note>The aspirated 'h' sound in Sanskrit</note>; thus, the syllable *Naḥ*. The "fourth" is *Prā*. The "fifth" is *ṇā*. "Fire" refers to the long vowel *Ī*. "The Swan joined with Wind" refers to *Ha*. "Pervasion joined with Wind" refers to *Ya*. || 67 || "One’s own" refers to the letter *Nu* joined with the "Earth-holder." "The Heart with Water and Wind" refers to *Svā*. "The Swan joined with Wind" refers to *Ha*. Thus, the Life-Breath Installation mantra consists of forty syllables. In all the Tantras, this is the mantra used for the installation of life-force during the consecration of icons, dolls used in rituals, water-pots, and for inducing the presence of a deity. || 68 ||

With the verse beginning "Starting with Ya," the author teaches the <term>Ṣaḍaṅganyāsa: The ritual practice of 'placing' syllables on six specific parts of the body (heart, head, crest, armor, eyes, and weapon) to sanctify the practitioner</term> for the Knowledge of Life-Breath Installation. There, "by double combinations" means by joining two letters at a time. Specifically: *Ya* and *Ra* for the heart; *Ra* and *La* for the head; *La* and *Va* for the crest; *Va* and *Śa* for the protective armor; *Ṣa* and *Śa* for the eyes; and *Sa* and *Sa* for the "weapon" <note>An 'astra' or weapon-gesture used for protection in ritual</note>. Thus, one should perform the six-limbed placement along with the ritual suffixes. "In the skin, etc." refers to the seven <term>dhātus: The structural tissues of the body, namely skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, and semen</term>. "Those same" refers to the previously mentioned seven syllables beginning with *Ya* and ending with *Sa*. "Enclosed within the syllable of Power" <note>original: "śakti-puṭa-sthitam"</note> describes the method: each letter is enveloped by the *Hṛllekhā* <note>The seed-syllable HRĪṂ</note> a thousand times. According to the oral tradition, these should be placed on the heart, the base of the arms, the upper limbs, the two armpits, the heart, and the pairs of hands and feet; or, they may be placed in the heart alone. || 69 ||

With the three verses beginning with "One should meditate" and ending with "in the center," the author teaches the meditation on the Life-Force. There, "a cluster of flowers" <note>original: "prasūna-piṇḍam"</note> is held in the right hand because the Goddess is the essence of life. <margin>(2) "That life-giving" is the reading in the commentary manuscript.</margin> From that comes "life-giving," represented by the cluster of flowers. "Ten Powers" refers to the vital breaths like Prāṇa and others. Each of these is further "endowed with infinite powers." || 70 || 71 || 72 ||

### In the Tantrarāja with the commentary named Manoramā

## The Attendant Powers and the Ritual of Consecration

The powers are Prāṇa, Apāna, Samāna, Vyāna, and Udāna;
Nāga, Kūrma, Kṛkara, Devadatta, and Dhanañjaya. || 73 ||
<note>These ten "powers" represent the ten vital breaths or physiological functions in yogic anatomy. Prāṇa (out-breath), Apāna (down-breath), Samāna (digestive breath), Vyāna (diffusive breath), and Udāna (up-breath) are the primary five. The latter five (Nāga to Dhanañjaya) are the secondary breaths responsible for functions like belching, blinking, and sneezing.</note>

Having drawn two squares, and within them two circles,
within that a ten-petaled lotus, and within that two more circles/lotuses; || 74 ||

Having invoked the Goddess in the center and offered the respectful water <note>original: arghya</note>, one should worship these powers.
One should chant the mantra one hundred thousand times while subsisting only on milk, and then perform a fire sacrifice with a tenth of that number. || 75 ||

The sacrifice is performed with pure sesame seeds and white mustard seeds mixed with the three sweet substances <note>original: madhura-traya; usually honey, ghee, and sugar</note>.
One should also perform daily libations <note>original: tarpaṇa</note> with fragrant water to achieve success. || 76 ||

In all instances in this system <note>original: tantra</note> where dolls <term>puttali: physical figurines used in ritual practice, often made of clay or dough</term> and mystical diagrams <term>yantra: geometric instruments used for meditation and ritual</term> are mentioned,
One should use this knowledge <note>the 40-syllable Prāṇapratiṣṭhā mantra</note> to instill life-force into them. || 77 ||

Listen, O Wise One! to the diagram of this Goddess, which brings immediate proof;
By its power, the doll becomes pulsing with life through the strength of the mantra. || 78 ||

Draw eight lines from East to West and eight from South to North.
This creates forty-nine squares; within these, one should place the letters. || 79 ||

Starting from the North-East <note>original: prāg-uttara</note>, filling the squares around the perimeter and moving inward,
In the nine squares remaining in the middle, one should write the letters in their proper order. || 80 ||

---

Regarding the verse starting with **Prāṇa**, the author describes the surrounding powers of the Goddess of Life-Force. Among them, the primary Life-Force power is the collective form of all these. || 73 ||

Regarding **two squares**, etc., through the three verses ending with **achieve success**, the author teaches the ritual circle for her worship, the worship itself, and the method of practicing that system. Here, **that pair** refers to the two circles. The rest of the construction of the ritual diagram is easy to understand. || 74 || **Offered respectful water** means as previously described. || 75 || **White** means pale or fair-colored mustard seeds. || 76 ||

Regarding **In all instances in this system**, etc., the author teaches the procedure for the Consecration of Life-Force <term>prāṇapratiṣṭhā: the ritual of inviting a deity or a soul into an image or diagram</term> everywhere. **In those** refers to those specific dolls and diagrams. The rest is easy. || 77 ||

Regarding **the diagram**, etc., through the four verses ending with **becomes**, the author teaches the construction of that specific diagram and its practical application. Here, **pulsing with life** refers to the arrival of the life-force of the person being worked upon <note>the "sādhya" or subject of the ritual</note>. **One should place** refers to the letters of the Life-Force Consecration mantra. || 78 || 79 || **North-East** refers to the direction of the deity Īśāna. **Around**—meaning moving clockwise.

# [ Chapter 13 ]

### Discussion of Bringing the Life-Force of the Target

Then, having written the name of the target <term>sādhya: the person who is the intended object of the ritual</term> in the two remaining spaces, the practitioner <term>sādhaka: the ritual adept performing the ceremony</term>
Should recite the mantra <note>original: vidyā</note> one hundred times while touching the diagram with the **living hand** <gloss>the hand corresponding to the side of the body through which the breath is currently flowing</gloss>. || 81 ||

With that material, one should fashion the **dolls** <term>puttalikā: figurines used as a ritual substitute for the target</term> for success; it cannot be accomplished otherwise.
Now listen, I shall describe the wonderful method of bringing the life-force and other elements of the target. || 82 ||

Concentrating on the **potency of the mantra** <note>original: mantra-vīrya; the inherent power of the sacred sound</note> <gloss>1</gloss>, and using that visualization, one draws from the interior of the target's body:
The objects of the senses of knowledge and action, the mind, the life-force, and the physical form. || 83 ||

From within the body of that target to the doll <gloss>2</gloss>, using their names, 
And visualizing a **red cord** extending from the center of the Power <note>original: Śakti</note>, one should mentally bring and offer these elements. || 84 ||

One should join the names of the target at the end of the syllables of the mantra.
Touching the doll, one should recite the mantra thus joined one thousand times. || 85 ||

With the **living hand** <gloss>the hand on the side of the active breath</gloss>, the practitioner should enter into the target's consciousness in the middle of the night.
When the life-breath is thus established, the doll wonderfully **pulsates** <gloss>3</gloss>. || 86 ||

---

**Commentary:**

"Certainly." "From the entrance" refers to the previously stated sequence. "Syllables of the limbs" refers to the seven syllables beginning with *Ya*. 
In the construction of the mystical diagram <term>yantra</term>, the rest is easy to understand. || 80 || "Touching" implies touching the yantra. || 81 || "With that" refers to the substance or material. 

The meaning is as follows: those substances mentioned for the creation of the seven dolls should be placed within the yantra, or the yantra should be placed upon those materials, and then the dolls should be fashioned from them. 

With the four verses starting from "The target etc." and ending with "wonderful," the author teaches the method of bringing the life-force of the target into the dolls. The "potency of the mantra" is not discussed here, as it will be explained in the twenty-fifth chapter. || 82 || 

"With that" means along with the visualization <note>original: smṛti</note>. "From the interior of that body" means from within the body of the target. "Objects" refers to the ten objects of the senses <note>the five senses of perception and five of action</note>. "Life" means the Self or Soul. "Physical form" refers to the eight constituents <term>dhātu: the fundamental elements of the body</term> known as skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, semen, and vital energy <note>original: ojas</note>. 

One should join the eight syllables starting with *Ya* (including the nasal *bindu* dots) at the very beginning, then after uttering the name of each constituent, one should "bring" and "establish" them according to the instructions. || 83 || 84 ||

"At the end of the syllables" means that in the syllables of the Consecration Mantra <note>original: prāṇapratiṣṭhā-vidyā</note>, one should insert the names of the target where the formula says "to such-a-one" <note>original: amuṣyai</note>. || 85 || 

"With the living hand" refers to the hand on the side of the body where the breath is currently flowing through the nostril.

# [ Chapter 13 ]

### On the Birth Stars and the Construction of the Ritual Effigy

->I shall now tell you the birth stars of the target;<-
->The sub-division <term>Navāṃśa: a one-ninth division of a zodiac sign used for precision in Indian astrology</term> arising from the birth ascendant is the primary <gloss>ṣa</gloss> factor. || 87 ||<-

->The nails, hair, and dust from the feet of the enemy,<-
->As well as other body hairs, should be incorporated into the doll for a death rite. || 89 ||<-

->In rites of subjugation and all others, use the doll as previously described;<-
->Thus, the entire ritual for the attraction of the life-force <note>original: prāṇākarṣaṇa</note> has been explained to you. || 90 ||<-

->Having performed the attraction of the life-force with the knowledge stated,<-
->One should then perform the specific prescribed actions upon that designated doll. || 91 ||<-

->In all lethal rites <note>original: māraṇa</note>, the positions of the planets relative to the target's stars,<-
->As well as the eight-fold point system <term>Aṣṭakavarga: a method of predicting planetary strength based on eight points of reference</term> for the nine stars, must be considered. || 92 ||<-

---

**Commentary:**

Regarding the phrase **"In that consciousness"**—this refers to the consciousness of the doll. The meaning is as follows: having established the doll in the center of the previously described ritual diagram <note>original: yantra</note>, one should carry out the process of bringing the life-force and other vital elements of the target into it. || 86 ||

With the two verses beginning with **"of the target"** and ending with **"in the fire ritual,"** the text teaches the ten types of birth stars <term>Nakṣatra: lunar mansions or star signs in the Hindu zodiac</term> belonging to living beings. Among them, the Navāṃśa sub-division of the birth ascendant is the "primary" one. This means: the specific degree-division and the specific star associated with the Navāṃśa at the moment of the target's birth is their most vital astrological point. || 87 || 

The **"nine other stars"** are secondary and are considered equal to one another. They are determined **"by the association of the nine planets"** <note>original: navagraha</note>. This implies their connection to the zodiac signs. This will be explained in the **"fire ritual"** section—the chapter dedicated to burnt offerings. || 88 ||

With the three verses beginning with **"of the enemy"** and ending with **"should perform,"** the author provides instructions on the qualities required for constructing the doll and concludes the preceding topic. Here, **"in death"** refers specifically to the ritual application for killing <note>original: māraṇa-prayoga</note>. || 89 || 

In the phrase **"in subjugation and others,"** the word "others" refers to rituals such as attraction, causing dissension, and so on. **"By that"** means using a doll made of materials specified for those particular rituals, even if they lack the target's physical remnants like nails or hair. **"There"** refers to the specific ritual application being performed. || 91 ||

With the two verses beginning with **"in all cases"** and ending with **"from debt,"** the text teaches the necessity of observing the planetary favorability of the person being targeted in malevolent magic <term>Abhicāra: rituals intended to cause harm, paralysis, or death</term>, and the negative consequences if this is ignored. Here, **"planetary positions relative to the target's stars"** refers to the strength or weakness of the planets in relation to the target's primary star and zodiac sign. The **"eight-fold point system"** <gloss>Aṣṭakavarga</gloss> refers to the calculation of the seven planets (Sun, etc.) and the birth ascendant for each of the target's nine birth stars...

# [ Chapter 13 ]

### Discourse on Those Subject and Not Subject to Lethal Rites

A self-controlled practitioner should perform a lethal rite <note>original: māraṇam; the tantric act of causing death through ritual means</note> only after carefully examining the status of the target's planetary periods <term>Daśā: specific blocks of time in an individual’s life ruled by particular planets, determining their fortune and vulnerability</term>. A ritual action performed without this observation kills the practitioner himself in an instant. || 93 ||

One should never employ lethal magic against a Brahmin <note>original: brāhmaṇa; a member of the priestly or scholarly class</note>, a righteous man, a king, a woman, a person of faith, a generous giver, or one who is perpetually compassionate. || 94 ||

If one employs such magic against these people out of personal enmity, it turns back and kills the practitioner. Now, I shall describe the appropriate subjects for lethal magic: || 95 ||

The wicked, atheists, thieves, those who revile the gods and the Brahmins, killers of the public, and those who remain intent on deeds that cause distress; || 96 ||

Those who seize the land, wealth, property, or wives of others; those who destroy families; those who revile the sacred traditions <note>original: samayānām; the secret vows and codes of the tantric community</note>; backbiters; and those who kill kings; || 97 ||

Those who perpetually harm living beings with poison, fire, theft, or weapons—one should employ lethal rites against these. By these actions, the practitioner does not become a sinner <note>original: pātakī</note>. || 98 ||

Having quickly performed the lethal rite, the practitioner must then, according to his means, worship his Guru and the Brahmins at the conclusion of the work, honoring them with his own wealth. || 99 ||

Then, having consecrated the secret knowledge <note>original: vidyām; here referring to the mantra used in the rite</note>, one should recite it one hundred thousand times while eating only ritual offerings <note>original: haviṣya; pure food like rice and ghee suitable for Vedic/Tantric offerings</note>. If the target was one whose birth star is "inimical" <note>original: janmadveṣya; a technical astrological term for a star that is naturally hostile to the practitioner's own</note>, one should perform the ritual sprinkling <note>original: abhiṣeka</note> for a full year. || 100 ||

***

**Commentary:**

The text also describes the "eight-fold points" <term>Aṣṭakavarga: a system where eight different points of reference—the seven planets and the ascendant—are used to calculate the strength of a house or planet</term> mentioned in the science of astrology as a means to indicate mutual favorability. || 92 ||

**Regarding "the status of the planetary periods"**—this refers to the status of the "Great Periods" within the Wheel of Time <note>original: kālacakra-mahādaśā</note>. The observation of whether the planets are favorable or unfavorable is required specifically for the lethal rite <note>original: māraṇa</note>, and not for other rituals. || 93 ||

Through the verses starting with **"A Brahmin..."** and ending with **"that [kills him],"** the text teaches who should not be targeted and the sin <note>original: pratyavāyam</note> incurred if one targets them. In that context, "righteous" is an adjective modifying the "king." Regarding lethal magic—the rest is easy to understand. || 94 ||

Through the three verses beginning with **"the subjects of lethal magic"** and ending with **"sinner,"** the text teaches who may be targeted. In this context, "by these"—refers to the lethal rites. "Sinner"—refers to the practitioner. || 95-98 ||

<margin>The original manuscript text for verse 100 contains a variant reading: *janmadveṣya* (hateful to birth) instead of *janmadvaye* (in two births).</margin>

# [ Chapter 13 ]

...By performing a fire sacrifice with Durva grass <note>original: dūrvā-homa; Durva is *Cynodon dactylon*, a sacred grass used for purification and longevity</note>, he is released from those sins. Thus, I have told you the entire ritual procedure for the goddess [Shiva]duti Nitya. || 101 ||

The pervasion consisting of the essence of the Feet <note>original: pāda-tattva; refers to the spiritual lineage or the "feet" of the deity/guru which permeate the practitioner's consciousness</note> has been well described. By contemplating this within the heart, that essence is made one's own. || 102 ||

->Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the Shri Kadimata, among the sixteen Nitya Tantras.<-

***

**[Commentary]**

With the three verses starting with "Having performed" <note>original: ṛtvā; referring to verse 99</note> and ending with "procedure" <note>referring to verse 101</note>, the author teaches the penance for performing malevolent magic <term>Abhicāra: tantric magic intended to harm, coerce, or kill</term>. In that context, "quickly" <note>original: āśu</note> is the correct word division. "Eating sacrificial food" <term>Haviṣyabhuk: one who follows a restricted ritual diet</term>—"sacrificial food" <note>original: havisya</note> specifically means rice <note>vrohi-taṇḍula</note> cooked without salt. || 99 || 100 ||

"From those sins"—meaning the sins of performing malevolent magic. "He"—refers to the practitioner <term>Sādhaka: an initiated practitioner of a spiritual or tantric discipline</term>. || 101 || 102 ||

Thus, in the commentary titled *Manoramā* <note>"The Delighter of the Mind"</note>—composed by Shri Subhaganandanatha for the complete Tantra known as the *Shri Kadimata* <note>The "K-initial" school of the Shrikula tradition</note>, which is the light of the King of Lions of the *Prapanchasara*—the thirteenth chapter, dedicated to revealing the ritual procedure for the wisdom of the goddess Shivaduti Nitya <note>Shivaduti is the thirteenth of the sixteen Nitya goddesses; her name means "She who has Shiva as her messenger"</note>, is fully concluded. || 13 ||

# Chapter Fourteen

Now, among the sixteen Nityas <term>Nityā: "Eternal" goddesses representing the fifteen lunar days plus the full cycle</term>, the one declared as the ninth is the goddess Tvarita <note>original: Tvaritā; her name means "The Swift One," reflecting the speed with which she grants results</note>. Her twelve-syllable mantra <term>Vidyā: a mantra dedicated to a female deity</term> has indeed been stated previously. || 1 ||

O Wise Lady! Hear now the ritual procedures for her, including the fire sacrifices and the use of mystical diagrams <term>Yantra: a geometric diagram used in meditation and ritual</term>, by which the practitioner <term>Mantrī: one who masters and recites a mantra</term>—becoming as beautiful as the God of Love—stirs the entire world. || 2 ||

With the seven syllables starting from the fourth syllable of the mantra, one should perform the ritual placement <term>Aṅganyāsa: the practice of "touching" parts of the body with specific sounds to sanctify them</term> on the hands and the six limbs in a sequential order, using pairs of syllables. || 3 ||

One should then place the remaining syllables—starting with the syllable *Tara* <note>original: tārādyaiḥ; likely referring to the sacred sound Om or a specific seed syllable</note>—sequentially upon the head, forehead, throat, heart, navel, the base <note>original: ādhāra; referring to the Mūlādhāra or root center at the base of the spine</note>, the thighs, the knees, the shanks, and the feet. || 4 ||

The placement should be done using the second syllable, the penultimate syllable, and those situated in the middle. Hear now the visualization of her form, her powers, and the method of her worship. || 5 ||

She is dark-complexioned <note>original: śyāma-varṇā; often a deep blue or black associated with primordial power</note>, of beautiful form, and glowing with the beauty of fresh youth. She is radiant, adorned with ornaments crafted from the eight great serpent kings <term>Aṣṭanāga: the eight legendary serpents of Indian mythology, such as Vasuki and Takshaka</term>. || 6 ||

---

## Commentary on Chapter Fourteen

In the previous thirteenth chapter, the procedure for the eighth Nitya, Dutonitya, was taught. Following that, the procedure for the ninth goddess, Tvarita Nitya, is taught in this fourteenth chapter, which consists of one hundred verses. Through the two verses beginning with "Now, among the sixteen" and ending with "the world," the author introduces the subject of the chapter. Regarding the phrase "stated previously"—this refers to the Third Chapter. || 1 || "Stirs"—meaning he makes himself famous or celebrated through his own power. || 2 ||

Through the three verses beginning with "With the [mantra's] syllables" and ending with "worship," the author teaches the ritual placement <note>Nyāsa</note> and other rites. "In that manner"—refers to the method used in the "Infusion of Life Force" <term>Prāṇapratiṣṭhā: a ritual to "awaken" the divine presence in an image or the practitioner's body</term>, where the six limbs are joined in a chain-like sequence, and the thighs, knees, shanks, and feet are addressed one by one. || 3 || 4 ||

"By those situated between the second and the penultimate": the second refers to the syllable *Hlalekha* <note>original: hlalekhā; a complex "seed" syllable used in Tvarita's mantra</note>; the penultimate is the one next to the last; and the placement uses the syllables situated between them, as well as the others starting with the syllable *Tara*. The meaning is as follows: first the syllable *Hlalekha*, and then...

# The Tantrarāja with the Commentary named Manoramā

Her earrings and armlets, as well as her belt and anklets, are formed by the four classes—Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra <term>Varṇa: the four traditional social classes, here represented by eight serpent kings</term>—who take on fierce forms as serpents. || 7 ||

She is draped in garments of fresh shoots and leaves, her arms adorned with beautiful bracelets made of peacock feathers. She shines with a crown of rubies. || 8 ||

She wears a crest of peacock feathers, and her umbrella and banner are likewise made of peacock feathers. Her breasts are decorated with saffron and shimmering necklaces of *gunja* berries <note>original: guñjā-guṇa; the red and black seeds of the Abrus precatorius plant, often associated with forest-dwelling deities</note>. || 9 ||

She has three eyes, a lovely countenance, and a lotus-like face with a gentle smile. In her four arms, she holds the noose and the goad, while her other hands display the gestures of granting boons and dispelling fear. || 10 ||

Having meditated on the Goddess Totala <note>a name for Tvarita</note> in this way, one should worship her surrounded by her companion powers. Before her stands Sphāṭakārī, radiant with a bow and arrow in her hands. || 11 ||

She is swift in granting favor and results to her practitioners; therefore, she is called Tvaritā ("The Swift One"). She is the ninth of the Māyā Nityās <note>The Nityas are goddesses of the lunar days; Tvarita is specifically associated with the ninth day</note>. || 12 ||

---

The practitioner should place the ten syllables of the mantra—starting with the sacred sound *Om* <note>original: praṇava</note>, then the penultimate syllable, then the seed-syllable of the Heart <note>original: hṛllekhā, the syllable Hrīṃ</note>, and those ending with the syllable of protection *Phaṭ*—in the ten prescribed locations of the body. || 5 ||

---

Through the five verses beginning with "She is dark-complexioned" and ending with "surrounded [by her powers]," the text teaches the daily meditation for the Goddess. Regarding the verses from "According to the order of the directions" to "fierce forms," it is said: The eight lords of serpents belonging to the Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra castes sequentially form her pair of earrings, armlets, belt, and anklets. || 6 || 

It should be understood here that the fashioning of her ornaments follows the traditional order of the emergence of the four castes. || 7 || 

"Draped in garments of fresh shoots" means she wears a dress of leafy branches. "A crest of peacock feathers"—the word *āpīḍa* means a crown or hair-ornament. "Her umbrella"—meaning her umbrella is made of peacock feathers. "Her banner" is the same. The visualization of her weapons should proceed from the upper-left hand down to the lower-right hand, in a clockwise fashion. || 10 ||

"Totalā" refers to Tvaritā. The names of the Goddess are Tvaritā, Totalā, and Tūrṇā <note>All three names signify "speed" or "swiftness," highlighting her nature of acting immediately for the devotee</note>.

Through the five verses beginning with "Standing before her" and ending with "The God of Love," the text teaches the surrounding powers and energies of the Goddess. There, "radiant with a bow and arrow" means her pair of hands shines while holding the bow and the arrow. || 11 ||

# Chapter 14: Description of the Daily Worship Procedure and Related Matters | 237

A servant <term>Kiṅkara: a specific type of attendant spirit or ghost-being who serves a higher deity</term> of black complexion, holding a mace in his hand and with curly hair standing upright, should be worshipped in front of her for the attainment of all success. || 13 ||

At the two sides of her door, the companion powers named Jayā and Vijayā should be worshipped. They resemble the goddess in appearance and hold golden canes in their swaying lotus-hands. || 14 ||

Then [the following powers]: Huṅkāra, Khecarī, Caṇḍā, Chedinī, Kṣepaṇī, Strī, Huṅkārī, and Kṣemakarī. These are equal to the World-Guardians <term>Lokapālas: the guardian deities of the cardinal directions, like Indra or Agni</term>. || 15 ||

These powers of the mantra's syllables <note>original: mantvārṇa-śaktayaḥ; the individual sounds of the goddess's secret mantra personified as deities</note> are to be worshipped while standing upon the eight petals of the lotus. By worshipping them daily, a man becomes like the God of Love <note>original: Manmatha; the deity of desire</note> among women. || 16 ||

O Great Goddess! Listen now to the ritual procedure <term>Pūjā-vidhi: the formal steps of worship</term> for that goddess Tvaritā. Having prepared the offering as before, one should place the Sovereign Lady on a beautiful golden seat marked with eight lions. || 17 ||

On that golden throne, one should construct a diagram with two square enclosures <term>Bhūpura: literally "earth-city," the square outer walls of a mandala</term> possessing a western gate. Inside that, draw two concentric circles. || 18 ||

Inside those circles, having drawn an eight-petaled lotus, one should invoke the supreme Auspicious One <note>original: Parā Śivā; here referring to the Goddess in her highest form</note> as before, surrounded on all sides by her companion powers. || 19 ||

---

**Commentary: The *Manoramā***

**On "favor" [verse 12]:** This implies her being well-disposed or facing the practitioner. Through this verse, the etymology of the Goddess's name is established. || 12 ||

**Holding a mace [verse 13]:** This attendant also has two hands. **Curly** <note>original: varbaraḥ</note> means having coiled hair. **Servant** <note>original: kiṅkaraḥ</note> refers to a specific type of spirit who acts as a messenger or servant to the Goddess. || 13 ||

**Resemble her [verse 14]:** This means they have the same complexion as the deity. **Golden canes in their swaying lotus-hands**: this indicates that they also possess two arms. || 14 ||

**Strī and Huṅkārī [verse 15]:** These are two distinct powers. **Equal to the World-Guardians**: this implies they should be understood as having similar colors, weapons, and mounts as the traditional direction-guardians. || 15 ||

**Powers of the mantra’s syllables [verse 16]:** These are the powers associated with the individual letters of Tvaritā’s mantra. **By whom**: refers to these letter-powers. **One becomes**: the practitioner is implied. **God of Love**: this means he agitates all women by his mere appearance, just as the god of desire does. || 16 ||

With the six verses beginning with "Listen" and ending with "concluding," the author teaches the daily worship ritual <note>original: nitya-saparyā-krama</note> of the Goddess. In that context, **as before** means using the root mantra and the lotus gesture. **Sovereign Lady**: the presiding deity of all. **Marked with eight lions**: having a seat supported by legs shaped like eight lions. || 17 ||

With the verse-half starting with "one should construct" and ending with "having drawn," the author describes the sacred diagram <term>Cakra: a geometric drawing used as a vessel for the deity's presence</term> for the Goddess's daily worship. The meaning is this: having drawn two squares with a western door, one should place within them an eight-petaled lotus with its central pericarp and two surrounding circles. || 18 || **In that**: refers to within the diagram.

# Tantrarāja with the Commentary Named Manoramā | 238

->**The Ritual of Mudras, Attendants, and Healing**<-

After first displaying the symbolic hand gestures <term>Mudras: ritual hand positions used to signal intentions to the deity</term>, one should worship her as prescribed. The two leading attendants <gloss>(1)</gloss> <note>These are the spirits Phaṭkāra and Kiṅkara</note> are to be worshipped either at the tip of the front-most petal or within the center of the outer circles. || 20 ||

One should devotedly offer a sacrifice <term>Bali: an offering of food or specialized substances to spirits</term> to the Servant <note>Kiṅkara</note> in front of the Goddess; he is envisioned as being surrounded by a multitude of his own kind within the sacred circle. || 21 ||

Having performed the worship in this manner, one should chant the sacred knowledge <term>Vidyā: the goddess's specific secret mantra</term> one thousand times, or one hundred times. Having performed the fire sacrifice <term>Homa: the act of pouring oblations into a consecrated fire</term>, one should conclude the worship as previously described. || 22 ||

Then, a person who has mastered the mantra <note>One who has achieved "Mantra-siddhi" or spiritual perfection of the sound</note> may perform practical applications. In the ritual of mastery, one should offer a tenth part of the total chant count into the fire using the leaves <gloss>(2)</gloss> and other parts of the wood-apple tree <term>Bilva: the Aegle marmelos tree, sacred in the worship of Shiva and Shakti</term>. || 23 ||

With water that has been empowered by these perfected mantras, one can revive those who have died from the fangs of a hooded snake <note>original: phani-daṃṣṭra-mṛtānām; referring to those seemingly dead from cobra or viper bites</note> by striking <note>or sprinkling</note> the water upon their faces. || 24 ||

One should chant the mantra into their ears, or for the success of the rite, one may strike the head with a stick <gloss>(3)</gloss> and suddenly revive the dead. || 25 ||

O Goddess! Listen now as I describe the ritual for desire-fulfilling fire sacrifices. Having constructed a ritual pit <term>Kuṇḍa: the receptacle for the sacred fire</term> in the shape of a womb <term>Yoni: symbolizing the source of all manifestation</term>, one should make offerings into that fire according to the rules. || 26 ||

---

**The Commentary named Manoramā explains:**

This is what is meant: "Invoking" <note>original: āvāya</note>—this implies into the center of the lotus pericarp. || 18 || "After first displaying the gestures"—this refers to the four primary gestures beginning with the gesture of "Establishing" <note>Sthāpanā-mudrā</note>. This is a standard requirement for all such rituals. "As prescribed"—meaning proceeding in a clockwise direction starting from the front.

"At the tip of the front petal"—this means at the very tip of the front-most petal among the eight. "Within the center of the circles"—this refers to the area between the two circles located outside the lotus. "The two leading attendants"—these are Phaṭkāra and Kiṅkara; the meaning is that one should worship them respectively at the tip of the front petal and in the paths between the circles. || 20 ||

"Sacrifice"—this implies an additional offering. "In front of the Goddess"—near her, as done previously. All sacrifices are to be performed in the vicinity of the primary deity. "With those previously mentioned"—meaning with food and other items, and using the specific mantra designated for them. The "circle" <note>original: maṇḍala</note> here refers to the space within the circles. || 21 || "As before"—meaning the conclusion of the worship should follow the procedure used for the goddess Lalitā. || 22 ||

With the three verses beginning with "Then," the text teaches the mastery of the mantra and the method for removing poison for one who has achieved success. There, "with leaves and so on"—the word "and so on" refers to the flowers, roots, stems, and fruits of the tree. "During the chant"—the connection is that one should offer a tenth part into the fire based on the total number of repetitions, which should be a hundred thousand for every syllable of the mantra, as appropriate for this Age. || 23 || "Empowered by mantra."

# Chapter 14 | Descriptions of Various Fire Sacrifices and Their Results

One should offer sesame, mustard, wheat, Shali rice, and barley into the fire. To achieve prosperity, these should be coated in the **three sweets** <term>Trimadhura: a ritual mixture of honey, clarified butter (ghee), and sugar</term>, offered either individually or all together. || 27 ||

For the attainment of the Goddess of Wealth <note>Indira, a name for Lakshmi</note>, one should offer Bakula, Champaka, and various lotuses: the day-blooming, the white <gloss>Kahlara</gloss>, the red <gloss>Arunotpala</gloss>, the night-blooming <gloss>Kairava</gloss>, as well as Jasmine <gloss>Mallika</gloss>, Kunda, and Madhuka flowers. || 28 ||

By offering Ashoka, Patala, and wood-apple <gloss>Bilva</gloss> flowers; white Jati and Vicakila flowers; fresh blue lotuses, oleander <gloss>Ashwaripuja</gloss> <note>Literally "born of the enemy of horses," a poetic name for the toxic Karavira or Oleander plant</note>, and Karnikara flowers— || 29 ||

—one surely attains wealth, beauty, long life, riches, and a treasury of fame. Whatever a person desires, all of it is certainly obtained through this fire sacrifice. || 30 ||

By offering Durva grass, heart-leaved moonseed <gloss>Guduchi</gloss>, the holy fig <gloss>Ashwattha</gloss>, the banyan <gloss>Vata</gloss>, the golden shower tree <gloss>Aragvadha</gloss>, white Arka, and the white fig <gloss>Plaksha</gloss>, a man is quickly freed from all diseases. || 31 ||

By offering sugarcane, rose-apple <gloss>Jambu</gloss>, coconut, banana <gloss>Mocha</gloss>, jaggery, and white sugar, one obtains stable wealth and will surely become a person of great enjoyment. || 32 ||

When these aforementioned substances are offered after being soaked in clarified butter, honey, and milk, they can bring a woman under one's influence <term>Vashya: the ritual act of attraction or subjugation</term> for as long as she lives, along with providing great wealth. || 33 ||

The phrase "one hundred times" is implied here. **In his ears** refers to the ears of the person who has been bitten by a snake. **Chanting**—the word "should revive him" is the implied conclusion. || 24 ||

**Or** indicates another option. **Through the perfection of the chant**—meaning by the perfection gained from chanting the secret knowledge <term>Vidya</term> one thousand times while touching the person’s limbs from head to toe. One may **raise the dead** who have perished from a snake bite. This is the third method. || 25 ||

With the five verses beginning with **"Desire-driven fire sacrifice"** and ending with **"beloved,"** the teacher instructs on the various substances for the fire sacrifice and the various results obtained from them. Regarding the phrase **the womb within the sacrificial pit**: having prepared the pit <term>Kunda: a consecrated fire-pit</term> according to the methods described in the chapter on sacrificial pits, one should fashion a "womb" <term>Yoni: a vulva-shaped protrusion on the pit representing the creative source of the fire</term> in its center. This applies to all these fire sacrifices. **Therein** means within that "womb." **In the fire**—it is implied "once the fire has been established." **According to the rules**—meaning after performing the "Face of the Fire" <note>Agni-mukha: the preliminary rites of inviting the deity into the flame</note> and other rites as previously described. || 26 || **Individually** means using each substance one by one. || 27 || **Red lotus**—as described before. **Night-lotuses** <gloss>Kairava</gloss>—it is implied these are the white variety. || 28 ||

# Chapter 14 | Rituals for Subjugation and the Destruction of Enemies

->**Manorama Commentary on the Tantrarāja**<-

By offering those same substances <note>referring to the sesame, grain, and flowers mentioned on the previous page</note> soaked in clarified butter, kings become subservient, O Beloved. When these are offered soaked in milk, all humans without exception remain under one's control. || 34 ||

By offering mustard seeds and clarified butter into a fire made from **death-wood** <term>Mrityu-kashtha: wood from the Karaskara tree (Strychnos nux-vomica), considered inauspicious and used for destructive rituals</term>, one brings about the death of an enemy. The same result is achieved by offering the flesh of the animal associated with the enemy's birth-source <note>referring to the *Yoni* or animal type associated with the enemy's birth star (Nakshatra)</note> coated in those same substances. || 35 ||

One should cook a sacrificial pap <gloss>Charu</gloss> in a fire fueled by ordinary kitchen wood, using the blood drawn from the animal associated with the target's birth-source. This should then be mixed with ghee and marking-nut <gloss>Arushkara</gloss> and offered into the fire using a ladle shaped like a **snake's head**. || 36 ||

The practitioner, wearing a black cloth wrapped around his head, holding a sword in his hand, and filled with wrath, should perform the sacrifice at the stroke of midnight to strike down the enemy by force. || 37 ||

By offering the fruits and leaves of the death-wood tree into a fire of the same wood, the enemy's elephants and horses will be stricken with disease within seven days. || 38 ||

By offering wood pieces measuring four finger-breadths in length, the enemy’s four-fold army <term>Chaturanga: the traditional Indian army divisions of elephants, chariots, cavalry, and infantry</term> will surely be afflicted by the pain of disease within seven days; of this there is no doubt. || 39 ||

Who indeed can describe the full majesty of this Science <gloss>Vidya</gloss>? Nevertheless, O Beloved, I shall describe a small portion of its direction. Listen! || 40 ||

***

**Commentary:**
Regarding the offerings of sugar, etc. (mentioned in verses 31-32): "By these stated items" refers to the sesame and other ingredients. "Soaked in clarified butter, honey, and milk" means they are drenched in the **three sweets** <term>Trimadhura</term>. Being drenched in the three sweets is a general rule for all these rites. Each item should be used individually as is common in all ritual applications. In the phrase "by wealth etc.," the word "etc." refers to the vital breath <note>original: "prāna-vishayah"</note>. || 33 ||

"By those same substances soaked in clarified butter" means one should perform the sacrifice with all thirty-six substances, such as sesame, coated only in ghee, following the prescribed order. "Soaked in milk" means performing the sacrifice with those same items in the stated order. 

The meaning is as follows:
1.  The first option is to offer the thirty-six substances, ending with sugar, drenched in the **three sweets** according to the sequence for those specific rituals.
2.  The second option is to offer them drenched only in clarified butter.
3.  The third option is to offer them drenched only in milk.

"Death" refers to the **Karaskara tree**. "Coated in those" means soaked in mustard seeds and clarified butter. "Flesh arising from the enemy's source" refers to the flesh of the animal corresponding to the enemy's birth-star <gloss>Nakshatra-yoni</gloss>. "For that purpose" means for the death of the enemy. || 35 ||

"Cooked with blood arising from the source" means cooked with the blood of the animal corresponding to the target's birth-star. "With a snake-head ladle" refers to a ritual tool made from wood that has been shaped...

<note>(2) Some manuscripts read "Phanishirsha-sruva" (a different type of ladle), while the base text reads "Phanishirsha-svava".</note>

# Chapter 14 | Description of the 121-Square Grace-Bestowing Yantra and Its Application
### 31

->Now I shall describe the mystical diagrams <term>Yantra: a geometric diagram used as a tool for concentration and ritual power</term> for the fulfillment of all desires.<-
->O Goddess! Retain them all in your mind in their proper order. || 41 ||<-
->One should draw twelve lines from east to west and twelve from south to north. At all the ends of these lines, one should draw tridents. In the... || 42 ||<-
->...central square, place the target's name inside the **syllable of liberation** <note>original: "Tara," referring to the sacred syllable Om</note>. Starting from the direction of Shiva <note>the Northeast</note> and entering in a clockwise direction, one should write the... || 43 ||<-
->...**Mantra** <term>Vidya: specifically the sacred mantra of the goddess Tvaritā</term> twelve times along with the **Maya** syllable <term>Maya: the seed-syllable HRĪṀ, which represents the power of the Goddess</term>. One should recite this and wear it for the attainment of all success: for wealth, fame, attraction, good fortune, and the acquisition of everything. || 44 ||<-
->To pacify poison, planetary afflictions, disease, and madness; for victory in battle; and for the subjugation of men, women, and kings, one should wear this diagram. || 45 ||<-
->One should draw nine lines from east to west and nine from south to north. Thus, sixty-four squares are created, O Great Goddess!<-

***

**The Manorama Commentary**

"With the hood of a serpent" <note>referring to verse 36</note> means the ritual ladle should be shaped like a cobra's hood. "To strike down enemies"—this connects to the previous instruction to perform sacrifices for the destruction of foes. || 37 ||

"With its fruits" means the fruits of the "death-tree" <note>the Karaskara or Strychnos nux-vomica</note>. "With its leaves" means the leaves of that same tree. || 38 || "Four-finger-long" refers to the blossoms of the *Aragvadha* tree <note>The Indian Laburnum, whose flowers are roughly four fingers in length</note>. || 39 || "That majesty"—the text suggests you should listen to a portion of the majesty or power of this ritual. || 40 ||

With the five verses beginning with "Now I shall describe the Yantras," the text teaches the construction of the **Grace-Bestowing Yantra of 121 Squares**, its ritual application, and its benefits. In this context, "three-pronged" <gloss>trishikhani</gloss> means drawing tridents at the tips of the lines. "In the middle" refers to the square located at the very center of the grid. || 41–42 || "With Maya" implies including the syllable **HRĪṀ** <note>original: "Hrllekha," the 'heart-streak' or seed-syllable of the Goddess</note>. || 43 || "That" refers to the Yantra itself.

The meaning is as follows: One should strike <note>draw</note> twelve lines running East-to-West and twelve lines running North-to-South at equal intervals. This creates a grid. By turning the forty-eight ends of these lines into tridents and focusing on the 121 resulting squares, one should write the **Pranava** (Om) containing the target's name in the centermost square. Then, entering from the Northeast corner in a clockwise spiral, one writes the ten syllables of the **Root Mantra**, excluding the first *Hrim*, twelve times into the squares, incorporating the second *Hrim* according to the prescribed method. This Yantra should then be worn as described. || 44–45 ||

# Chapter 14 | The Great Diagram of Grace and the Secret Mantra
### 242

In those squares, starting from the **Southwest** <note>original: "Nirṛti," the direction associated with destruction, here used as a starting point for transformation</note>, one should write the Lakshmi mantra in sequence. On the outside, one should encircle it with the syllables of the **Swift One** <note>referring to the goddess Tvaritā</note> <gloss>(1)</gloss> which end with the word **vashaṭ** <gloss>one should worship</gloss>. || 47 ||

O Great Goddess! Now hear of the **Great Diagram of Grace** <term>Anugraha Mahachakra: a powerful geometric tool used to bestow blessings and spiritual power</term> and its secret knowledge. It is arranged as a **"Good-on-all-sides"** grid <term>Sarvatobhadra: a complex, symmetrical square used in Tantric worship where the mantra is woven into the grid</term> in the **Anuṣṭubh** meter <note>a poetic meter of 32 syllables</note>, and it grants all success. || 48 ||

The first syllable is **Space** combined with the **Fire of Destruction** and **Ordinary Fire**. Next is the **Heart** joined with **Wind**. Then the **Sky** joined with **Wind**, followed by the **Pervasive** joined with that same **Wind**. || 49 ||

These same syllables in reverse order shall form the first quarter of the verse. The first part of the second quarter shall be the same, or the second syllable may be **Empty** <note>original: "shunya," likely referring to the anusvara or "m" sound</note>. || 50 ||

The third syllable shall be the fourth, <gloss>indeed</gloss>, and then comes the **"with water"** syllable. The reverse of these shall form the second quarter of the verse. || 51 ||

---

**The Manorama Commentary**

With the two verses beginning with "In the east" and ending with "one should encircle," the author teaches the construction of the sixty-four-square **Grace-bestowing Yantra** <term>Anugraha Yantra</term>. The meaning is as follows: Having struck nine lines from east to west and nine lines from south to north at equal intervals, one creates sixty-four squares. There, starting from the row beginning in the direction of **Shiva** <note>the Northeast</note> and ending in the **South-North** orientation, one should write the **Shrividya Mantra** in the **Anustubh** meter in the form of a *Sarvatobhadra* (as will be described). Outside of that, in the four directions starting from the East, one should encircle it four times from the **Northeast** (Isha) back to the **Northeast** with the syllables of the **Tvaritā Mantra** <note>the "Swift" goddess</note> which touch the outer lines and contain the syllable *vashaṭ* (or *phaṭ*). || 46 || 47 ||

With the seven verses beginning with "Grace" and ending with "by the gathering," the author introduces and teaches the extraction of the **Shrividya Mantra** in the form of an *Anustubh* verse arranged as a *Sarvatobhadra*, along with its greatness. In that context, "an *Anustubh* in a *Sarvatobhadra* arrangement" refers to the fact that it can be read eight times through the four rows, both in forward and reverse order. || 48 ||

"The first is **Space** joined with the **Fire of Destruction** and **Ordinary Fire**"—this means the first letter of the *Shrividya* mantra is the syllable **Śrī**. "Then the **Heart** with **Wind**"—**Sā** is the second. "The **Sky** joined with **Wind**"—**Mā** is the third. "**Pervasive** joined with that [Wind]"—with that same Wind, **Pā** is the fourth. || 49 ||

"These same"—meaning the four syllables established in the stated order. "Reverse"—by reversing the stated order. "Quarter"—a foot of the verse. The meaning is: the four syllables in the stated order, when reversed, become: **Pā-Mā-Sā-Śrī**.

# The Glory of the Revelation of Shrividya and Other Matters
### 243

<margin>In the 14th Chapter</margin>

### The third and fourth syllables follow; then Ilā is praised, (1) then Ilā |
### joined with the Wind; this third quarter is the reverse of that. || 52 ||
### The fourth, twelfth, and twentieth, and the one before it—these are reversed. |
### This is the fourth quarter in the Shrividya, O Great Goddess! || 53 ||
### This Knowledge, in the form of a "Good-on-all-sides" grid, accomplishes all goals. |
### Wherever this exists, placed upon a ritual diagram, no inauspicious thing can gather there. || 54 ||

In this way, the eight syllables of the first quarter of the **Shrividya-Anuṣṭubh** <note>a poetic meter consisting of four quarters of eight syllables each, totaling 32 syllables</note> are formed. Now, for the beginning of the second quarter:

**The second shall be**—this means the second syllable of the previously mentioned first quarter becomes the first syllable of the second quarter. The syllable **Sā** is the first syllable of the second quarter. **"Empty of the earth" is the second**—the syllable **No** <note>original: "ko-no"</note> is the second syllable. || 50 || **The third shall be the fourth**—this means the fourth syllable **Pā** of the first quarter becomes the third syllable of the second quarter. **Then "Jya" joined with the "Sky-goer"**—"Jya" refers to the letter **Ja**. "Sky" <note>original: "Abhra"</note> refers to the letter **Jha**. "Goer" <note>original: "Cara"</note> refers to the vowel **E**. Thus, **Jhe** shall be the fourth syllable. For these four syllables placed in reverse order, the quarter is formed as before. This is what is meant: for the four syllables placed in the stated order, one should read them in reverse as **jñe-no-sā** <note>the text describes a specific phonetic reversal common in Tantric cryptography</note>. That becomes the second quarter of the Anuṣṭubh meter. || 51 ||

**The third and fourth follow**—this means the third and fourth syllables of the first quarter, **Sā-yā**, become the first and second syllables of the third quarter. **Ilā is praised**—by the word **Vandya**. The "u" sound is substituted by the "i" sound due to grammatical independence. **Lī** is the third syllable. **Ilā joined with the Wind**—**Lā** is the fourth syllable. **This reversed**—the four syllables placed in the stated order are reversed to become **Lā-lī-yā-mā**, which is the third quarter. This completes the explanation of the [third] quarter. || 52 ||

**The fourth, twelfth, twentieth, and the one before it**—the fourth syllable of this Knowledge is **Pā**, the twelfth is **Jhe**, the twentieth is **Lā**, and the one before it (the nineteenth) is **Lī**. These four syllables should follow the stated order. **These are reversed**—these four characters, placed in the stated order, are read in reverse. **This**—the eight characters. **The quarter as before**—this is what is meant: the four characters placed in the stated order and those same characters read in reverse order—**ca-yo jhe lā lī-lā jñe-yā**—this eight-syllable sequence becomes the fourth quarter of that **Shrividya-Anuṣṭubh**. || 53 ||

**This is the "Good-on-all-sides" form**—this is what is meant: in the previously mentioned sixty-four squares, starting from the top, in the first, second, third, and fourth rows, one should write the four quarters in order, ending with the "teeth" <note>original: "dantāntam," a technical term for a specific part of the grid or a phonetic marker</note>...

### 244

In the four bottom rows, if one writes the first quarter of the verse in reverse order starting from the very bottom, and then observes those four bottom rows, the first quarter appears correctly whether read forward or backward. In all cases, in the four rows of the second section, the second quarter appears in the same way. Likewise, in the four rows of the third section, the third quarter is seen. And in the four rows of the fourth section, the fourth quarter is seen. This concludes the discussion of the **Shrividya** <note>the sacred Knowledge of the Goddess</note>. || 54 ||

With the seven verses starting with **"By drawing ten [lines],"** the text teaches the construction of the ritual diagram called the **Amrita-kumbha** <note>The Jar of Nectar</note> which consists of eighty-one squares, along with its application and its fruits. In that context, **"Dvāva"** refers to the letter **Tha** <note>ठ</note>. || 55 ||

The word **"Tat"** <note>That</note> connects to the command **"Listen."** The phrase **"With the earth-holder and the weapon"** results in the syllable **Jūṃ**. **"Taken by the illusion"** refers to the letter **Sa** joined with the visarga <note>the ":" sound</note>, resulting in **Saḥ**. **"Water"** refers to the letter **Va**. **"Touching the Dala"** refers to **Ṣla** <note>or Ṭa</note>. 

According to the tradition, one should write these four syllables in the four squares adjacent to the central square, moving in an outward direction. Some traditionalists say that one should write one of these four letters in each of the four rows in succession, four times each. However, this is not the view favored by my venerable Teacher. || 56 ||

**"With the Swift-Nectar syllables"** means the syllables of the **Tvaritā-Vidyā** <note>the mantra of the Goddess Tvaritā, "the Swift One"</note> when they are separated from the syllable "Sha" and joined with the "Vaṣaṭ" call. || 57 ||

**"Water joined with its own"** refers to the syllable **Vaṃ**. **"With that"** refers to the syllable **Vaṃ** alone. **"In a form linked like a garland"** implies that the visual forms of the letters are written so they are interconnected with one another. **"With lotuses above and below"** means the Jar is depicted with two lotuses, one facing upward and one facing downward. || 58 || **"Having worshiped"**—

# Chapter 14 | Description of the Jar of Nectar Diagram and its Benefits
### 245

In that place, prosperity <note>original: "Lakshmī"</note> is exceedingly abundant, and the subjects are free from disease. Elephants, horses, cattle, and all other living beings are constantly happy. || 60 ||

One should carry this diagram to protect against the afflictions caused by ghosts, spirits, and demons <note>original: "bhūta-preta-piśāca"</note>, and to ward off fear. It is used for the pacification of misfortune <note>original: "Alakshmī"</note>, for the success of subjugation rituals <note>original: "vashya"</note>, and for the attainment of all wealth. || 61 ||

Now listen, O Goddess of the Devas, to the ritual of suppression <note>original: "nigraha"</note>. By its power, enemies lose their lives in a very short time. || 62 ||

Having created a grid of eighty-one squares as before, in the central square, place the name of the target within the "Womb of Fire" <note>original: "dāha-garbhe"; likely referring to a specific seed-syllable or geometric placement associated with heat or destruction</note>. Then, in the directions and pathways in order... || 63 ||

---

<note>The following is the scholarly commentary known as the Manoramā, explaining the technical details of the verses above.</note>

**"The deity"**—this completes the thought; it means "having worshiped the deity." **"The diagram"**—this completes the thought; it means "having worshiped the ritual diagram <note>yantra</note>." **"In the previously mentioned"**—this refers to the times when the eleven zodiac signs rise, and when planets are positioned in those specific signs. || 58 ||

The meaning of what has been said is as follows: By drawing ten lines from East to West and from South to North at equal intervals, one forms eighty-one squares. In the very central square of these, one should write the name of the person within the belly of the letter **'Tha'** <note>original: "ṭhakāra"; the letter ṭha (ठ) is shaped like a circle, symbolizing the jar</note> which is topped with a dot <note>original: "bindu"</note>. 

In the four rows of squares adjacent to that center, one should write the following syllables in a clockwise order, moving from the inside toward the outside: **"Jūṃ,"** then the syllable **"Saḥ,"** then the letter **"Va,"** and finally **"Ṣaṭ."** 

Then, beginning from the Northeast <note>original: "īśādi"</note> and the Southwest <note>original: "nirṛtyādi"</note>, one should write the previously mentioned "Auspicious Verse of Sacred Knowledge" <note>original: "Śrī-vidyā-anuṣṭubh"</note> in a thunderbolt or diamond pattern <note>original: "vajra"</note> across the four middle pathways. 

On the outermost edge, surrounding everything from the Northeast back to the Northeast, one should write the "Nectar Syllables for Men" <note>original: "nṛṇāmṛta-akṣarāṇi"</note> in four rotations, just as described before. 

Holding the center of the very middle square as the axis, one should draw a circle with a compass <note>original: "bhramena"</note> using the measurement of the Nectar syllables located in the four corners. Outside of that, one should draw another circle at a distance of four finger-breadths <note>original: "caturaṅgula"</note>. 

In the upper part, the lower part, and the middle, one should erase a four-finger-wide space between the two circles. From those four resulting ends, one should slightly curve the lines and raise them upward at equal intervals for four finger-breadths so that they take the shape of the mouth of a jar <note>original: "kumbha-mukha"</note>. Across the mouth of the jar, draw two horizontal lines. 

The middle pathway of this jar should be filled with a chain-like series of the letter **"Va"** <note>original: "vakāra-mālā"</note> where the letters touch each other and face inward. At the very top, write a dot <note>bindu</note>. 

Below the jar, draw the jar as if it is resting upon the seed-vessel of a lotus <note>original: "padma-karṇikā"</note>. At the mouth of the jar, draw a lotus with its stem pointing upward and the flower-head facing downward. 

By employing this in the desired rituals according to the stated order, the mentioned fruits <note>results</note> will be achieved. || 60 || 61 ||

Regarding the "ritual of suppression" <note>nigraha</note> and the subsequent eighteen verses: these describe the suppression diagram <note>nigraha-yantra</note> consisting of eighty-one squares. There, one writes the "Code Syllables" <note>original: "kūṭākṣarāṇi"</note>, the "Auspicious-on-All-Sides" <note>original: "sarvatobhadra"</note> shape, the "Wisdom of Kali" <note>original: "Kālī-vidyā"</note>, and the "Mantra of Yama" <note>the God of Death</note> in a similar fashion.
